name: The New Humanitarian
regions: Global / Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa / Switzerland
format: Field reporting, analysis, investigations, newsletters, podcasts
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Conflict and Security / Migration / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; direct fit with humanitarian work; Sahel and crisis zone reporting
integrity_note: An independent Swiss nonprofit, formerly a UN service, funded by governments and foundations that it lists; it reports critically on the same aid sector its donors finance.
description: The New Humanitarian is an independent nonprofit newsroom based in Geneva, founded in 1995 as IRIN inside the United Nations, independent since 2015 and renamed in 2019. Use it for field reporting on crises and for critical coverage of aid policy, funding cuts and reform of the humanitarian system.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only newsroom devoted entirely to humanitarian crises and to holding the aid sector itself to account.

name: The Reporter (報導者)
owner: The Reporter Cultural Foundation (財團法人報導者文化基金會)
topics: Investigations / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Donation funded nonprofit; investigative depth in Traditional Chinese
integrity_note: Run by a foundation funded by public donations under a rule that donors neither own, interfere nor recoup; it publishes donation records and declares progressive values.
description: Taiwan's nonprofit investigative newsroom, founded in 2015 and run by The Reporter Cultural Foundation on public donations. Use it for long investigations and data journalism in Traditional Chinese on labour, migration, environment and social policy that Taiwan's commercial press rarely funds.
what_makes_it_distinct: A donation funded Taiwanese newsroom whose long investigations appear first in Traditional Chinese, with selected English translations.

name: Afrobarometer
owner: Afrobarometer (Ghanaian nonprofit company limited by guarantee)
format: Dispatches, working papers, policy papers, survey data, annual report
topics: Data and Statistics / Politics and Policy / Development
modifier_reason: African citizen survey data in English and French; an underserved geography
integrity_note: An African led nonprofit network whose funding comes mostly from foreign aid agencies and foundations, all named on its site, with methods and data published.
description: Afrobarometer is a pan African, nonpartisan survey research network headquartered in Ghana that conducts public attitude surveys on democracy, governance, the economy and society. Working with national partners, it publishes dispatches, working papers, policy papers and freely available data covering more than 40 countries.
what_makes_it_distinct: Direct evidence of what citizens in African countries think about services, climate, migration and governance, published in English and French with open data.

name: Centro de Periodismo Investigativo
topics: Investigations / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Politics and Policy / Energy
modifier_reason: Disaster accountability reporting from a climate exposed Caribbean territory
integrity_note: Nonprofit funded by foundations and individual donors, with published annual reports; it also sues the government for access to public information.
description: The Centro de Periodismo Investigativo is a Puerto Rican nonprofit founded in 2007 that combines investigative journalism, access to information litigation and journalism training. It reports in Spanish and English on government contracts, energy, water, disaster recovery, coastal development and public debt.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its investigations of hurricane deaths, recovery spending and coastal protection are a model of disaster accountability reporting in a climate exposed territory.

name: International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ)
owner: International Consortium of Investigative Journalists, Inc.
topics: Investigations / Economy and Finance / Human Rights and Justice / International Affairs
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded by foundations, individuals and some governments, all listed publicly; donors have no say over stories, though reliance on large grants remains a structural dependence.
description: The International Consortium of Investigative Journalists is a nonprofit newsroom in Washington that coordinates reporters at partner outlets worldwide on cross border investigations such as the Panama Papers. Use it for financial secrecy, corruption and accountability projects, and for the searchable Offshore Leaks Database behind them.
what_makes_it_distinct: Coordinates hundreds of reporters across countries on shared leaked datasets, then publishes the data as searchable public records.

name: Statistics Canada
format: Data tables, The Daily releases, census profiles, boundary files, reports
topics: Data and Statistics / Economy and Finance / Geography and Mapping / Labour and Work
integrity_note: A federal agency funded by Parliament, whose professional independence over methods and release timing is written into the Statistics Act.
description: Statistics Canada is the national statistical office of the Government of Canada, established in 1971 as successor to the Dominion Bureau of Statistics and responsible for the census and official economic and social data. Use The Daily for new releases and the census profiles and boundary files for mapping work in English or French.
what_makes_it_distinct: The source of Canadian census geography, boundary files and official indicators that every other Canadian outlet cites.

name: Mongabay
regions: Global / Southeast Asia / Latin America and Brazil / Sub-Saharan Africa / South Asia
topics: Climate and Environment / Science / Indigenous Affairs / Investigations
modifier_reason: Local reporters across the Global South; nonprofit
integrity_note: Nonprofit funded by foundations and individual donors, with funders and annual reports published; reporting is evidence based with a clear conservation outlook.
description: Mongabay is a nonprofit environmental news service founded by Rhett Butler in 1999, with bureaus and local reporters in Latin America, Africa, India and Southeast Asia. Read it for original reporting on forests, oceans, biodiversity and Indigenous land rights, in English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Indonesian and Hindi.
what_makes_it_distinct: A large network of local environmental reporters in tropical countries, with separate language bureaus.

name: ProPublica
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Nonprofit model with open data and free republishing
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded by foundations and a large base of individual donors, which it discloses; the Sandler Foundation was its founding funder and the base has since broadened.
description: ProPublica is a nonprofit newsroom in New York that produces long investigations into abuses of power in government, business and institutions, often with partner newsrooms. Use it for documented accountability reporting and for its public data tools, which show how evidence led investigations are built.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes its investigations with open data and lets other newsrooms republish them free of charge.

name: Investigate Europe
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Journalist cooperative with a cross border method
integrity_note: A journalist owned European cooperative funded by foundations and reader donations, with funders published; stories are researched by one team across many countries.
description: Investigate Europe is a cooperative of journalists from about a dozen European countries, registered in Berlin and funded by foundations and reader donations. Read its joint investigations into European Union policy, corporate lobbying, labour and technology, published at the same time with partner newspapers in several languages.
what_makes_it_distinct: One team researches a single story in many countries at once, then publishes it in each national language.

name: The Barents Observer
regions: Arctic and Indigenous / Russia and Central Asia
owner: The Independent Barents Observer AS (owned by its journalists)
topics: Climate and Environment / Conflict and Security / Indigenous Affairs / Energy
modifier_reason: Journalist owned Arctic newsroom; rare coverage of northern Russia and Indigenous issues
integrity_note: Fully owned by its reporting staff and funded by donations and foundation grants; it is blocked in Russia and declares support for democracy and free speech.
description: The Barents Observer is a journalist owned online newspaper in Kirkenes, Norway, covering the Euro Arctic region and northern Russia in English and Russian. Its reporters, some in exile from Russia, follow climate change, energy, shipping, security, borders and Indigenous peoples' issues.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is one of the few independent sources on Arctic Russia, with regular reporting on sea ice, shipping routes and Indigenous communities.

name: The Narwhal
regions: Canada and Quebec / Arctic and Indigenous
topics: Climate and Environment / Indigenous Affairs / Investigations / Energy
modifier_reason: Reader funded nonprofit; Canadian environment and Indigenous land reporting in depth
integrity_note: A nonprofit society funded mainly by reader members plus foundation grants, with no advertising; it reports from a declared environmental and Indigenous rights perspective.
description: The Narwhal is a nonprofit online magazine published by The Narwhal News Society, founded in Victoria, British Columbia in 2018, with reporters in British Columbia, the Prairies and Ontario. Use it for investigative reporting on Canadian land, water, energy and Indigenous rights that the national dailies cover only in passing.
what_makes_it_distinct: A reader funded Canadian newsroom devoted entirely to environment and Indigenous rights investigations, with strong photojournalism.

name: ACAPS
owner: ACAPS (independent nonprofit; legal hosting arrangement unconfirmed)
format: Crisis analysis, risk and scenario reports, datasets, severity index
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Conflict and Security / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Analysis independent of the UN system; core to humanitarian information work
integrity_note: Not affiliated with the UN and governed by its own board, but funded largely by donor governments; it publishes methods, sources and limitations.
description: ACAPS is an independent humanitarian analysis provider founded in 2009, with a team of more than 100. It monitors crises worldwide and publishes country analysis, risk and scenario reports, humanitarian access overviews and datasets such as the INFORM Severity Index.
what_makes_it_distinct: It offers crisis analysis outside the UN system with stated methods and caveats, directly usable for needs assessment and severity mapping.

name: CIPER Chile
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Nonprofit foundation model with reader members; Spanish practice
integrity_note: Owned by Fundación CIPER and financed mostly by recurring member donations, with yearly income reports that itemise each donor category and amount.
description: CIPER, the Centro de Investigación Periodística, is a nonprofit investigative newsroom in Santiago founded in 2007 by Mónica González and financed by a foundation and reader members. Read its document driven investigations into Chilean politics, business and policing as Spanish practice with strong sourcing.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Chilean nonprofit for document based investigations, with a section where academics publish research for general readers.

name: The Citizen Lab
owner: University of Toronto (Munk School of Global Affairs and Public Policy)
topics: Technology and AI / Human Rights and Justice / Investigations / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Forensic digital rights research fills a gap among technology sources
integrity_note: A university lab that states it works independently of government and corporate interests; its research focuses on abuses against civil society.
description: The Citizen Lab is an interdisciplinary research unit at the University of Toronto's Munk School, founded in 2001 by Ronald Deibert. It investigates spyware, censorship, transnational repression and influence operations, publishing forensic reports with documented methods.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its forensic evidence on surveillance of activists and journalists is primary material for understanding digital risk to civil society and humanitarian workers.

name: GroundUp
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Urban Planning / Labour and Work / Health
modifier_reason: Community level housing and labour reporting; exemplary corrections log
integrity_note: Donation funded nonprofit that names its funders and keeps a public, dated log of corrections; its reporting starts from a declared human rights position.
description: GroundUp is a South African nonprofit news agency that began in 2012 and became a stand alone nonprofit company in 2020. Its reporters cover housing, sanitation, social grants, health, public transport, labour and immigration in working class communities, free to read and republish.
what_makes_it_distinct: Reports service delivery, housing and informal settlement issues from the ground, the lived side of urban planning and basic infrastructure.

name: Ojo Público
format: Investigations, data journalism, fact checks, video reports
topics: Investigations / Climate and Environment / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Andean and Amazonian investigations with data methods and Spanish practice
integrity_note: Nonprofit newsroom funded mainly by international foundations and donors that it lists publicly; it has no commercial owner and runs its own fact checking unit.
description: OjoPúblico is a Peruvian nonprofit digital newsroom founded in 2014, known for investigative and data journalism on power, organised crime, health and the environment. It also runs a fact checking unit and a section on the Amazon and Indigenous territories.
what_makes_it_distinct: Data driven investigations into Amazon land, mining and urban green space in Peru, written in Spanish that rewards an intermediate reader.

name: VertigO
owner: Les Éditions en environnement VertigO, with Université du Québec à Montréal
format: Peer reviewed articles, thematic issues, debates, three issues a year
topics: Climate and Environment / Science / Development
modifier_reason: Francophone open access environmental research including African authors
integrity_note: A nonprofit academic journal with open access and peer review, free of commercial publisher control; it depends on university and research council support.
description: VertigO is a French language, open access, peer reviewed journal of environmental sciences founded in Montreal in 2000 and distributed through OpenEdition Journals. It publishes interdisciplinary research on environment, territory, climate adaptation and resource governance in Quebec, Europe and francophone Africa.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is a French language venue where natural and social sciences meet on environmental risk and adaptation, with many authors from francophone Africa.

name: InfoAmazonia
topics: Climate and Environment / Geography and Mapping / Indigenous Affairs / Investigations
modifier_reason: Map based journalism matching the reader's cartographic discipline; underserved Amazon geography
integrity_note: Nonprofit geojournalism outlet funded by foundation grants and partnerships; its environmental protection perspective is declared, and it publishes the data and maps behind its stories.
description: InfoAmazonia is a Brazilian nonprofit outlet founded in 2012 that combines reporting with maps, satellite data and geolocated stories on the countries of the Amazon basin. It publishes in Portuguese, Spanish and English on deforestation, climate, mining, elections and forest communities.
what_makes_it_distinct: A working model of geojournalism, with stories built on satellite data and open maps that speak directly to the reader's cartographic and community mapping practice.

name: Associated Press (AP)
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Cooperative ownership adds diversity among the wires already listed
integrity_note: A not for profit cooperative owned by its member news organisations, with no shareholder or state to answer to; it earns by licensing content to members and clients.
description: The Associated Press is a not for profit news cooperative based in New York, owned by its member news organizations, with bureaus in roughly 100 countries. Use it as a factual baseline for breaking events and for checking claims that other outlets repeat.
what_makes_it_distinct: A member owned cooperative wire whose stylebook and news values statement set working norms for much of English language journalism.

name: Global Voices
languages: Multi / EN / FR / ES / ZH-Hant / ZH-Hans / JA / RU / AR
regions: Global / Sub-Saharan Africa / Latin America and Brazil / Russia and Central Asia / Caribbean
topics: International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Underreported regions by local writers; volunteer nonprofit community
integrity_note: A Dutch registered nonprofit funded by foundations under a published fundraising ethics policy, with stories chosen by its contributor community.
description: An international community of writers and translators, incorporated as a Dutch nonprofit foundation and founded in 2004 at Harvard's Berkman Center, that reports on citizen media worldwide. Use it for stories from the Caribbean, Central Asia and Africa written by local contributors, and for parallel reading in French, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese.
what_makes_it_distinct: Volunteer translators render the same locally written stories into dozens of languages, making parallel reading possible.

name: Our World in Data
owner: Global Change Data Lab, with the University of Oxford
format: Data, interactive charts, articles, data explorers, newsletter
topics: Data and Statistics / Development / Health / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Open reusable data platform; nonprofit and academic
integrity_note: Run by the nonprofit Global Change Data Lab with Oxford researchers and funded by grants and reader donations; every chart links to its data, sources and methods.
description: An open data publication produced by the nonprofit Global Change Data Lab with researchers at the University of Oxford. Use its charts, country profiles and downloadable datasets on poverty, health, energy, emissions and work as a first stop for long run comparative evidence, then follow the cited primary sources.
what_makes_it_distinct: Every chart comes with downloadable data and documented sources, so figures can be reused directly in maps and reports.

name: amaBhungane
owner: amaBhungane Centre for Investigative Journalism NPC
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Law
modifier_reason: Nonprofit investigative newsroom in southern Africa
integrity_note: Nonprofit financed by charitable foundations and public donations under a published board funding policy that restricts corporate money to protect editorial independence.
description: The amaBhungane Centre for Investigative Journalism is a nonprofit newsroom in South Africa, funded by donors and public contributions, that investigates corruption, state capture and corporate misconduct. Use it for documented accountability reporting on southern Africa and for its advocacy work on access to information and media freedom.
what_makes_it_distinct: A donor and crowd funded investigative unit that pairs its reporting with litigation for information rights.

name: Global Labour Journal
owner: International Sociological Association Research Committee on Labour Movements (RC44), hosted by McMaster University Library Press
format: Peer reviewed articles, debate pieces, book reviews, three issues a year
topics: Labour and Work / Development / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Open access labour research with strong Global South authorship
integrity_note: Run by an academic research committee with no paywall and no commercial publisher; authors generally write from a perspective sympathetic to organised labour.
description: The Global Labour Journal is an open access, peer reviewed journal hosted by McMaster University Library Press and linked to the research committee on labour movements of the International Sociological Association. It publishes research and debate on work, employment and labour organising worldwide, in three issues a year.
what_makes_it_distinct: It carries labour scholarship from Asia, Africa and Latin America in free full text, matching the reader's interest in decent work and global political economy.

name: Uppsala Conflict Data Program (UCDP)
owner: Uppsala University, Department of Peace and Conflict Research
format: Conflict datasets, georeferenced events, conflict encyclopedia, annual reviews
topics: Conflict and Security / Data and Statistics / International Affairs / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Academic standard for conflict data; complements faster event monitors
integrity_note: A university research programme at Uppsala; its coding rules are public and conservative, which can undercount violence that is poorly reported.
description: The Uppsala Conflict Data Program at Uppsala University has recorded organised violence since the 1970s and publishes open datasets on state based conflict, non state conflict and one sided violence. Its georeferenced event data and conflict encyclopedia apply fixed definitions that are widely used in research.
what_makes_it_distinct: Strict, published definitions and georeferenced events make it the conservative counterpart to faster conflict monitors when analysing harm to civilians.

name: Cybergeo: European Journal of Geography
owner: CNRS research unit Géographie-cités; published on OpenEdition Journals
format: Peer reviewed articles, data and model papers, book reviews
topics: Geography and Mapping / Urban Planning / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: French language quantitative geography and cartography, free to read
integrity_note: An academic journal backed by French public research bodies with no author fees or commercial publisher; editorial choices rest with a scholarly board.
description: Cybergeo: European Journal of Geography is a peer reviewed open access journal founded in 1996 and hosted on OpenEdition Journals, with support from the French National Centre for Scientific Research. It publishes articles in several languages on spatial analysis, cartography, urban systems, environment and geographic theory.
what_makes_it_distinct: It carries the French school of quantitative and theoretical geography, with cartography and spatial modelling papers that are free to read.

name: IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change)
languages: EN / FR / ES / ZH-Hans / AR / RU
owner: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (established by WMO and UNEP)
format: Assessment reports, summaries for policymakers, interactive atlas, data
topics: Climate and Environment / Science / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Energy
modifier_reason: Primary intergovernmental evidence base that no news outlet replaces
integrity_note: Scientists write the assessments, but member governments fund the panel and approve each Summary for Policymakers line by line, which makes the wording cautious and negotiated.
description: The United Nations body for assessing climate science, created by the World Meteorological Organization and the UN Environment Programme and hosted in Geneva. Read the summaries for policymakers and regional chapters as primary evidence on flood risk, adaptation limits and mitigation pathways, and use the Interactive Atlas for mapped projections.
what_makes_it_distinct: Line by line government approval of its summaries makes every sentence a negotiated scientific and diplomatic baseline.

name: Dialogue Earth (formerly China Dialogue 中外对话)
languages: Multi / EN / ZH-Hans / ES / PT / ID
regions: Taiwan and Greater China / Global / Latin America and Brazil / South Asia / Southeast Asia
owner: China Dialogue Trust (operating as Dialogue Earth)
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Development / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; bilingual bridge on China's environmental footprint across the Global South
integrity_note: A London charity funded by philanthropic foundations; it keeps staff in China and aims for even handed dialogue, which makes it cautious on Chinese domestic politics.
description: Dialogue Earth is the London based nonprofit founded in 2006 by Isabel Hilton as China Dialogue and renamed in 2024, when it merged its regional sites into one platform. Use it for environmental reporting from China, Latin America and South and Southeast Asia, much of it published in Chinese and Spanish.
what_makes_it_distinct: Commissions local journalists in China and across the Global South and publishes environmental reporting in parallel languages.

name: WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF
owner: Swiss Federal Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape Research WSL (ETH Domain)
format: Avalanche bulletin, research news, data, reports
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Science / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Alpine hazard science applicable to Canadian mountain risk
integrity_note: A federally funded research institute with academic autonomy inside the ETH Domain; its output is scientific and operational, not journalistic.
description: The WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF in Davos is part of the Swiss Federal Research Institute WSL within the ETH Domain. It studies snow, avalanches, permafrost and other alpine natural hazards, issues the national avalanche bulletin and publishes research news and data.
what_makes_it_distinct: It combines hazard research with an operational warning service, showing how avalanche, rockfall and glacier science becomes public bulletins.

name: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC)
format: Annual global report, displacement database, policy analysis, country profiles
topics: Migration / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Humanitarian Affairs / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Reference disaster displacement data linking hazards and mobility
integrity_note: Part of the Norwegian Refugee Council, an operational and advocacy NGO, and funded by donor governments and foundations; its figures come with published methods and caveats.
description: The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre, established in 1998 as part of the Norwegian Refugee Council and based in Geneva, produces global data and analysis on internal displacement caused by conflict and disasters. Its annual Global Report on Internal Displacement and open database inform policy and operational decisions.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its disaster displacement figures and risk models connect hazard events to human mobility, with report summaries in French, Spanish and Arabic.

name: Agence France-Presse (AFP)
languages: FR / EN / ES / PT / DE / AR
format: Wire text, photo, video, fact checks
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: French language wire balancing the Anglophone agencies
integrity_note: A French statutory agency with no shareholders, funded mainly by client subscriptions; the French state is its largest client and sits on its board.
description: Agence France-Presse is the global news agency headquartered in Paris, operating under a 1957 French statute that guarantees its independence, with bureaus in about 150 countries. Use its French wire and its fact checking service to cross check Reuters and Associated Press, especially on Africa and the Middle East.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only one of the three global wires that works first in French.

name: Eurostat
format: Databases, Statistics Explained articles, visualizations, GISCO geodata
topics: Data and Statistics / Economy and Finance / Labour and Work / Geography and Mapping
integrity_note: A directorate general of the European Commission whose professional independence is guaranteed by European Union statistical law and a published code of practice.
description: The statistical office of the European Union, a directorate general of the European Commission based in Luxembourg that harmonizes data from national institutes. Use its database, Statistics Explained articles and GISCO geographic datasets for comparable figures on labour, migration, climate and regions, including Switzerland and other EFTA states.
what_makes_it_distinct: Harmonized statistics with matching NUTS boundary files, so European regional data can be mapped directly.

name: Programming Historian
topics: History / Technology and AI / Geography and Mapping / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Fills the digital humanities gap; volunteer run open access charity
integrity_note: Run by a small British charity with volunteer editors and funded by partner libraries, universities and individual donors; lessons go through open peer review that anyone can read.
description: Programming Historian publishes peer reviewed, open access tutorials that teach humanists digital tools and methods, from text analysis to mapping with QGIS and Python. It is run by the charity ProgHist Ltd with volunteer editors, and its English, French, Spanish and Portuguese editions make it a working reference, not a news source.
what_makes_it_distinct: Peer reviewed digital methods lessons maintained in four languages, each edition with its own editorial team.

name: Bellingcat
regions: Global / Russia and Central Asia / Europe / Middle East and North Africa
topics: Investigations / Conflict and Security / Geography and Mapping / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Geospatial verification methods fill a disciplinary gap; nonprofit foundation
integrity_note: A Dutch foundation funded about half by grants and the rest by training workshops; it publishes its funders and its methods, so findings can be checked independently.
description: Bellingcat is an investigative collective run by Stichting Bellingcat, a Dutch foundation based in Amsterdam, founded by Eliot Higgins in 2014. It uses satellite imagery, geolocation and public data to verify events in conflicts, and publishes its methods and tools, which a GIS practitioner can reuse directly.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes its geolocation and open source verification methods as reusable guides alongside each investigation.

name: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism
topics: Investigations / Health / Technology and AI / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: British nonprofit investigations; adds ownership diversity
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded by foundations and donors, with the founding Potter Foundation still a backer; it publishes funders, accounts and corrections and reports to drive change.
description: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism is a nonprofit newsroom in London, founded in 2010 and funded by foundations and donors. Use it for long investigations into global health, big technology, the environment, corporate power and British public services, often published with partner outlets.
what_makes_it_distinct: A British nonprofit that runs investigations for months and releases them through partner newsrooms.

name: The Conversation
regions: Global / Canada and Quebec / Europe / Sub-Saharan Africa / Southeast Asia
owner: The Conversation Media Group and affiliated national nonprofits
topics: Science / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Nonprofit academic network with Canadian English and French editions
integrity_note: Nonprofit network paid for mainly by member universities and foundations; every author is an academic who must disclose funding and affiliations, and articles are edited, not peer reviewed.
description: The Conversation is a nonprofit network of national editions in which academics write news analysis and explainers with professional editors, published under a Creative Commons licence. Use the Canadian editions in English and French for research based context on policy, climate and technology, and the other editions for regional expertise.
what_makes_it_distinct: Every article is written by a named academic with a funding disclosure, and can be republished freely.

name: World Inequality Database
owner: World Inequality Lab, Paris School of Economics
format: Datasets, interactive maps and graphs, working papers, reports
topics: Economy and Finance / Data and Statistics / Labour and Work / Development
modifier_reason: Open, documented global inequality data from a French academic base
integrity_note: Run by academics at the Paris School of Economics on research grants; methods and code are open, though some economists dispute its estimates.
description: The World Inequality Database is an open access collection of income and wealth distribution series for most countries, built by an international network of academic economists and maintained by the World Inequality Lab in Paris. It also publishes working papers, methodological guidelines and the World Inequality Report.
what_makes_it_distinct: Gives the reader documented, downloadable inequality series and maps that can be joined to spatial analysis of labour, exposure and climate burdens across countries.

name: Institut de la statistique du Québec
format: Statistical tables, indicators, reports, regional profiles
topics: Data and Statistics / Economy and Finance / Labour and Work / Health
modifier_reason: Data below the provincial level complements Statistics Canada
integrity_note: A statutory statistics agency of the Quebec government that publishes its methods and quality standards; it is funded by the province and answers to the finance minister.
description: The Institut de la statistique du Québec is the province's official statistics agency, established in 1999 under its own statute. It publishes data and analysis on population, economy, labour, health, culture and environment, with breakdowns by administrative region and regional county municipality.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its tables by region and regional county municipality are a ready base layer for mapping Quebec population, vulnerability and territorial change.

name: Mediapart
owner: Société éditrice de Mediapart, held through the Fonds pour une presse libre
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Reader funded with nonprofit ownership; French accountability reporting in depth
integrity_note: Funded only by subscribers, with no advertising or subsidies, and its capital is locked in a nonprofit fund; investigations are rigorous and the left editorial line is explicit.
description: Mediapart is a French digital daily founded in 2008 by Edwy Plenel and colleagues, funded only by subscribers and owned since 2019 through the nonprofit Fonds pour une presse libre. Use it for investigations into French politics, finance and policing, read alongside Le Monde for balance.
what_makes_it_distinct: A subscriber funded daily with no advertising whose capital is locked in a nonprofit fund to prevent takeover.

name: OCCRP (Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project)
regions: Global / Europe / Russia and Central Asia
format: Investigations, data projects, daily news, document database
topics: Investigations / Economy and Finance / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Nonprofit network with Central Asia and Caucasus reporting partners
integrity_note: A nonprofit network that has long relied on US government grants for a large share of its budget, alongside foundations; it states that donors have no editorial say.
description: OCCRP is a nonprofit investigative network founded in 2007 by Drew Sullivan and Paul Radu, headquartered in Amsterdam, that works with partner newsrooms across Eastern Europe, Central Asia, Africa and Latin America. Use it for cross border investigations into money laundering, kleptocracy and organized crime, and for its Aleph document database.
what_makes_it_distinct: A network of dozens of partner newsrooms that publishes joint investigations and shares a searchable archive of leaked records.

name: EM-DAT (CRED, UCLouvain)
owner: Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters (CRED), UCLouvain
format: Disaster database, statistical briefs, annual reviews, documentation
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Data and Statistics / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Reference disaster loss database whose continuity is at risk
integrity_note: A university research centre that long relied on United States aid funding; in 2026 the site appeals for donations and signatures to keep the database open.
description: EM-DAT is the international disaster database maintained since 1988 by the Centre for Research on the Epidemiology of Disasters at UCLouvain in Brussels. It records the occurrence and human and economic impacts of more than 27,000 disasters from 1900 to the present, with documented entry criteria.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the standard global source for disaster loss statistics, with country level records and documentation that support hazard and exposure analysis.

name: Words Without Borders
format: Translated fiction, poetry, essays, interviews, book reviews, teaching resources
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Many underrepresented literatures and regions in one place
integrity_note: Nonprofit supported by public arts councils, foundations and publishing industry donors, all listed; selection reflects editorial taste rather than a political line.
description: Words Without Borders is a nonprofit digital magazine founded in 2003 that publishes fiction, poetry, essays and interviews translated into English from languages around the world. It also reviews translated books and runs WWB Campus, which supplies teaching material built on its archive.
what_makes_it_distinct: Lets the reader browse contemporary writing by country and language, including literatures from regions that rarely reach the English language press.

name: Civio
format: Data investigations, official gazette explainers, open data tools
topics: Data and Statistics / Investigations / Politics and Policy / Law
modifier_reason: Open data methods and public records reporting at a rare transparency standard
integrity_note: An independent foundation financed by donors, members and project grants that publishes its accounts, ethics code and lobbying activity; it campaigns openly for transparency laws.
description: Civio is a Spanish nonprofit foundation created in 2012 that uses data journalism, public records requests and litigation to expose opacity in public administration. It explains the official gazette daily and investigates public spending, lobbying, medicine prices and algorithmic transparency.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its open data methods, published code and court cases on public algorithms are a model for evidence based work with government data.

name: The Guardian
owner: Scott Trust Limited (through Guardian Media Group)
format: Articles, longform, podcasts, newsletters, data and interactives
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Climate and Environment / Investigations
integrity_note: Owned by the Scott Trust, which exists to protect editorial independence and has no shareholders to pay; reporting is reliable and the centre left editorial line is declared.
description: A British daily founded in Manchester in 1821 and owned by the Scott Trust Limited, a structure meant to protect editorial independence and reinvest profits in journalism. Use it for open access coverage of climate, labour, migration and human rights, while keeping its centre left editorial line in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: Trust ownership and voluntary reader contributions keep a large international newsroom free to read with no paywall.

name: V-Dem Institute
format: Datasets, annual report, working papers, policy briefs, graphing tools
topics: Politics and Policy / Data and Statistics / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Open country and year indicators suited to mapping and comparison
integrity_note: A university institute funded by research foundations, research councils and government donors, listed publicly; its indicators rest on expert judgement, with methods published.
description: The V-Dem Institute at the University of Gothenburg manages the Varieties of Democracy project, which measures democracy across five principles using thousands of country experts. It publishes open datasets, an annual Democracy Report, working papers, policy briefs and online graphing tools.
what_makes_it_distinct: Open, disaggregated indicators for nearly every country and year, suitable for joining to maps and for checking claims about democratic decline.

name: El Faro
format: Investigations, chronicles, audio, documentary, English edition
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Migration
modifier_reason: Exile nonprofit newsroom covering underserved Central America
integrity_note: Published by a Costa Rican foundation and funded mainly by international philanthropy and readers; its journalists face sustained pressure from the Salvadoran government and many work from exile.
description: El Faro is a digital newspaper founded in San Salvador in 1998, now published by Fundación Periódica in Costa Rica after moving its legal base in 2023 under government pressure. Read its investigations on corruption, gangs, migration and democratic decline in Central America, in Spanish with a selection in English.
what_makes_it_distinct: An early digital native newspaper in Latin America, still reporting on El Salvador from exile.

name: Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism (ARIJ)
topics: Investigations / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Arab investigative network using geospatial and open source methods
integrity_note: Donor funded and registered as a Danish foundation since 2017; it lists every partner above one percent of budget but lets some donors stay anonymous.
description: ARIJ is an Amman based nonprofit founded in 2005 that funds, edits and publishes investigative reporting and fact checking by journalists across the Arab countries. It also trains reporters and hosts an annual forum, publishing in Arabic with English versions of major investigations.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its data investigations use satellite imagery, location data and field surveys, as in its mapping of West Bank movement barriers.

name: Le Monde
owner: Groupe Le Monde (controlled through Le Monde Libre and the Fonds pour l'indépendance de la presse)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Investigations
modifier_reason: Core French language anchor with strong Africa desk
integrity_note: Controlled through Le Monde Libre and a press independence fund created by Xavier Niel; journalist, staff and reader shareholders hold blocking rights and vote on the newsroom director.
description: Le Monde is the French daily of record, published in Paris by Groupe Le Monde, with newsroom independence protected by a bloc of journalist and staff shareholders. Read it daily in French for France, Europe and Francophone Africa, and use Le Monde in English when sharing pieces.
what_makes_it_distinct: The French language baseline for international news, with a dedicated Africa desk and a parallel English edition.

name: PTS News (公視新聞網)
owner: Public Television Service Foundation (公共電視文化事業基金會)
format: Daily news, long form reports, documentaries, data stories, video
topics: Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Traditional Chinese public media with strong environmental reporting
integrity_note: Funded by government appropriation under the Public Television Act, with a signed newsroom covenant barring board and management interference; board appointments have been politically contested.
description: PTS News is the news site of Taiwan's Public Television Service, on air since 1998 under the Public Television Act. It carries daily Taiwanese and international news with long form programmes such as Our Island on the environment, plus news in Southeast Asian languages, sign language and Indigenous programming.
what_makes_it_distinct: Traditional Chinese public service news with decades of environmental documentary work on waste, forests, energy and coasts, close to the reader's hazard and climate interests.

name: Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism (PCIJ)
format: Investigations, data sets, documents, maps, video
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Data and Statistics / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Open data investigations on flood control spending
integrity_note: An independent nonprofit supported by grants, donations and an endowment fund; no proprietor or advertiser has a stake in its findings.
description: The Philippine Center for Investigative Journalism is an independent nonprofit newsroom founded in 1989. It investigates public spending, campaign finance, political clans, human rights and the energy transition, and releases the underlying documents, data sets and maps, including its work on flood control contracts.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its flood control investigations pair contract data with maps to show how disaster mitigation money is captured, a direct case study in risk governance.

name: The Markup
topics: Technology and AI / Investigations / Data and Statistics / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Nonprofit newsroom with open methods on technology accountability
integrity_note: A nonprofit newsroom now part of CalMatters, funded by foundations and individual donors that it lists publicly; it publishes methods, data and code with its investigations.
description: The Markup is a nonprofit newsroom, part of CalMatters since 2024, that investigates how technology companies and algorithms affect people, publishing its data and methods with each story. Use it for evidence on algorithmic bias, surveillance and data privacy, and for the Blacklight privacy inspection tool.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes a full methodology, and often the code and data, behind each technology investigation.

name: APTN News
regions: Canada and Quebec / Arctic and Indigenous
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy / Investigations / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Indigenous run national newsroom in a priority geography
integrity_note: Nonprofit Indigenous broadcaster funded mainly by mandatory cable carriage fees set by the CRTC, which frees it from advertiser pressure but ties it to licence renewal.
description: APTN News is the news service of the Aboriginal Peoples Television Network, a nonprofit Indigenous broadcaster based in Winnipeg with bureaus across Canada. Follow it for daily reporting, investigations and current affairs programs on First Nations, Inuit and Métis communities, told by Indigenous journalists.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only national news service in Canada run by and for Indigenous peoples.

name: Small Axe: A Caribbean Journal of Criticism
owner: Small Axe Inc., published by Duke University Press
format: Peer reviewed essays, visual art, book discussions
topics: Literature and Books / Visual Arts / History / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Caribbean scholarship and arts criticism from an academic publisher
integrity_note: Owned by the nonprofit Small Axe Inc. and published by Duke University Press, with peer review and a declared postcolonial critical stance.
description: Small Axe is a peer reviewed journal of Caribbean criticism edited by the anthropologist David Scott and published three times a year by Duke University Press. Read it for essays on Caribbean intellectual history, literature and visual art, and see the free companion projects of the Small Axe Project at smallaxe.net.
what_makes_it_distinct: The leading forum for Caribbean intellectual criticism, linking scholarship with commissioned visual art projects.

name: Jàmbá: Journal of Disaster Risk Studies
owner: AOSIS, a South African open access publisher
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Development / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: African disaster risk scholarship, an underserved geography and discipline
integrity_note: Published by the South African open access publisher AOSIS and financed by author fees; editorial decisions rest with an academic board and peer reviewers.
description: Jàmbá: Journal of Disaster Risk Studies is a peer reviewed open access journal published since 2006 and now issued by AOSIS in South Africa. It covers disaster risk reduction and resilience across disciplines, with a declared emphasis on Africa and other developing regions.
what_makes_it_distinct: It publishes African researchers on vulnerability, early warning and community resilience, a body of work that is thin in northern journals.

name: Métropolitiques
owner: Association Métropolitiques (French nonprofit association under the 1901 law)
format: Essays, field reports, debates, dossiers, book reviews
topics: Urban Planning / Architecture / Politics and Policy / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Free French urban research essays across planning and architecture
integrity_note: Run by a board of academics and practitioners and asking readers for donations; essays are argued positions by named researchers under a published editorial charter.
description: Métropolitiques is a French online review on cities, architecture and territories, run by academics and practitioners from the urban disciplines. It publishes short essays, field reports, debates, dossiers and book reviews several times a week, and translates a selection into English.
what_makes_it_distinct: It turns current French urban research into short, readable essays that cross planning, architecture, sociology and geography.

name: Geospatial Information Authority of Japan (国土地理院)
owner: Government of Japan (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism)
format: Web maps, map tiles, geodetic data, aerial photographs, disaster mapping
topics: Geography and Mapping / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Data and Statistics / Science
modifier_reason: National mapping reference directly relevant to the reader's cartography
integrity_note: A government survey agency paid from the state budget; its maps and geodetic data are technical products issued under published standards and open terms of use.
description: The Geospatial Information Authority of Japan is the national survey and mapping agency under the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism. It publishes base maps through the GSI Maps web viewer, geodetic and crustal movement data, aerial photographs, and rapid mapping after earthquakes, floods and landslides.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its open map tiles, historical aerial photographs, landform classification layers and post disaster imagery are a working model for hazard cartography and Japanese map conventions.

name: HumAngle
topics: Conflict and Security / Humanitarian Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Humanitarian and geospatial reporting from the Sahel and Lake Chad
integrity_note: Founder led outlet that relies largely on foundation grants; its exact legal structure and current funders are not confirmed.
description: HumAngle is a Nigerian newsroom founded in 2020 by journalist Ahmad Salkida that reports on conflict, displacement, humanitarian crises and development in Nigeria, the Lake Chad basin and the Sahel. It combines field reporting from affected communities with open source and geospatial investigation.
what_makes_it_distinct: Uses satellite imagery and mapping to document insurgency, displacement and missing persons, close to the reader's own humanitarian cartography practice.

name: Japan Meteorological Agency (気象庁)
owner: Government of Japan (Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism)
format: Forecasts, warnings, earthquake and tsunami bulletins, climate data, press releases
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Climate and Environment / Science / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Reference hazard source for Japan and the western Pacific
integrity_note: A government agency under the transport ministry paid from the state budget; its observations and warnings follow published scientific methods, not political direction.
description: The Japan Meteorological Agency is the national service for weather, climate, earthquakes, tsunami and volcanoes, attached to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism. Its site carries live warnings, risk distribution maps, observation data, climate assessments and press releases in Japanese, with English pages.
what_makes_it_distinct: The primary source for typhoon, heavy rain, earthquake and tsunami information in Japan, with map based warning products worth studying as early warning design.

name: Hong Kong Free Press
owner: Hong Kong Free Press Limited (nonprofit company)
format: News, features, explainers, opinion, photography, newsletter
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Law / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Transparent reader funded model in a shrinking press environment
integrity_note: Reader funded and nonprofit with published accounts and an ethics code; it works under Hong Kong's national security laws, which limit what local outlets can safely publish.
description: Hong Kong Free Press is a nonprofit English language news outlet founded in 2015 and funded mainly by about a thousand monthly donors. It reports daily on Hong Kong politics, courts, national security cases, press freedom, society and the environment, and publishes annual and transparency reports.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the few independent newsrooms still working inside Hong Kong, with published accounts and a free image project on extreme heat and outdoor workers.

name: ABC News (Australia)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Investigations
modifier_reason: Strong hazard and Pacific coverage, though partly redundant with other public broadcasters
integrity_note: Statutory corporation funded by the Australian parliament; the ABC Act requires accuracy and impartiality, though budgets and board appointments are recurring points of political pressure.
description: ABC News is the news division of the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, the national public broadcaster established by statute. It covers Australia, Asia and the Pacific across online, radio and television, and includes investigative programmes, a verification unit and emergency broadcasting.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its emergency broadcasting role and sustained bushfire, flood and cyclone reporting make it a practical reference for hazard communication in Oceania.

name: BBC News
languages: Multi / EN / FR / ZH-Hant / ZH-Hans / JA / ES / RU / AR
format: Articles, live coverage, video, radio, podcasts
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security
integrity_note: Funded by the UK licence fee under a Royal Charter; governments set the fee and appoint the chair, which brings recurring political pressure despite formal editorial independence.
description: BBC News is the news division of the British Broadcasting Corporation, funded mainly by the UK licence fee and governed by published editorial guidelines. Use it as a factual baseline for world and British news, and for its World Service editions in French, Chinese, Japanese and Spanish.
what_makes_it_distinct: The widest correspondent network of any public broadcaster, with parallel services in more than forty languages.

name: CORRECTIV
owner: CORRECTIV Recherchen für die Gesellschaft gGmbH
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Media and Information Integrity / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Nonprofit ownership diversity; Swiss desk adds a priority geography
integrity_note: A nonprofit company financed by individual donors and foundations that publishes its finances in detail; a few large foundation grants remain important.
description: CORRECTIV is a nonprofit investigative newsroom founded in 2014 and based in Essen and Berlin, financed by donations and foundations and publishing its finances. Read it in German, with selected English translations, for cross border investigations, fact checking and its newer Swiss desk.
what_makes_it_distinct: Germany's first donor funded investigative newsroom, with citizen participation projects and a dedicated Swiss edition.

name: Follow the Money (FTM)
owner: Follow the Money (independent company funded by members)
topics: Investigations / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Member funded model; European Union money trail beat
integrity_note: Funded almost entirely by paying members and free of advertising; its declared mission is to hold financial and political power to account.
description: Follow the Money is a Dutch investigative platform founded in 2010 and funded by its members, publishing in Dutch at ftm.nl and in English at ftm.eu. Use the English edition for investigations into European Union institutions, lobbying, subsidies and corporate finance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Financial investigations paid for by members, with a Brussels desk that tracks money through European Union institutions.

name: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
format: Refereed encyclopedia entries, quarterly archived editions
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / History / Science
modifier_reason: Fills the philosophy reference gap with refereed, citable entries
integrity_note: Hosted by Stanford and funded by the university, library memberships, public humanities grants and donors; entries are refereed, mostly from within the analytic tradition.
description: The Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy is an open access reference work of about 1,800 entries, each written and kept up to date by specialists and refereed by an editorial board before publication. Fixed quarterly editions are archived so that entries can be cited reliably.
what_makes_it_distinct: A dependable free starting point for any philosophical topic the reader meets, with full bibliographies and fixed versions the reader can cite.

name: The Local
owner: The Local TO Publishing (registered journalism organisation)
format: Features, investigations, quarterly issues, election tracker
topics: Urban Planning / Health / Labour and Work / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Nonprofit urban reporting with depth on planning and health
integrity_note: A registered journalism organisation funded by foundations and donors, with a published ethics code, a corrections page and a stated firewall between funders and editors.
description: The Local is a nonprofit online magazine covering urban health and social issues in the Greater Toronto Area, spun off from UHN OpenLab in 2019. It publishes quarterly themed issues and regular features on housing, transit, climate, education, labour and health.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its long narrative features turn housing, transit and health policy into reported stories from suburbs that most Toronto media overlook.

name: High Country News
region_label: Western United States and Indigenous nations
topics: Climate and Environment / Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Indigenous affairs reporting and nonprofit ownership
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded mainly by subscribers and donors with no corporate owner; its environmental outlook shapes which stories it chooses more than how accurately it reports them.
description: High Country News is a nonprofit magazine founded in 1970 that reports on land, water, wildlife, climate and communities across the western United States. Its Indigenous Affairs desk, staffed by Indigenous journalists, makes it useful for comparing land and resource questions with those facing Indigenous nations in Canada.
what_makes_it_distinct: A dedicated Indigenous Affairs desk inside a regional environmental magazine.

name: Radio-Canada
regions: Canada and Quebec / Arctic and Indigenous
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Indigenous Affairs / Investigations
modifier_reason: Home geography in French; distinct newsroom from CBC English
integrity_note: A Crown corporation funded mainly by a parliamentary appropriation, with independence set in the Broadcasting Act, published journalistic standards and an ombudsman who rules on complaints.
description: The French language service of Canada's national public broadcaster, a Crown corporation with its French headquarters in Montreal and newsrooms across the country. Use it as the daily French baseline for Quebec and federal news, with the investigative program Enquête and the Espaces autochtones desk for Indigenous coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only French language newsroom with stations in every Canadian region, including a dedicated Indigenous desk.

name: Revista 5W
owner: Unconfirmed (founded and run by a group of journalists, directed by Agus Morales)
format: Long form chronicles, photo essays, podcasts, annual print issue, books
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Migration / Humanitarian Affairs
modifier_reason: Member funded Spanish field reportage on migration and conflict
integrity_note: Founded and run by journalists and financed chiefly by paying members rather than advertising; its legal ownership could not be confirmed.
description: Revista 5W is a Barcelona magazine of long form international reporting founded in 2015 by Spanish foreign correspondents and photographers. It publishes chronicles, photo essays, podcasts and an annual print issue on conflict, migration and daily life far from the news cycle.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its field reporting on migration routes, displacement and conflict, written in Spanish, is close to the humanitarian contexts the reader maps.

name: Disclose
topics: Investigations / Conflict and Security / Climate and Environment / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Nonprofit, donation funded investigations in French
integrity_note: A nonprofit association funded by donations with no advertising or shareholders; it publishes its financing and charter and describes itself as both newsroom and nongovernmental organisation.
description: Disclose is a French nonprofit investigative newsroom founded in 2018, funded by donations and open to all readers without a paywall. Read its document based inquiries into arms exports, surveillance, environmental harm and corporate conduct, published in French with English versions and often released with partner media.
what_makes_it_distinct: A donor funded French newsroom built like a nongovernmental organization, known for leaks on arms sales and state surveillance.

name: Le Devoir
format: Articles, analysis, opinion, newsletters, podcasts, data journalism
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Independent ownership; home geography covered in French
integrity_note: Held outside any chain through a trust structure and funded mostly by subscribers and donors; its editorial pages take a declared Quebec nationalist, social democratic line.
description: Le Devoir is the independent Montreal daily founded by Henri Bourassa in 1910, published by Le Devoir Inc. under a trust structure that shields it from chain ownership. Use it as the French language paper of record for Quebec politics, culture, ideas and education, alongside Radio-Canada and La Presse.
what_makes_it_distinct: Quebec's only independent daily of record, outside every chain and sustained by subscribers and donors for over a century.

name: Lincoln Institute of Land Policy
owner: Lincoln Institute of Land Policy, a private operating foundation
format: Magazine, policy reports, working papers, books, courses, podcast
topics: Urban Planning / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Endowed and donor independent; land economics with Latin American reach
integrity_note: Financed mainly by its own endowment, so it does not depend on donors; it promotes a disclosed view that land taxation and value capture are sound policy.
description: The Lincoln Institute of Land Policy is a private operating foundation in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with origins dating to 1946, that researches land use, land taxation and stewardship. It publishes Land Lines magazine, policy reports, working papers, books and courses, with programmes on Latin America and China.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its work on property taxation, land value capture and land based climate resilience connects urban economics to planning, with material in Spanish.

name: Projets de paysage
owner: École nationale supérieure de paysage (Versailles), with partner French landscape schools
format: Peer reviewed articles, thematic issues, reviews
topics: Landscape Architecture / Urban Planning / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Landscape architecture research in French, a disciplinary gap
integrity_note: Published by French public landscape schools on a public open access platform; academic and peer reviewed, with no commercial owner.
description: Projets de paysage is a French peer reviewed open access journal on landscape design and spatial planning, founded in 2008 and published by the École nationale supérieure de paysage with partner schools. It appears on OpenEdition Journals with thematic issues, research articles and reviews.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is one of the few scholarly journals devoted to landscape architecture research in French, linking design practice with geography and planning.

name: Eye on the Arctic
regions: Arctic and Indigenous / Canada and Quebec
topics: Climate and Environment / Indigenous Affairs / International Affairs / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Arctic and Inuit coverage is underserved elsewhere
integrity_note: Part of CBC/Radio-Canada, funded by Parliament at arm's length; Radio Canada International was cut sharply in 2021, so much content now comes from wires and partners.
description: Circumpolar news project run by Radio Canada International at CBC/Radio-Canada, combining its own reporting with stories from partner newsrooms across the Arctic states. Use it for northern communities, Inuit governance, climate, shipping and security, in English with a French counterpart, Regard sur l'Arctique.
what_makes_it_distinct: A public broadcaster's dedicated Arctic desk pooling reporting from newsrooms in several circumpolar countries.

name: Stockholm Environment Institute
format: Reports, briefs, perspectives, tools and data, podcasts
topics: Climate and Environment / Development / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Energy
modifier_reason: Adaptation research with centres in Africa, Asia and Latin America
integrity_note: Set up by the Swedish government as an independent foundation and reliant mainly on public development and research funders; governance and annual reports are published.
description: The Stockholm Environment Institute is an international nonprofit research institute founded in 1989, with headquarters in Stockholm and centres in Bangkok, Nairobi, Bogotá, Tallinn, Oxford, York and the United States. It publishes research and tools on climate, water, air, land, energy, governance and adaptation.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its research on locally led adaptation and community water resilience in Kenya, Bolivia and Southeast Asia matches the reader's work on community based adaptation.

name: Initium Media (端傳媒)
format: Long form reports, essays, newsletters, podcasts
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Investigations
modifier_reason: Independent subscriber funded Sinophone outlet in Traditional Chinese
integrity_note: Subscriber funded and run from Singapore beyond Beijing's direct reach, but it is a private company with undisclosed shareholders, and it is blocked in mainland China.
description: Initium Media is an independent Chinese language digital outlet founded in Hong Kong in 2015 and headquartered in Singapore since 2021, funded mainly by subscribers. Use it for long investigations and essays that compare Taiwan, Hong Kong, mainland China and the diaspora in Traditional Chinese, with a Simplified option.
what_makes_it_distinct: Subscriber funded long form journalism that reports across Taiwan, Hong Kong and mainland China for the whole Sinophone world.

name: International Crisis Group
format: Reports, briefings, monthly conflict tracker, podcasts
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Humanitarian Affairs
modifier_reason: Field analysis of the Sahel, Central Asia and Myanmar
integrity_note: A Brussels based organisation funded by governments, foundations and private donors that it lists; its analysis is field based and always ends in policy recommendations.
description: International Crisis Group is an independent organization based in Brussels whose analysts produce field based reports and briefings on armed conflicts and political crises worldwide. Use its CrisisWatch monthly tracker and regional reports for context on the Sahel, Central Asia, Myanmar and other places where humanitarian operations run.
what_makes_it_distinct: CrisisWatch gives a consistent monthly reading of whether each conflict is deteriorating or improving.

name: Humanitarian Data Exchange (OCHA)
owner: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), Centre for Humanitarian Data
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Data and Statistics / Geography and Mapping / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Core data infrastructure for humanitarian mapping
integrity_note: Run by a UN Secretariat office answerable to member states; data come from hundreds of contributing organisations and vary in quality, with sources stated per dataset.
description: The Humanitarian Data Exchange is an open platform run by the OCHA Centre for Humanitarian Data in The Hague, launched in 2014. It hosts datasets shared by UN agencies, NGOs, governments and researchers, including administrative boundaries, population, needs, displacement and hazard data for crisis countries.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the standard place to find common operational datasets and crisis geodata, with metadata, sources and update dates for each file.

name: Cochrane
owner: The Cochrane Collaboration (charity registered in the United Kingdom)
format: Systematic reviews, plain language summaries, news, podcasts
topics: Health / Science
modifier_reason: Reference health evidence, multilingual, but outside the reader's core fields
integrity_note: A charity that refuses commercial sponsorship of its reviews and relies on Cochrane Library licences and public research funders; a few reviews have drawn methodological disputes.
description: Cochrane is an international charity whose network of researchers and volunteers produces systematic reviews of health interventions, published in the Cochrane Library. Volunteer teams translate its plain language summaries into about 20 languages, including French, Spanish, Chinese and Japanese.
what_makes_it_distinct: Plain language summaries in French, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese let the reader check health claims and practise reading in several of the reader's languages.

name: International Court of Justice (ICJ)
format: Judgments, advisory opinions, orders, pleadings, press releases
topics: Law / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
integrity_note: A United Nations organ financed by member states; judges are elected by states but independent by statute, and dissenting opinions are published in full.
description: The International Court of Justice is the principal judicial organ of the United Nations, seated in The Hague, and its website publishes judgments, advisory opinions, orders, pleadings and press releases in English and French. Use it to read rulings in full rather than relying on summaries in the news.
what_makes_it_distinct: The full bilingual record of disputes between states and of advisory opinions, including the 2025 opinion on climate obligations.

name: Pew Research Center
format: Survey reports, short reads, datasets, newsletter
topics: Data and Statistics / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Reference survey data; United States centred, limited tie to core fields
integrity_note: A subsidiary of The Pew Charitable Trusts, its main funder; it takes no commissioned work and makes no policy recommendations.
description: Pew Research Center is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research organisation in Washington that conducts public opinion polling, demographic research and data analysis. It publishes reports and short reads on politics, religion, technology, media and global attitudes, with questionnaires and datasets released for reuse.
what_makes_it_distinct: Carefully documented surveys of public attitudes in many countries, including views on artificial intelligence, work and social media, without policy recommendations.

name: Reuters
topics: International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security
integrity_note: Owned by Thomson Reuters, which the Thomson family controls through its Woodbridge company; the Trust Principles and a founders share company formally guard editorial independence.
description: Reuters is the international news agency of Thomson Reuters, reporting from bureaus worldwide under its published Trust Principles of independence and freedom from bias. Use it as the factual baseline for breaking events, markets and diplomacy before turning to outlets that interpret them.
what_makes_it_distinct: A global wire bound by formal Trust Principles that a founders share company can enforce against its own owner.

name: Science (AAAS)
owner: American Association for the Advancement of Science
format: Peer reviewed journal, news, policy forums, podcast
topics: Science / Politics and Policy / Health / Climate and Environment
integrity_note: Published by a nonprofit scientific society, the AAAS; research is peer reviewed and the news desk reports independently, including on science funders and institutions.
description: Science is the weekly peer reviewed journal of the American Association for the Advancement of Science, paired with a staff newsroom that follows research policy and funding. Use the news section for reporting on science and government, and the journal for primary research and policy forums.
what_makes_it_distinct: Combines a flagship research journal with an independent news desk governed by its own published editorial standards.

name: Balkan Insight
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Nonprofit network covering a region the big outlets neglect
integrity_note: Published by the nonprofit BIRN network and financed mainly by Western governments, the European Union and foundations, which it lists; reporting is rights based and locally staffed.
description: Balkan Insight is the English language publication of the Balkan Investigative Reporting Network, a nonprofit network of newsrooms across Southeast Europe. Use it for investigations and daily analysis on corruption, war crimes trials, digital rights and democratic backsliding in the Balkans and Central Europe.
what_makes_it_distinct: Follows war crimes trials and transitional justice across the Balkans with local reporters in each country.

name: The Continent
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
format: Weekly digital newspaper sent by messaging app and email
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Investigations
modifier_reason: Continent wide African reporting, nonprofit, novel distribution
integrity_note: Published by a South African nonprofit set up by its own editors and funded by donors and some commercial income, with no corporate or state owner.
description: The Continent is a free weekly newspaper launched in 2020 from Johannesburg and designed to be read and shared on WhatsApp, Signal and email, with reporters across Africa. what_makes_it_distinct: The peer reviewed journal of the Francophone digital humanities community, free to read.

name: Project Multatuli

name: The Collective (集誌社)

what_makes_it_distinct: Traditional Chinese reporting from inside Hong Kong on housing, redevelopment, the Wang Fuk Court fire and workplace heat, subjects close to the reader's planning and climate interests.

integrity_note: Nonprofit published by the association Al Khatt and reliant on grants; it describes itself as an engaged counter power, which is a declared stance.

name: Le Temps

description: Le Temps is the French language daily of record for western Switzerland, founded in 1998, based in Geneva and owned since 2021 by the nonprofit Fondation Aventinus. Use it for Swiss federal politics, international Geneva and the UN system, finance, science and culture seen from Suisse romande.
what_makes_it_distinct: The French language paper of record for Switzerland, owned by a Geneva foundation and close to international Geneva.

name: Business & Human Rights Resource Centre

integrity_note: A charity that states it accepts no funding from companies and relies mainly on foundations and other grants; its purpose is corporate accountability advocacy.
description: The Business & Human Rights Resource Centre is a nonprofit that tracks the human rights conduct of thousands of companies worldwide. It collects allegations, invites companies to respond, and publishes news, lawsuit records, benchmarks and data trackers on labour rights, supply chains and energy transition minerals.
what_makes_it_distinct: Company level records of labour and human rights allegations, with responses, searchable by country and sector in several languages including Chinese and Japanese.

name: Eurofound

integrity_note: An agency financed from the European Union budget and overseen by a board of governments, employers, unions and the Commission, which shapes its research agenda.
description: Eurofound is the European Union agency for the improvement of living and working conditions, set up in 1975 and based in Dublin. what_makes_it_distinct: Comparable survey data on job quality, working time and social conditions across European countries, governed jointly by governments, employers and unions.

description: SWI swissinfo.ch is the international service of the Swiss Broadcasting Corporation, publishing in ten languages on Swiss politics, direct democracy, science, business and international Geneva. what_makes_it_distinct: Covers one small federal country in ten languages, with a dedicated desk on international Geneva.

name: Canadian Centre for Architecture (CCA)
