integrity_note: A private nonprofit founded and endowed by Phyllis Lambert, with arts council support; its editorial choices are curatorial and openly critical, not neutral.
description: The Canadian Centre for Architecture is a Montreal museum and international research institution founded in 1979 by Phyllis Lambert on the premise that architecture is a public concern. what_makes_it_distinct: It treats architecture, landscape and territory as one public question, and its exhibitions, bookshop and study centre are in the reader's own city.

name: Géoconfluences

modifier_reason: French language geography reference with a strong glossary

description: Géoconfluences is a French geography resource site published by the École normale supérieure de Lyon with the school directorate of the French Ministry of National Education. It offers thematic and regional dossiers, scientific articles written by academics, a large glossary, map commentaries and short news items for teachers and students.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its glossary and regional dossiers give precise French geographic vocabulary and current French scholarship, useful for writing and mapping in French.

name: U.S. Geological Survey Natural Hazards

It publishes real time earthquake feeds, shaking and impact estimates, hazard maps, open datasets and scientific reports for the United States and, for earthquakes, the world.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its open earthquake feeds, shaking maps and hazard models are standard inputs for exposure mapping and can be read directly into GIS software.

name: Central Weather Administration (中央氣象署)

description: The Central Weather Administration is Taiwan's national agency for weather forecasting, typhoon warnings, earthquake and tsunami monitoring and marine observation, under the Ministry of Transportation and Communications. Its site provides township forecasts, radar, satellite and rainfall products, earthquake reports and climate data in Chinese and English.
what_makes_it_distinct: Primary real time typhoon, rainfall and earthquake data for Taiwan, useful beside the Japanese agency for comparing warning products across the western Pacific.

name: Ouranos

integrity_note: A nonprofit consortium governed and largely funded by its members, chiefly Quebec ministries and Hydro-Québec, so its research agenda follows member needs under a scientific council.
description: Ouranos is a Montreal consortium on regional climatology and adaptation to climate change, created in 2001 by the Quebec government, Hydro-Québec and Environment Canada with partner universities. It produces regional climate projections, impact studies and adaptation guidance for Quebec, drawing on some 450 researchers and practitioners.
what_makes_it_distinct: It supplies the climate scenarios and adaptation guidance widely used in Quebec for flooding, coastal erosion, heat and drought, in French and English.

It investigates public spending, corruption and environmental harm, files freedom of information requests and lawsuits, and runs a whistleblowing platform.

what_makes_it_distinct: Among the oldest English language journals of African studies, combining research articles with shorter topical briefings.

what_makes_it_distinct: A Spanish language source on Argentine and regional public debate, with published methods, funding and collaborative work across Latin American newsrooms.

what_makes_it_distinct: Tests public claims against African statistics in English and French, and explains where reliable data on the continent exist or are missing.

name: BBC News Russian (BBC News Русская служба)

integrity_note: Part of the BBC World Service, funded by the licence fee and a Foreign Office grant; blocked in Russia since 2022 and produced largely from exile.

what_makes_it_distinct: Russian language reporting under BBC editorial guidelines, produced largely from exile after the 2022 block.

name: Quinto Elemento Lab

name: RNZ (Radio New Zealand)

what_makes_it_distinct: RNZ Pacific offers daily reporting on Pacific island states, cyclones and climate displacement that few other English language newsrooms sustain.

name: SIPRI

what_makes_it_distinct: Its open data on military spending and arms transfers gives a factual base for reading global political economy and security debates.

what_makes_it_distinct: Open peer review: referee reports and author replies are published alongside each paper.

what_makes_it_distinct: Newsrooms in every province and territory, including dedicated Indigenous and northern desks.

name: Digital Humanities Quarterly (DHQ)

Use it for methods and critique in text encoding, spatial humanities, data visualization and digital archives, including occasional special issues in French, Spanish and Portuguese.
what_makes_it_distinct: A fully open journal of record for digital humanities, published with no author or reader fees.

name: Inside Climate News

integrity_note: A public charity living wholly on foundation grants and individual donations, with no advertising; rigorous and nonpartisan, but it treats climate accountability as its mission.

what_makes_it_distinct: A Pulitzer Prize winning climate newsroom with a network of state level environmental reporters across the United States.

modifier_reason: Open access hazard science; fills a disciplinary gap
integrity_note: Owned by the European Geosciences Union and published open access by Copernicus with public peer review; funded by author charges, with no commercial owner steering content.
description: NHESS is the open access journal of the European Geosciences Union on natural hazards, from floods and landslides to compound and cascading events, with a public discussion stage before papers are accepted. Use it for current methods in hazard modelling, risk mapping and impact assessment.
what_makes_it_distinct: Open peer review lets readers follow the debate on each hazard paper, not only the final article.

name: Vérificateur général du Québec

modifier_reason: Independent audits of Quebec environmental and climate programmes

Its reports include financial audits, performance audits, a review of the fiscal report issued before each election and the reports of the sustainable development commissioner.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its sustainable development commissioner audits how Quebec manages environmental and climate risks, producing evidence that ministries do not publish themselves.

what_makes_it_distinct: One public broadcaster serving four national language regions, with an international service in ten languages.

name: Critique internationale

integrity_note: Edited at Sciences Po's CERI and published by its university press; peer review and academic governance protect content, though it depends on public university and research funding.

Read its thematic dossiers in French for fieldwork based studies of politics and society outside Europe, available through Cairn.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French language journal that reads international questions through comparative fieldwork instead of strategic commentary.

name: Eurozine

description: Eurozine is a nonprofit network and online magazine in Vienna that links about ninety European cultural journals, publishing their essays in English alongside the original languages. Use it to follow debates on democracy, media, culture and eastern Europe that would otherwise stay inside small national journals.
what_makes_it_distinct: A network that translates and republishes essays from dozens of small European cultural journals.

name: Frontier Myanmar

integrity_note: A privately owned magazine supported by a membership programme; it reports under military rule, where staff have been detained, which limits access and sourcing.

what_makes_it_distinct: Sustained field based reporting from a country at war, with coverage of displacement, aid access and disaster response that the reader's humanitarian work can draw on.

name: Himal Southasian

integrity_note: A nonprofit funded by grants and reader members that moved from Kathmandu to Colombo after official pressure in Nepal; it rejects national framings by design.
description: A review magazine of South Asian politics and culture founded in Kathmandu in 1987 by Kanak Mani Dixit and published from Colombo since 2018 after bureaucratic pressure in Nepal. Use it for longform reporting and essays that treat the subcontinent as one region, from Afghanistan to Myanmar, beyond national framings.
what_makes_it_distinct: Edits South Asia as a single cross border region and spells it Southasia as a matter of principle.

name: ACLED

Use it in Spanish for transnational stories on corruption, migration, extractive industries and authoritarian drift, especially in Venezuela, Nicaragua and Cuba.
what_makes_it_distinct: A hub model in which one Bogotá desk coordinates investigations by partner reporters in many Latin American countries.

name: Devpolicy Blog

what_makes_it_distinct: Evidence based posts on aid effectiveness, Pacific labour mobility and climate in Papua New Guinea and the Pacific, many of them written by Pacific authors.

Use it as the main English language window on Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan, with attention to labour migration, water and governance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Sustained local correspondent reporting from all five Central Asian republics in English, which almost no other outlet offers.

Use it as the daily French baseline for Quebec and Canadian politics, city affairs, investigations and culture, free to read and supported by advertising and donations.
what_makes_it_distinct: A major metropolitan daily converted to a nonprofit trust structure and published entirely online without a paywall.

name: News & Market (上下游新聞)

integrity_note: Supported by reader co-publishers and by sales from its own farm product market; the newsroom refuses paid placement, but the market is a commercial interest.

what_makes_it_distinct: Ground level Traditional Chinese reporting on farmland, water, food systems and rural land use change, a field that touches the reader's planning and climate adaptation interests.

integrity_note: A donor funded nonprofit that publishes financials and an editorial independence policy; it also sells data products to insurers and planners.
description: Climate Central is a nonprofit group of scientists and communicators based in Princeton, New Jersey, that researches and reports on climate change impacts. It produces sea level rise and coastal flood maps, daily attribution through the Climate Shift Index, local climate analyses and a billion dollar disasters database for the United States.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its coastal flood layers, elevation data and attribution tools are built for local use and can inform flood exposure mapping and public communication.

name: IndigiNews

modifier_reason: Indigenous led newsroom in Canada; independent ownership
integrity_note: Owned since 2025 by tâpwêwin media, an Indigenous led nonprofit, and openly committed to decolonising journalism, with some reporting funded by federal Local Journalism Initiative grants.
description: IndigiNews is an Indigenous led digital newsroom launched in 2020 by The Discourse in partnership with APTN and now owned by tâpwêwin media, a national Indigenous media nonprofit. Use it for trauma informed coverage of child welfare, land defence, language revival and culture written by Indigenous journalists.
what_makes_it_distinct: Indigenous journalists reporting for their own communities with trauma informed editorial practice.

name: International Labour Organization (ILO)
format: Reports, statistics, standards databases, news, podcasts
topics: Labour and Work / Data and Statistics / Law / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Primary source for labour and SDG 8, in French and English
integrity_note: A United Nations agency governed jointly by governments, employers and workers and funded by member states; its statistics are standard references, while reports reflect negotiated institutional positions.
description: The International Labour Organization is the United Nations specialized agency for the world of work, founded in 1919 and based in Geneva, governed jointly by governments, employers and workers. Use ILOSTAT for labour statistics, NORMLEX for conventions and ratifications, and flagship reports such as World Employment and Social Outlook for SDG 8 evidence.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only tripartite United Nations agency, and the custodian of international labour standards and SDG 8 indicators.

name: World Meteorological Organization (WMO)
languages: EN / FR / ES / AR / ZH-Hans / RU
owner: World Meteorological Organization, a United Nations specialised agency

modifier_reason: Primary reference for climate state and early warning standards
integrity_note: An intergovernmental body governed by its member states; its science is consensus based and sound, but public messaging reflects what members will accept.
description: The World Meteorological Organization is the United Nations specialised agency for weather, climate and water, with 193 Member States and Territories. It publishes the State of the Global Climate and water resources reports, greenhouse gas and ozone bulletins, El Niño updates and standards for data exchange.
what_makes_it_distinct: It helps lead the Early Warnings for All initiative and sets the standards behind national hydrometeorological services, so its reports anchor multi hazard early warning work.

name: World Resources Institute
format: Research reports, insight articles, data platforms, maps
topics: Climate and Environment / Urban Planning / Energy / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Open geospatial water, forest and city data relevant to the reader's mapping
integrity_note: Nonprofit funded by governments, foundations and corporations, which it lists with its financials; the research is sound but serves its own policy agenda.
description: World Resources Institute is a research organisation based in Washington with offices in Mexico, India, Indonesia, China, Brazil, Colombia, Europe and Africa. It publishes analysis and open data platforms on climate, cities, energy, food, forests, freshwater, the ocean and finance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its Aqueduct water risk and Global Forest Watch platforms supply open geospatial layers that can go straight into flood exposure and adaptation mapping.

name: Dabanga
owner: Unconfirmed; Dabanga media house in Amsterdam, long supported by Free Press Unlimited
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Rare daily window on Sudan and Darfur for humanitarian work

description: Dabanga is an independent Sudanese broadcaster and news site founded in 2008 to report on Darfur and now run from exile in Amsterdam. It reaches Sudan by shortwave radio, satellite television and online, covering the war, displacement, relief, human rights, health and agriculture.
what_makes_it_distinct: Daily English reporting from Darfur and other hard to reach parts of Sudan, valuable for humanitarian situational awareness and displacement mapping.

name: espazium revue (formerly Tracés)

integrity_note: Published by espazium AG, a house tied to the Swiss engineers and architects society SIA; it speaks for the profession but keeps a critical editorial voice.
description: Tracés, now published as espazium revue, is the French language Swiss monthly on architecture, engineering and urbanism, a partner of the Swiss Society of Engineers and Architects for 150 years. With the espazium platform it covers new buildings, competitions, academic research and debates on the built environment.
what_makes_it_distinct: It treats architecture, engineering, environment and urban planning as one building culture, in French, with close coverage of Swiss design competitions.

name: Verfassungsblog
format: Scholarly commentary, symposia, books, weekly editorial, podcast
topics: Law / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Open access legal scholarship on rule of law; fills a disciplinary gap
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded by academic libraries, institutional partners, donations, project grants, publication fees and some advertising, with a published transparency page and a liberal constitutionalist outlook.
description: Verfassungsblog is a Berlin nonprofit open access forum on constitutional law and politics in Germany, Europe and beyond, publishing about 800 edited articles a year in English and German. It also runs online symposia, books and a weekly editorial.
what_makes_it_distinct: It explains rule of law, rights and climate litigation questions through short pieces by legal scholars, published within days of events.

name: JSTOR

topics: History / Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Nonprofit library of primary sources and scholarship
integrity_note: Run by the nonprofit ITHAKA and financed by fees from participating libraries and publishers; it hosts scholarship and does not shape its content.
description: JSTOR is a digital library of academic journals, books, images and primary sources run by the nonprofit ITHAKA in New York. Use a free personal account for limited monthly reading or institutional access for full search across the humanities and social sciences, including art history, geography and historical maps.
what_makes_it_distinct: Deep back files of scholarly journals, often from the first issue, in one searchable archive.

name: Office of the Parliamentary Budget Officer
owner: Parliament of Canada (independent officer of Parliament)
format: Fiscal reports, costing notes, economic outlooks
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: High integrity but a narrow fiscal remit
integrity_note: An officer of Parliament whose independence has been set in statute since 2017 and who reports to Parliament, not to the government; the remit is narrow and technical.
description: The Office of the Parliamentary Budget Officer gives the Parliament of Canada independent analysis of federal finances, the estimates and the economy. It publishes fiscal sustainability reports, costings of legislation and programmes, and costings of party platform proposals during elections.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its costings give a neutral check on federal spending claims, including disaster assistance, climate measures and labour programmes.

name: Anthurium: A Caribbean Studies Journal
format: Peer reviewed articles, interviews, creative writing
topics: Literature and Books / Visual Arts / History
modifier_reason: Caribbean scholarship, open access, university published
integrity_note: An open access journal published by the University of Miami with an academic editorial board and peer review; it carries no advertising and charges no fees to readers.
description: Open access, peer reviewed journal of Caribbean literature, arts and culture founded in 2003 and published by the University of Miami. Read it for scholarly essays, interviews and creative writing on Caribbean and diaspora writers when a topic needs more depth than news coverage gives.
what_makes_it_distinct: A free scholarly journal that pairs criticism of Caribbean literature with new poetry and fiction from the region.

name: Disasters
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Humanitarian Affairs / Development
modifier_reason: Core humanitarian research journal
integrity_note: Owned by the think tank ODI Global and published by Wiley; peer review and academic editors keep content separate from ODI's government and foundation funders.
description: Disasters is a peer reviewed journal managed by the Humanitarian Policy Group at ODI Global and published by Wiley, covering disaster studies, humanitarian policy and practice. Use it for research on aid, vulnerability and response that speaks directly to humanitarian work.
what_makes_it_distinct: The longest running journal that joins disaster science with humanitarian policy and practice.

description: Asymptote is an online journal of world literature in translation founded in 2011 by Lee Yew Leong and based in Taiwan. Its quarterly issues present fiction, poetry, drama, essays and interviews translated into English, often beside the original text, with a frequently updated blog.
what_makes_it_distinct: Translations often appear with the original language text, so the reader can read Chinese, Japanese, French or Spanish pieces against the English.

name: Eos

description: The science news magazine of the American Geophysical Union, a nonprofit scientific society in Washington, covering Earth and space science for researchers and the public. Use its research spotlights and news on hydrology, natural hazards, climate, remote sensing and geohealth to track new findings relevant to flood and risk mapping.
what_makes_it_distinct: A scientific society's own newsroom summarizing new geoscience papers in plain language, with selected Spanish translations.

name: Landscape Research

description: Landscape Research is the peer reviewed journal of the Landscape Research Group, a British charity founded in 1967, published by Routledge for Taylor & Francis. Use it for scholarship that joins landscape architecture, geography, planning, heritage and environmental humanities, including work on landscape justice, perception and climate adaptation.
what_makes_it_distinct: A charity owned journal treating landscape as a shared object of design, geography and the humanities.

name: Nexo Jornal

description: Nexo Jornal is an independent digital newspaper in São Paulo founded in 2015, known for explanatory articles, charts and podcasts on Brazilian politics, economy, science and culture. Use it for context on Brazil, in Portuguese that a French and Spanish reader can follow with some effort.
what_makes_it_distinct: Brazilian journalism built around explanation and data graphics, funded by subscribers without advertising.

name: The New York Times
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Investigations / Science
modifier_reason: Prestige with a United States centred frame
integrity_note: Publicly traded but controlled by the Ochs-Sulzberger family through a trust; subscriptions dominate revenue, and news pages sit apart from a liberal editorial page.
description: American daily owned by The New York Times Company, with one of the largest newsrooms and foreign correspondent networks in the world. Use it for investigations, science, technology and culture coverage, and for its Chinese edition, while keeping in mind its United States centred frame.
what_makes_it_distinct: The largest newsroom in the directory, with a Chinese language edition readable in Traditional characters.

name: ICT (Indian Country Today)
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy / Law / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Indigenous peoples are underserved; nonprofit Indigenous run newsroom
integrity_note: Owned since 2021 by the nonprofit IndiJ Public Media after leaving the National Congress of American Indians, and funded by foundations, donors and tribal sponsors.
description: ICT, formerly Indian Country Today, is a nonprofit newsroom owned by IndiJ Public Media in Phoenix that covers Indigenous nations across the United States and beyond. Use its daily reporting and video newscast for tribal politics, law, climate and culture, with some coverage of Canada, Alaska and global Indigenous affairs.
what_makes_it_distinct: A national Indigenous newsroom in the United States that produces its own daily broadcast newscast.

Use its English edition for original reporting on Egyptian politics, economy, labour and regional conflicts that state aligned media do not publish.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the last independent newsrooms still reporting from inside Egypt despite site blocking, raids and prosecutions.

name: Natural Hazards Center
format: Research briefs, quick response reports, newsletter, workshop
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Science / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Social science of disasters; academic model
integrity_note: A University of Colorado Boulder centre funded mainly by the US National Science Foundation and federal agencies; academically independent but exposed to shifts in federal research funding.
description: The Natural Hazards Center at the University of Colorado Boulder connects disaster researchers and practitioners through its Research Counts briefs, Quick Response reports from recent disasters and the Natural Hazards Observer. Use it to read social science findings on warning, evacuation, recovery and equity in plain language.
what_makes_it_distinct: Turns fresh fieldwork from recent disasters into short, practitioner ready findings within months.

name: Oxpeckers Investigative Environmental Journalism
topics: Investigations / Climate and Environment / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; map driven investigative method relevant to cartographic practice
integrity_note: A small South African nonprofit funded by project grants; it shares data and source documents, and reports from a stated environmental justice position.
description: Oxpeckers is a nonprofit environmental investigations unit based in South Africa and founded by the journalist Fiona Macleod, pairing field reporting with data analysis and interactive geographic tools. Use it for wildlife trafficking, mining licences, water and climate finance stories, and as a working example of map driven accountability journalism.
what_makes_it_distinct: Africa's first environmental investigations unit, built on geojournalism tools such as MineAlert and WildEye that map licences and prosecutions.

name: Sahel Research Group

modifier_reason: Underserved Sahel geography; academic source with French content

description: The Sahel Research Group is an interdisciplinary team at the University of Florida's Center for African Studies that studies politics, religion and society in six Sahelian countries from Senegal to Chad. Use its working papers, election briefs and bilingual resources for background that news coverage of coups and insurgency rarely supplies.
what_makes_it_distinct: A university group producing English and French scholarship devoted solely to the six Francophone Sahel states.

name: Made in China Journal

topics: Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice / Economy and Finance / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Fills the labour and China gap; open access academic
integrity_note: Open access journal published by ANU Press and edited by academics; it takes a critical, labour centred view of the Chinese state and of capital.
description: Made in China Journal is an open access publication from ANU Press, edited by Ivan Franceschini and Nicholas Loubere, on labour, civil society and rights in China and in Chinese projects abroad. Read its themed issues for scholarly essays written to be understood outside academia.
what_makes_it_distinct: Free scholarly writing on Chinese labour and political economy, written for readers outside the academy.

name: PassBlue
topics: International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Independent scrutiny of the UN system; nonprofit and women led
integrity_note: A small nonprofit that publishes its donor list, with Carnegie philanthropy as its main long standing supporter.
description: An independent nonprofit newsroom in New York, founded in 2011 by former New York Times correspondent Barbara Crossette and editor Dulcie Leimbach, that reports on the United Nations. Use it for Security Council dynamics, leadership contests, peacekeeping, budgets and women's rights at the UN, covered from inside the building.
what_makes_it_distinct: A women led newsroom reporting daily UN politics independently of the organization's own communications.

name: BBC News 中文 (BBC Chinese)
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Language service of BBC already listed; Traditional Chinese adds value
integrity_note: Part of the BBC World Service, funded by the licence fee and a Foreign Office grant under the BBC's royal charter and editorial guidelines.
description: The Chinese language service of the BBC World Service, published in Traditional and Simplified script and blocked in mainland China. Use the Traditional edition for original features on Taiwan, Hong Kong and China written under BBC editorial guidelines, and for world news explained in Chinese.
what_makes_it_distinct: BBC editorial standards applied to original Chinese language reporting, with a full Traditional script edition.

name: Courrier international
owner: Groupe Le Monde (majority held indirectly by the Fonds pour l'indépendance de la presse since April 2024)
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Media and Information Integrity
integrity_note: Owned by Groupe Le Monde, now majority held through an endowment fund with a journalists' independence pole; it selects and translates foreign press, labelling each source.
description: Courrier international is a French weekly owned by Groupe Le Monde that selects and translates articles from newspapers and magazines around the world. Use it to compare how the press in different countries frames the same events, reading in French sources first written in Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Arabic or Spanish.
what_makes_it_distinct: Translates the press of many countries into French and identifies each source and its leaning.

name: Retraction Watch
format: News posts, investigations, retraction database, newsletter
topics: Science / Investigations / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Dedicated watchdog of the scholarly record with an open retraction database
integrity_note: Run by the nonprofit Center for Scientific Integrity, funded by foundation grants, donations and a Crossref agreement, and independent of journal publishers.
description: Retraction Watch is a blog founded in 2010 by journalists Ivan Oransky and Adam Marcus that reports on retractions, corrections and research misconduct. Its parent nonprofit, the Center for Scientific Integrity, also built the Retraction Watch Database, now openly available through Crossref.
what_makes_it_distinct: A check on the scholarly record itself, showing which papers, journals and authors have been corrected or withdrawn and why.

name: Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism
format: Research reports, annual survey, fellowship papers, news features
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Technology and AI / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Reference data on news use; outside the reader's core disciplines
integrity_note: Core funding comes from the Thomson Reuters Foundation, which also sits in its governance, alongside grants from foundations and industry partners including technology platforms.
description: The Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism is a research centre at the University of Oxford that studies news media worldwide. It publishes the annual Digital News Report, research reports, journalist fellowship papers and news features on audiences, trust, business models and artificial intelligence.
what_makes_it_distinct: The Digital News Report offers comparable survey data on news use and trust across dozens of countries, with methods and funders disclosed.

name: Technology and Culture
owner: Society for the History of Technology, published by Johns Hopkins University Press
format: Peer reviewed articles, book and exhibit reviews
topics: History / Technology and AI / Science
modifier_reason: History of technology depth from a scholarly society
integrity_note: Owned by the Society for the History of Technology and published by Johns Hopkins University Press; peer reviewed scholarship with no commercial or political owner.
description: Technology and Culture is the quarterly peer reviewed journal of the Society for the History of Technology, published since 1959 and now by Johns Hopkins University Press. Use it for historical context on infrastructures, tools, maps and machines when current debates about technology need a longer view.
what_makes_it_distinct: The flagship journal of the history of technology, reviewing museum exhibitions as well as books.

name: Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ)
owner: Committee to Protect Journalists (United States nonprofit)
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Human Rights and Justice / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Overlaps with RSF; stronger case methodology and no government funding
integrity_note: Funded by individuals, foundations and media companies and accepts no government money; it is an advocacy body, so case selection reflects its mandate.
description: The Committee to Protect Journalists is a New York nonprofit founded in 1981 that documents attacks on the press worldwide. It publishes alerts, special reports and databases of journalists killed, imprisoned or missing since 1992, each case confirmed through at least two sources.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its case level databases, with a published methodology, allow press freedom conditions to be compared and mapped by country and year.

name: Aboriginal Policy Studies

format: Peer reviewed articles, commentary, book reviews
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Indigenous policy research, open access; no issue found since 2023

description: Open access, peer reviewed journal from the Faculty of Native Studies at the University of Alberta, focused on policy affecting Métis, non status and urban Indigenous peoples in Canada. Use it for research articles and commentary; the latest issue found is dated 2023, so treat it as slow or dormant.
what_makes_it_distinct: The one journal dedicated to policy for Métis, non status and urban Indigenous populations in Canada.

name: Caribbean Quarterly
owner: University of the West Indies (published with Taylor & Francis)
format: Peer reviewed articles, reviews, special issues
topics: History / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Caribbean scholarship edited from the region itself
integrity_note: Owned and edited at the University of the West Indies with peer review; published commercially by Taylor & Francis, so most articles sit behind a paywall.
description: Journal of Caribbean culture founded in 1949 at the University of the West Indies and now published with Taylor & Francis. Use it for peer reviewed scholarship on Caribbean history, literature, arts and society written largely from within the region, including Barbados and the wider anglophone Caribbean.
what_makes_it_distinct: The University of the West Indies' flagship cultural journal, publishing continuously since 1949.

name: Journal of the American Planning Association
topics: Urban Planning / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Planning research; paywalled
integrity_note: Owned by the American Planning Association and published by Taylor and Francis; academic editors and peer review govern content, though the association also advocates for the planning profession.
description: JAPA is the peer reviewed journal of the American Planning Association, publishing research on land use, housing, transportation, hazard mitigation and planning practice for both scholars and practitioners. Use it for evidence on what planning interventions actually achieve.
what_makes_it_distinct: Research written to be usable by practising planners, with a practice implications section in each article.

name: Le Monde Afrique
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Development
integrity_note: The Africa desk of Le Monde, sharing its owners and editorial charter; it covers the continent from a Paris newsroom with correspondents and contributors in African countries.
description: Le Monde Afrique is the Africa desk of the Paris daily Le Monde, published by Groupe Le Monde with correspondents and contributors across the continent. Use it for French language reporting on North and West Africa held to the parent paper's editorial standards, alongside independent African outlets.
what_makes_it_distinct: A paper of record's dedicated Africa desk writing in French for both African and European readers.

name: OC Media
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Underserved geography covered across conflict lines
integrity_note: Funded by institutional donors and a growing reader membership; it declares values of social justice and peace alongside political independence.
description: OC Media (Open Caucasus Media) is a Tbilisi based newsroom founded in 2017 that covers Armenia, Azerbaijan, Georgia and the Russian North Caucasus in English. It publishes daily news, analysis, investigations and podcasts with staff drawn from across the region.
what_makes_it_distinct: Reports across conflict lines, including the North Caucasus republics and the unrecognised territories that most international outlets leave uncovered.

name: Voxeurop

format: Translated press articles, analysis, data journalism, cartoons, newsletter
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Migration / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Multilingual cooperative translating the European press; rare plural structure
integrity_note: A cooperative of journalists, translators and readers that depends substantially on European Union and foundation project grants alongside member subscriptions; the outlook is openly pro European.
description: Voxeurop is a multilingual European news site that selects and translates articles from the press across Europe and publishes its own analysis, data journalism and cartoons. It was created in 2014 by former Presseurop staff and operates as a European cooperative society.
what_makes_it_distinct: It lets the reader read the same European story as told by newspapers in many countries, in English, French or Spanish.

name: Agence Science-Presse
format: Science news, fact checks, podcast, newsletter
topics: Science / Health / Media and Information Integrity / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Only French language science news agency; adds fact checking in French
integrity_note: A nonprofit agency funded partly by the Quebec government, with federal project grants and earned revenue; it publishes financial statements and a corrections policy.
description: Agence Science-Presse is a nonprofit science news agency founded in Montreal in 1978 that supplies Quebec media with science reporting. Its Détecteur de rumeurs section checks viral claims on health, climate and technology and is recognised by the International Fact-Checking Network.
what_makes_it_distinct: It offers checked science news in French on health, climate and artificial intelligence, backed by published financial statements and a corrections policy.

name: Antipode
owner: Antipode Foundation, a charity registered in the United Kingdom; journal published by Wiley
format: Peer reviewed papers, interventions, book reviews, lectures
topics: Geography and Mapping / Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Critical geography theory relevant to critical cartography
integrity_note: Owned by a British charity and published by Wiley; peer reviewed, but openly committed to radical left scholarship, so it does not aim at neutrality.
description: Antipode: A Radical Journal of Geography is a peer reviewed journal founded in 1969, owned by the Antipode Foundation and published by Wiley in six issues a year. Its companion site carries interventions, book reviews, lectures, video abstracts and foundation news.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is a central venue for Marxist, feminist and decolonial geography, which informs critical cartography and debates about space, labour and power.

name: Imago Mundi: The International Journal for the History of Cartography
owner: Imago Mundi Ltd (published by Routledge, Taylor & Francis)
topics: Geography and Mapping / History
modifier_reason: Fills the cartography history gap; academic ownership
integrity_note: Owned by Imago Mundi Ltd, a company run by scholars in the field, and produced under contract by the commercial publisher Routledge.
description: Imago Mundi is the peer reviewed international journal for the history of cartography, founded in 1935 by Leo Bagrow and published twice a year by Routledge for Imago Mundi Ltd. Use it for scholarship on early maps, mapmakers and map collections, plus its bibliography and conference reports.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only long running scholarly journal devoted entirely to the history of maps and mapmaking.

name: Malaysiakini
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Law
modifier_reason: Subscriber supported independent in a priority Southeast Asian country
integrity_note: Owned by its founders and staff with a minority investor, the Media Development Investment Fund; it is subscription led and has faced repeated state pressure.
description: Malaysiakini is an independent Malaysian news site founded in 1999 by Steven Gan and Premesh Chandran and published by Mkini Dotcom in English, Malay, Chinese and Tamil. Use it for daily reporting and commentary on Malaysian politics, courts and civil society from outside the party linked press.
what_makes_it_distinct: Malaysia's first online only newsroom, sustained by subscriptions and publishing in four languages.

name: Nawaat
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Investigations
modifier_reason: North African independent with original French content; underserved geography
integrity_note: A Tunisian nonprofit that lists each grant and its amount, mostly from Western media and democracy donors, and works under pressure from the Tunisian authorities.
description: Nawaat is an independent Tunisian media platform founded in 2004 as a collective blog by Sami Ben Gharbia and Riadh Guerfali, publishing in Arabic, French and English. Use it for investigations, opinion and documentary video on Tunisian politics, rights, economy and environment after the 2011 revolution.
what_makes_it_distinct: Began as a dissident collective blog under Ben Ali, censored in Tunisia until 2011, and grew into a full newsroom.

name: ACME: An International Journal for Critical Geographies
format: Peer reviewed articles, themed issues, interventions
topics: Geography and Mapping / Philosophy and Ideas / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Collective owned, multilingual open access journal with Canadian roots
integrity_note: Run by an academic collective with no commercial publisher or author fees; it is explicitly committed to radical and critical scholarship.
description: ACME: An International Journal for Critical Geographies is a peer reviewed open access journal founded in 2002 and run by an editorial collective with Canadian roots. It publishes critical and radical work on space, power and social justice in English, French, Spanish and other languages, without author fees.
what_makes_it_distinct: It offers critical geography that is free to read and written in several of the reader's languages, outside the commercial journal system.

name: Alternatives Économiques
owner: SCOP Alternatives Économiques (cooperative of employees and readers)
format: Daily analysis, monthly magazine, data graphics, newsletters
topics: Economy and Finance / Labour and Work / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Cooperative ownership and French labour economics fill a gap
integrity_note: A cooperative owned by its staff with reader participation and no billionaire shareholder; its declared aim is to challenge mainstream economic thinking from the left.
description: Alternatives Économiques is a French economics magazine founded in 1980 by Denis Clerc, publishing a monthly print edition and daily online analysis of the economy, work, social policy and ecology. It is a cooperative that says it belongs to its employees and readers.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its plain language coverage of labour, inequality and ecological transition offers a heterodox French counterpoint to the market liberal business press.

name: Animal Político
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Independent Mexican newsroom; Spanish reading practice
integrity_note: Independent commercial newsroom financed by advertising, grants and reader support, with a record of disclosing its income sources; it has no party or conglomerate owner.
description: Mexican digital news outlet published by Grupo Editorial Criterio, known for investigations into corruption and for its fact checking unit El Sabueso. Read it for Mexican politics, rights and public spending in clear Spanish that suits a reader at intermediate level.
what_makes_it_distinct: Mexico's digital newsroom behind El Sabueso, a fact checking unit listed under the IFCN code of principles.

name: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace
regions: Global / Russia and Central Asia / Middle East and North Africa / Taiwan and Greater China
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI
integrity_note: An endowed nonprofit that also takes grants from foundations, governments and companies; it publishes donors yearly and its outlook is liberal internationalist.
description: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a Washington think tank founded in 1910, with research centres covering Europe, the Middle East, India, China and Russia and Eurasia. Use its papers, commentary and Carnegie Politika for policy analysis on Russia, Central Asia, technology governance and democracy.
what_makes_it_distinct: A think tank whose Russia Eurasia team relocated to Berlin and keeps publishing analysis by Russian scholars in exile.

name: Financial Times
region_label: Global, strongest on Europe and Asia
topics: Economy and Finance / International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI
integrity_note: Owned by the Japanese media group Nikkei since 2015, with a record of editorial autonomy; reader subscriptions dominate revenue and its outlook is market liberal.
description: The Financial Times is a London daily owned by Nikkei that covers global business, finance, economic policy and geopolitics through a large correspondent network. Use it for rigorous reporting on trade, central banks, industrial policy and the economics of technology and climate.
what_makes_it_distinct: A business daily whose foreign bureaus make economic policy legible across Europe and Asia.

name: Institute for Security Studies (ISS Africa)
format: Daily ISS Today analysis, reports, policy briefs, events, podcasts
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Development
modifier_reason: African authored analysis of an underserved region, in English and French
integrity_note: African run nonprofit that depends mostly on foreign government donors and foundations, so its agenda is partly shaped by external development funding.
description: The Institute for Security Studies is an African policy research organisation founded in 1991, with its head office in Pretoria and regional offices in Nairobi, Addis Ababa and Dakar. It publishes daily ISS Today analysis, reports and briefs on conflict, governance, crime, migration and development.
what_makes_it_distinct: Analysis written from within the continent, in English and French, on conflict, displacement and governance in countries where the Red Cross movement works.

name: Meduza
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Exile newsroom funded by readers; Russia from outside state control
integrity_note: A Latvian registered exile outlet funded by reader donations from outside Russia, where it is banned as an undesirable organisation; its anti war stance is declared.
description: Independent Russian language news outlet founded in 2014 and run from Riga, Latvia, with a full English edition. Banned in Russia and funded by readers abroad, it is the reader's route into Russian politics, war reporting and society through translation instead of state media.
what_makes_it_distinct: Russian reporting produced in exile and translated into English by the same newsroom.

name: The Walrus
topics: Politics and Policy / Literature and Books / Indigenous Affairs / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Charity ownership and long features on Canada
integrity_note: Published by a registered charity funded by donors, corporate sponsors, advertising and grants; sponsored events and partner content sit beside fact checked editorial work.
description: The Walrus is a Canadian general interest magazine founded in 2003 and published by The Walrus Foundation, a registered charity in Toronto. Read it for fact checked long features, essays, fiction and poetry on Canadian politics, Indigenous issues, environment, technology and culture, in print and free online.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Canadian magazine run by a charity, with a dedicated fact checking department and a public events series.

name: Town Planning Review
topics: Urban Planning / Politics and Policy / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Adds planning scholarship; subscription access limits everyday use
integrity_note: Published by a university press with an academic editorial board; most content sits behind a subscription, with some open access articles.
description: Town Planning Review is a peer reviewed journal of urban and regional planning founded in 1910 at the University of Liverpool and published by Liverpool University Press. It carries research articles, policy commentary and book reviews on planning theory, practice and history across many countries.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the oldest planning journals, useful for tracing how ideas on housing, resilience and regional development are argued and tested over time.

name: Afrique XXI
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / History
modifier_reason: Francophone Africa and Sahel depth from a reader funded association
integrity_note: Run by a French association and funded by reader donations, with a published ethics charter; it writes from a declared position critical of French policy in Africa.
description: Afrique XXI is an independent online journal on Africa launched in 2021 as the sister publication of Orient XXI, run by an association and funded by reader donations with free access. Read it in French for researched long reads on the Sahel, West and Central Africa that question French policy narratives.
what_makes_it_distinct: A donation funded French journal pairing journalists and researchers for long reads on the Sahel and Françafrique.

name: Caribbean Investigative Journalism Network
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Underserved Caribbean geography plus nonprofit ownership
integrity_note: A project of the Media Institute of the Caribbean supported by individual donors, regional foundations and international agencies, with small resources and irregular output.
description: The Caribbean Investigative Journalism Network is a nonprofit project of the Media Institute of the Caribbean that funds, trains and publishes journalists across the islands. Use it for collaborative investigations into corruption, climate vulnerability, public health and finance in Caribbean states that rarely receive sustained international coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only regional network producing investigations across islands by Caribbean journalists for Caribbean audiences.

name: Copernicus Emergency Management Service
format: Rapid mapping activations, flood and fire early warning systems
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Geography and Mapping / Climate and Environment / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Primary geospatial evidence for humanitarian mapping
integrity_note: A European Union service run by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre and paid from the EU budget; a technical mapping and forecast provider, not an editorial voice.
description: The Copernicus Emergency Management Service provides satellite based rapid mapping after disasters and runs early warning systems for floods, droughts and wildfires, including GloFAS and EFAS. Use its activation pages and map products as primary geospatial evidence during and after a crisis.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes the actual satellite damage and flood extent maps that responders use, often within days of an event.

name: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team (HOT)
format: News, case studies, tools, project updates
topics: Geography and Mapping / Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Direct fit with community mapping practice
integrity_note: A US registered nonprofit funded mostly by large philanthropic and institutional grants; its site reports on its own programmes, so read it as organisational communication, not independent journalism.
description: HOT is a nonprofit that coordinates open mapping in OpenStreetMap for disaster response, preparedness and development, maintaining the Tasking Manager and running regional hubs in Africa, Asia and Latin America. Use its updates to follow community mapping practice, data quality debates and new open tools.
what_makes_it_distinct: The organizing centre of volunteer and community mapping for humanitarian response.

name: Le Monde diplomatique
owner: Le Monde diplomatique SA (Groupe Le Monde 51 percent, reader and staff associations 49 percent)
topics: International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Cartographic essays and reader and staff shareholding add distinct perspective
integrity_note: Majority owned by Groupe Le Monde, with reader and staff associations holding a blocking minority; funded mostly by its readers, it argues an explicit left critique of neoliberalism.
description: A Paris monthly of long form reporting and analysis on geopolitics and political economy, majority owned by Groupe Le Monde with reader and staff associations holding a blocking minority. Read it in French for Global South perspectives and for its cartography, weighing its consistent left critique against other sources.
what_makes_it_distinct: Pairs long essays with an in house cartographic tradition and dozens of foreign language editions.

name: World Weather Attribution
owner: World Weather Attribution (academic collaboration led from Imperial College London)
topics: Climate and Environment / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Science
modifier_reason: Unique hazard attribution role
integrity_note: An academic collaboration led from Imperial College London and supported by philanthropic grants; rapid studies appear before journal peer review, using methods that are published and peer reviewed.
description: World Weather Attribution is an academic collaboration that publishes rapid studies on how climate change altered the likelihood and intensity of specific heatwaves, floods, droughts and storms, with published methods and vulnerability analysis. Use it to ground claims about a single extreme event in evidence.
what_makes_it_distinct: Rapid, event by event attribution that pairs climate modelling with an analysis of who was exposed and why.

name: weeklyOSM
languages: EN / FR / ES / JA / ZH-Hans / DE
owner: Unconfirmed (volunteer editorial team; code and archive hosted on the FOSSGIS GitLab)
topics: Geography and Mapping / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Multilingual open mapping digest with no comparable alternative
integrity_note: Written and translated by unpaid volunteers with no commercial owner; it curates links from the OpenStreetMap community and does little original reporting.
description: weeklyOSM is a volunteer edited weekly digest of news from the OpenStreetMap community, covering mapping campaigns, software, humanitarian mapping, events and research. Each issue is translated by volunteers into several languages, and the archive and source code are openly available.
what_makes_it_distinct: It lets the reader follow open mapping tools and community debates each week, and read the same issue in French, Japanese, Chinese or Spanish.

name: CommonWealth Magazine (天下雜誌)
format: Biweekly magazine, features, data journalism, podcasts, English edition
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Independent Taiwanese publisher; depth in Traditional Chinese
integrity_note: Independent Taiwanese magazine group with no conglomerate or party owner; it publishes editorial independence and reporting principles and relies on advertising and subscriptions.
description: CommonWealth Magazine is a long established Taiwanese business and current affairs biweekly, founded in 1981 by Diane Ying (殷允芃) and published by the independent CommonWealth Magazine Group in Taipei. Use it in Traditional Chinese for long reporting on industry, semiconductors, education, local government and social change, with selected stories in English.
what_makes_it_distinct: Four decades of independent Taiwanese economic and social reporting, with annual surveys of cities, companies and public opinion.

name: Policy Options / Options politiques
owner: Institute for Research on Public Policy (IRPP)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Indigenous Affairs / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Montreal think tank magazine with original French content
integrity_note: Published by the IRPP, a think tank financed largely by its own endowment; it is a commentary forum, so authors are often officials or stakeholders arguing their case.
description: Policy Options is the bilingual digital magazine of the Institute for Research on Public Policy, a Montreal think tank, publishing commentary by researchers and practitioners on Canadian public policy. Use it to follow federal and provincial debates on climate adaptation, labour, housing, technology and Indigenous governance.
what_makes_it_distinct: A bilingual forum where Canadian researchers and officials argue policy in plain language for general readers.

name: Reporterre
owner: La Pile (Association pour une presse libre et écologique)
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Reader funded nonprofit; ecology reporting in French
integrity_note: Published by a nonprofit association and funded almost entirely by reader donations, with no advertising or shareholders; its reporting is openly committed to the ecologist cause.
description: French daily news site on ecology founded by Hervé Kempf and published by the nonprofit association La Pile, free to read and funded almost entirely by reader donations. Use it for field reporting on climate, agriculture, energy, land struggles and environmental policy in France.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French ecology daily with no paywall, no advertising and no shareholders.

name: Rest of World
regions: Global / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Sub-Saharan Africa / Latin America and Brazil / Taiwan and Greater China
owner: Rest of World (founded and funded by Sophie Schmidt)
topics: Technology and AI / Labour and Work / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; technology and labour reporting from priority Global South regions
integrity_note: Funded mainly by its founder Sophie Schmidt, daughter of former Google chief Eric Schmidt; reporting is solid, but a technology fortune pays for technology coverage.
description: Rest of World is a nonprofit newsroom based in New York, founded in 2020 by Sophie Schmidt, with reporters and editors across Asia, Africa, Latin America and the Middle East. Use it for original reporting on how platforms, AI, gig work and electric vehicles reshape life and labour outside Western markets.
what_makes_it_distinct: The only newsroom reporting technology entirely from outside North America and Western Europe, using locally based correspondents.

name: National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction (國家災害防救科技中心)
owner: Administrative corporation supervised by the National Science and Technology Council, Taiwan
format: Research reports, hazard information maps, newsletter, disaster surveys
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Climate and Environment / Science / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Applied disaster science in Traditional Chinese, rare in the directory
integrity_note: A state funded research centre that supports the government's own emergency operations, so its science is sound but it seldom criticises official disaster policy.
description: The National Science and Technology Center for Disaster Reduction is Taiwan's public research centre for disaster science, supervised by the National Science and Technology Council. It studies typhoon, flood, earthquake and climate risk, supplies integrated hazard information to government emergency operations, and publishes a regular newsletter, household survey reports and risk maps.
what_makes_it_distinct: A close institutional counterpart to the reader's own work: applied hazard mapping, household disaster surveys and climate risk adaptation methods, in Traditional Chinese with some English.

name: The Marshall Project
format: Investigations, data projects, newsletters, first person essays
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Investigations / Law / Migration
modifier_reason: High integrity, but the subject sits outside the reader's main fields
integrity_note: Donor funded nonprofit that lists its supporters; reporting is rigorous but begins from the stated view that the justice system needs scrutiny and reform.
description: The Marshall Project is a nonprofit newsroom founded in 2014 that covers the criminal justice system and immigration enforcement in the United States. It publishes investigations, data reporting and first person accounts, and runs local newsrooms in Cleveland, Jackson and St. Louis.
what_makes_it_distinct: A model of data driven accountability reporting on a single system, with published data and methods worth studying as craft.

name: KFF Health News
format: Reporting, investigations, podcasts, newsletters, free republication
topics: Health / Politics and Policy / Investigations
modifier_reason: Rigorous and open, though health policy is peripheral for the reader
integrity_note: Editorially independent programme of KFF, an endowed health policy nonprofit unconnected to Kaiser Permanente; donors supply about a third of KFF funding.
description: KFF Health News is a national newsroom covering health care and health policy in the United States, operated as a core programme of the nonprofit KFF. Its reporting, investigations and podcasts are free to read and republish, and selected stories appear in Spanish.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its data investigations sometimes cross into the reader's field, as in its mapping of nursing homes that face severe flood risk.

name: The Ferret
owner: The Ferret Media Ltd (member owned cooperative)
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Member owned cooperative; Scotland is thinly covered elsewhere
integrity_note: A cooperative owned and largely funded by its reader and journalist members, with published funding and transparency pages; members help choose what is investigated.
description: The Ferret is an investigative journalism cooperative in Scotland, launched in 2015 and owned by its members. It reports on corruption, environmental harm, political influence and human rights, runs a fact checking service and has opened a community newsroom.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is a working example of member owned accountability journalism, with regular environmental and marine protection reporting on Scotland.

name: Taiwan FactCheck Center (台灣事實查核中心)
format: Verification reports, media literacy material, annual reports
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / Health / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Traditional Chinese verification from Taiwan; a scarce perspective on cross strait rumours
integrity_note: Run by an independent foundation that publishes annual reports and states it takes no money from government, parties or politicians; donors have included technology platforms.
description: The Taiwan FactCheck Center is a nonprofit fact checking organisation founded in 2018 and run by the Taiwan FactCheck Education Foundation. It publishes verification reports in Traditional Chinese on politics, health, technology, scams and cross strait rumours, with media literacy material and some English content.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Traditional Chinese source for tracing how false claims circulate in Taiwan, including artificial intelligence fakes and rumours tied to foreign information operations.

name: VSquare
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Media and Information Integrity / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Cross border Central European investigations; region underserved in English
integrity_note: Published by Warsaw's Reporters Foundation and financed by institutional donors, starting with the National Endowment for Democracy; it lists its networks and donors publicly.
description: VSquare is a nonprofit English language investigative outlet on Central Europe, created in 2017 by journalists from the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland and Slovakia. It publishes cross border investigations on Russian and Chinese influence, disinformation, corruption and environmental crime, plus the Goulash newsletter.
what_makes_it_distinct: It pools the work of investigative centres in four countries, giving the reader English access to reporting otherwise locked in local languages.

name: Debates in the Digital Humanities
format: Open access book series, annotatable online editions
topics: Technology and AI / Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Fills the digital humanities gap; open access
integrity_note: A University of Minnesota Press book series edited by academics and hosted open access at CUNY; essays are argued positions within the field, not neutral surveys.
description: Book series from the University of Minnesota Press, edited by Matthew K. Gold and Lauren F. Klein, with open access editions hosted on the Manifold platform at the CUNY Graduate Center. Use its volumes to follow arguments over method, labour, race and infrastructure in digital humanities.
what_makes_it_distinct: The field's main venue for argument about itself, published as open, annotatable books.

name: Engaging Science, Technology, and Society (ESTS)
owner: Society for Social Studies of Science (4S)
format: Peer reviewed articles, thematic collections, essays
topics: Science / Technology and AI / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Open access society journal; critical study of technology and data
integrity_note: Owned by a scholarly society and free to readers and authors, with double blind peer review; the field it serves is openly critical and engaged in stance.
description: Engaging Science, Technology, and Society is the open access journal of the Society for Social Studies of Science, launched in 2015 and free to both readers and authors. Use it for peer reviewed science and technology studies on infrastructure, data, expertise, environment and knowledge politics, including work by scholars outside Europe and North America.
what_makes_it_distinct: The society journal of science and technology studies that charges neither readers nor authors.

name: Kyiv Independent
owner: Kyiv Independent (held by its founding team; states it has no single owner)
format: News, analysis, investigations, documentaries, newsletters, podcasts
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Investigations
modifier_reason: Reader funded reporting from inside a major war zone
integrity_note: It has no single owner and drew 70 percent of 2025 revenue from members and donations; it reports from a Ukrainian standpoint during a war.
description: The Kyiv Independent is an English language news outlet created in November 2021 by journalists dismissed from the Kyiv Post. It publishes continuous news, analysis, investigations, documentaries and newsletters on Ukraine and the war, including a unit investigating war crimes.
what_makes_it_distinct: It reports the war from inside Ukraine without a paywall and has investigated misconduct within the Ukrainian military.

name: Nature
format: Peer reviewed papers, news, features, comment, podcast, daily briefing newsletter
topics: Science / Climate and Environment / Technology and AI / Health
integrity_note: Owned by the commercial publisher Springer Nature, whose income depends on subscriptions and author fees; research is peer reviewed and the news section is editorially independent.
description: A weekly multidisciplinary science journal founded in 1869 and published in London by Springer Nature, combining peer reviewed research with a professional news and comment section. Use the news pages and the Nature Briefing newsletter for science policy, climate and AI research, and consult papers as primary evidence.
what_makes_it_distinct: Joins a flagship peer reviewed journal to a staffed newsroom covering science policy every week.

name: la diaria
owner: La Diaria S.A., majority held by its workers' cooperative
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Worker managed, subscriber funded daily adds ownership diversity from Uruguay
integrity_note: Majority owned by its workers through a cooperative and funded mainly by subscribers; its editorial line is left of centre and it says so.
description: la diaria is a Uruguayan daily newspaper founded in 2006, managed by its workers and financed mainly by subscribers. It covers national politics, justice, labour, education, culture and international news, with separate editions for several of the country's departments.
what_makes_it_distinct: A worker managed, subscriber funded daily with a dedicated labour beat, showing a cooperative ownership model that is rare in the Spanish language press.

name: Daily Maverick
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Economy and Finance / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Strong African accountability reporting with a climate desk
integrity_note: Privately owned by its founders and investors, with income from voluntary memberships, advertising, sponsored content and philanthropy; opinion and sponsored pieces are labelled.
description: Daily Maverick is a South African digital news publisher founded in 2009 that covers politics, corruption, business, the environment and sport. It is known for investigations into state capture and funds itself through voluntary reader membership, advertising and grants.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its Our Burning Planet desk gives sustained climate and environment reporting from southern Africa alongside municipal accountability coverage.

name: Tansa
format: Investigative series, document releases, English versions
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Ownership diversity in a press club dominated media system
integrity_note: Funded by reader donations and foundation grants with no advertising; it openly campaigns on its chosen issues, so read it as investigative advocacy.
description: Tansa is a Tokyo nonprofit newsroom devoted to investigative reporting, launched in 2017 as Waseda Chronicle and independent of the university since 2018. It publishes long running series on government secrecy, corporate wrongdoing, chemical pollution and defence policy, free to read in Japanese with some English versions.
what_makes_it_distinct: Works outside Japan's press clubs, takes no advertising, and offers document based Japanese reading on pollution, public records and whistleblowers at a manageable pace.

name: The Caravan
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Human Rights and Justice / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Rigorous long form scrutiny scarce in Indian media
integrity_note: Published by the family owned Delhi Press and supported by subscribers; it is sharply critical of the Modi government and lists lawsuits it has faced.
description: The Caravan is a monthly magazine of long form narrative journalism published by Delhi Press and relaunched in its current form in 2010. It publishes reportage, investigations, profiles, essays and literary criticism on Indian and South Asian politics, society, labour, religion and culture.
what_makes_it_distinct: Deep investigative profiles and reportage on power, caste and labour in India, with a public record of the legal cases brought against it.

name: +972 Magazine
topics: Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice / Investigations / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Nonprofit binational newsroom; reporting on AI in armed conflict
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded by foundations and reader donations, with no state or corporate owner; its reporting is openly committed to ending the occupation.
description: +972 Magazine is an independent online magazine founded in 2010 and run by a nonprofit group of Israeli and Palestinian journalists. Use it for field reporting and investigations from Israel and Palestine, including work on military use of artificial intelligence, read with its declared opposition to the occupation in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: A joint Palestinian and Israeli newsroom whose investigations into automated targeting have been cited worldwide.

name: CENOZO
owner: Cellule Norbert Zongo pour le journalisme d'investigation en Afrique de l'Ouest (CENOZO)
topics: Investigations / Economy and Finance / Human Rights and Justice / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Francophone Sahel investigations, an underserved geography
integrity_note: Membership association with a seven person board, dependent on international donor grants; publishing is sparse and its funders are not confirmed.
description: CENOZO, the Norbert Zongo Cell for Investigative Journalism in West Africa, is a Ouagadougou based association that funds, trains and publishes investigative reporters across the region. Its investigations cover illicit financial flows, gold mining, drug markets, corruption and environmental harm, mostly in French.
what_makes_it_distinct: French language investigations on gold, extractives and illicit flows in the Sahel, from member journalists in countries with few independent outlets.

name: Data & Society
format: Research reports, primers, essays, policy briefs
topics: Technology and AI / Labour and Work / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Empirical work on AI and labour supports the reader's decent work theme
integrity_note: An independent nonprofit that lists its foundation funders by year and publishes financials; its research takes an explicit public interest stance on technology.
description: Data & Society is an independent nonprofit research and policy institute in New York, founded in 2014. It studies the social, political and economic effects of data centric technologies, automation and artificial intelligence, publishing reports, primers and essays grounded in empirical and ethnographic research.
what_makes_it_distinct: Field based studies of how algorithms and automation affect workers and communities, directly relevant to labour and decent work questions.

name: La Vie des idées / Books & Ideas
owner: Collège de France (Institut du Monde Contemporain)
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books / Politics and Policy / History
modifier_reason: Free bilingual academic essays; French social science rarely reaches English readers
integrity_note: Hosted by the Collège de France and edited by academics, it carries no advertising but reflects a reformist social science view of French debate.
description: La Vie des idées is a free French magazine of essays, book reviews and interviews written mostly by academics across the social sciences, philosophy, history and the arts. Its English edition, Books and Ideas, translates a large share of the articles.
what_makes_it_distinct: It delivers French social science and philosophy at essay length, free of charge and in both of the reader's daily reading languages.

name: Ada Lovelace Institute
format: Reports, policy briefings, blog essays, events
topics: Technology and AI / Politics and Policy / Law
modifier_reason: Endowment funded AI governance research with public participation methods
integrity_note: Funded chiefly by the Nuffield Foundation, an endowed charitable trust, which gives it stable income but makes it dependent on one funder.
description: The Ada Lovelace Institute is a research institute established in 2018 by the Nuffield Foundation to ensure data and artificial intelligence work for people and society. It publishes reports, policy briefings, public attitudes research and blog essays on governance, regulation and public sector use.
what_makes_it_distinct: Measured, evidence based analysis of artificial intelligence regulation in the United Kingdom and Europe, with public participation research and outside contributors.

name: Coda Story
regions: Global / Russia and Central Asia / Europe
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Technology and AI / Human Rights and Justice / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Nonprofit with a Caucasus and Eurasia vantage point
integrity_note: A nonprofit newsroom funded mostly by foundation grants and donations; its liberal democratic stance is declared and its themes centre on authoritarian power.
description: Coda Story is a nonprofit newsroom launched in 2016 by Natalia Antelava and Ilan Greenberg, registered in New York with an editorial hub in Tbilisi, Georgia. Use it for sustained thematic reporting on authoritarian technology, disinformation, the rewriting of history and oligarchy, with strong coverage of Eurasia.
what_makes_it_distinct: Follows a few authoritarian trends over months instead of chasing daily news, from a Tbilisi editorial base.

name: DGBAS (行政院主計總處)
topics: Data and Statistics / Economy and Finance / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Primary Taiwan data in Traditional Chinese
integrity_note: A cabinet level office of Taiwan's Executive Yuan that also prepares the state budget, so it is a government body, not an arm's length statistics agency.
description: The Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics is the statistical and budget office of Taiwan's Executive Yuan, publishing national accounts, prices, labour force, wage and census data. Use its National Statistics portal for primary figures on Taiwan in Traditional Chinese, with a smaller English edition.
what_makes_it_distinct: The primary source for Taiwan's official labour, price and census statistics, in Traditional Chinese.

name: Musicworks
format: Print magazine with companion audio, online features
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Fills the sound art gap from Canada; nonprofit publisher
integrity_note: A small nonprofit society with a volunteer board, sustained by arts council grants, donors and subscribers; it champions experimental music more than it critiques it.
description: Musicworks is a Toronto magazine of experimental music and sound art founded in 1978 and published three times a year by the nonprofit Musicworks Society of Ontario, each issue paired with a curated recording.
