Use it for profiles of Canadian composers, improvisers, sound artists and instrument builders, including Quebec and Indigenous practitioners.
what_makes_it_distinct: Canada's only magazine devoted to experimental sound, issued with companion audio since the cassette era.

name: Orient XXI
region_label: Middle East, North Africa and Muslim Worlds
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Francophone analysis of the Maghreb and Mashriq; independent association
integrity_note: Run by a nonprofit association and financed largely by reader donations; analysis is well informed and openly sympathetic to Palestinian and Arab civil society perspectives.
description: An online magazine founded in Paris in 2013 by former Le Monde diplomatique editor Alain Gresh and run by a nonprofit association of journalists, academics and former diplomats. Use it in French for reporting and analysis on the Maghreb, Egypt, Palestine and the Gulf, with selected pieces in Arabic and English.
what_makes_it_distinct: French language analysis of the Arab and Muslim worlds by regional writers, with translations into Arabic, English and other languages.

name: Places Journal
format: Long essays, photo essays, reading lists, book series
topics: Architecture / Landscape Architecture / Urban Planning / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Fills the landscape architecture and urbanism gap; nonprofit
integrity_note: A nonprofit journal sustained by a partner network of university design schools, foundations and donors; essays are scholarly and carefully edited, with a consistent progressive, spatial justice outlook.
description: Places Journal is a nonprofit journal of public scholarship on architecture, landscape and urbanism, founded in 1983 and supported by a network of university design schools. Read its long illustrated essays for work on infrastructure, climate, land and spatial justice, including regular writing on maps and media.
what_makes_it_distinct: Free, carefully edited long essays that treat architecture, landscape and urbanism as one field.

name: The Globe and Mail
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Investigations / Indigenous Affairs
integrity_note: Owned by the Thomson family through Woodbridge, which also controls Thomson Reuters; the newsroom has a published code and standards editor, with a business friendly editorial page.
description: Canada's national newspaper, published in Toronto and owned by the Thomson family's Woodbridge Company. Use it for federal politics, business, investigations and Indigenous affairs coverage, and as the English language record against which smaller Canadian outlets can be read.
what_makes_it_distinct: The national English daily with Canada's largest business desk and a long record of investigative reporting.

name: Yale Environment 360
topics: Climate and Environment / Science / Energy
integrity_note: Published at the Yale School of the Environment with named foundation funders and a stated editorial firewall; it mixes reported features with opinion by scientists and advocates.
description: Yale Environment 360 is an online magazine published by the Yale School of the Environment, carrying reporting, analysis and opinion by journalists and scientists on climate, biodiversity, energy and pollution worldwide. Use it for science grounded features and the short E360 Digest when you want context beyond daily climate news.
what_makes_it_distinct: A university published environmental magazine that pairs working scientists with veteran reporters on field features from many regions.

name: ALNAP
owner: ALNAP network; secretariat hosted by and legally part of ODI, London
format: Reports, evaluation library, guidance, webinars, podcast
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Development / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Sector wide evaluation evidence that news sources rarely supply
integrity_note: A member network of aid agencies, donors and UN bodies hosted by ODI; it evaluates the same humanitarian system that funds and governs it.
description: ALNAP is a network of about 100 humanitarian organisations, including NGOs, United Nations agencies, Red Cross and Red Crescent members, donors and academics, hosted by ODI in London. It publishes the State of the Humanitarian System report, evaluation guidance and a library of more than 22,000 learning resources.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its system wide performance reviews and evaluation library give evidence on what humanitarian response achieves, including Red Cross operations, beyond agency press material.

name: AyiboPost
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Humanitarian Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Independent Haitian reporting in French from a core humanitarian context
integrity_note: Independent Haitian digital outlet led by its founders; ownership and funder mix are not confirmed here, and it reports under severe insecurity in Port-au-Prince.
description: AyiboPost is an independent Haitian digital outlet publishing investigations, explainers, video and cultural reporting in French and Haitian Creole, with some English. It covers politics, insecurity, public services, the environment, the diaspora and everyday life in Haiti.
what_makes_it_distinct: Explanatory and investigative reporting by Haitian journalists working in the country, valuable context for humanitarian operations and for daily French reading.

name: International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED)
owner: International Institute for Environment and Development
topics: Climate and Environment / Development / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Adaptation and informal urbanism research with Global South partners
integrity_note: A British charity funded largely by government aid agencies and foundations, whose research is rigorous but framed by an explicit equity and advocacy mission.
description: IIED is an independent policy research institute founded in 1971 by Barbara Ward and based in London, working with partner organizations across Africa, Asia and Latin America. Use its briefings and the journal Environment and Urbanization for evidence on adaptation finance, informal settlements, land rights and locally led adaptation.
what_makes_it_distinct: Decades of partner led research on informal settlements and locally led adaptation, including the journal Environment and Urbanization.

name: Nunatsiaq News
regions: Arctic and Indigenous / Canada and Quebec
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Arctic and Inuit coverage is an underserved geography
integrity_note: Privately owned by Nortext Publishing; it discloses federal journalism subsidies and relies partly on advertising from the governments and Inuit organisations it covers.
description: Nunatsiaq News is the newspaper of record for Nunavut and Nunavik, published by Nortext Publishing Corporation with a newsroom in Iqaluit. Use it for reporting on Inuit governance, housing, climate, health and infrastructure in the eastern Arctic, with some content in Inuktitut.
what_makes_it_distinct: Weekly local reporting from Nunavut and Nunavik, with Inuktitut alongside English.

name: ODI Global
topics: Development / Humanitarian Affairs / Climate and Environment / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Humanitarian policy research close to the reader's field
integrity_note: An independent charity that publishes its funders, most of them governments, foundations and multilateral agencies with a direct interest in the aid policies it studies.
description: ODI Global, formerly the Overseas Development Institute, is a London think tank on development, climate and humanitarian policy that discloses its funders. Use the reports of its Humanitarian Policy Group for evidence on aid reform, local response, displacement and anticipatory action relevant to humanitarian mapping work.
what_makes_it_distinct: Home of the Humanitarian Policy Group, a main research voice on reform of the aid system.

name: China Media Project
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Fills a discourse analysis gap; independent nonprofit
integrity_note: An independent research project that began at the University of Hong Kong; its funders are not clearly disclosed, and it reads party media critically.
description: China Media Project is an independent research organization, founded in 2004 at the University of Hong Kong and now based in the United States with a research hub in Taipei, that analyzes official discourse, propaganda and journalism in the People's Republic of China. Use its dictionary of political terms to read Chinese state media critically.
what_makes_it_distinct: The CMP Dictionary decodes Chinese Communist Party phrases and how official media deploy them.

name: Cultural Survival
regions: Arctic and Indigenous / Global / Latin America and Brazil
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Underserved Indigenous peoples coverage from a nonprofit
integrity_note: The publishing arm of an Indigenous led advocacy nonprofit funded by donors and foundations; it reports accurately but always in support of Indigenous rights claims.
description: Cultural Survival is an Indigenous led nonprofit founded in 1972 and based in Cambridge, Massachusetts, which publishes Cultural Survival Quarterly and produces Indigenous Rights Radio in many languages. Use it for writing by Indigenous authors on land defence, language, climate and UN rights mechanisms worldwide.
what_makes_it_distinct: Indigenous authored reporting and radio from communities worldwide, produced by an organization active since 1972.

name: ICRC Humanitarian Law and Policy Blog
owner: International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Law / Conflict and Security / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Expert debate on technology, law and civilian protection
integrity_note: Hosted and edited by the ICRC, which is funded mainly by governments; posts carry a disclaimer that they are not ICRC positions, yet the institutional frame remains.
description: Humanitarian Law and Policy is a blog hosted by the International Committee of the Red Cross that publishes analysis and debate on international humanitarian law and the policies shaping humanitarian action. Academics, practitioners and ICRC staff write on topics such as artificial intelligence in warfare, the Geneva Conventions and humanitarian principles.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its series on artificial intelligence, digital technology and civilian protection in conflict bear directly on humanitarian data and mapping practice.

name: Canadian Climate Institute
format: Reports, economic modelling, blogs, data trackers
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Politics and Policy / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Costed Canadian adaptation research relevant to resilience work
integrity_note: Created with federal government funding and still largely dependent on it, yet governed by an independent board and willing to report that Canada is missing its targets.
description: The Canadian Climate Institute is a climate policy research organisation created in 2020 as the Canadian Institute for Climate Choices. It publishes modelling and analysis on emissions progress, carbon pricing, adaptation and the costs of climate damage, and has an Indigenous research stream.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its costing of climate damages and adaptation options for Canada supports the case the reader makes for resilience investment.

name: Nepali Times
topics: Climate and Environment / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Politics and Policy / Migration
modifier_reason: Himalayan hazard and climate reporting from Nepal
integrity_note: Privately owned by Himalmedia, the publishing house of founder Kunda Dixit, and funded mainly by advertising; ownership details beyond that are not confirmed.
description: Nepali Times is an English language weekly published in Kathmandu by Himalmedia since 2000. It offers reporting and commentary on Nepali politics, society, culture and business, with sustained attention to climate change, glaciers, floods and landslides, conservation and labour migration.
what_makes_it_distinct: Regular coverage of Himalayan glacial retreat, monsoon floods, landslides and Nepali geography makes it directly relevant to hazard and climate adaptation work.

name: The Funambulist
owner: The Funambulist (founded and edited by Léopold Lambert)
format: Print and digital magazine with six issues a year, essays, podcast, maps
topics: Architecture / Geography and Mapping / Human Rights and Justice / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Critical geography and architecture gap; independent; Global South contributors
integrity_note: Founder led independent magazine that reports being 90 percent funded by subscribers and readers; it is openly committed to anticolonial and antiracist struggles and is not neutral.
description: An independent magazine on the politics of space and bodies, founded by architect Léopold Lambert and edited in Paris, with six themed issues a year. Use it for anticolonial readings of architecture, cartography, borders and urbanism written by contributors from Palestine, the Caribbean, the Pacific and Africa.
what_makes_it_distinct: Reads architecture and cartography as instruments of colonial power, with most contributors writing from the places concerned.

name: GDACS, Global Disaster Alert and Coordination System
owner: Joint framework of the United Nations and the European Commission, operated with the Commission Joint Research Centre
format: Automated hazard alerts, impact estimates, maps, data feeds
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Humanitarian Affairs / Geography and Mapping / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Real time multi hazard alerts with open geodata feeds
integrity_note: Operated by the European Commission's Joint Research Centre with the United Nations; alerts are automated model outputs that the operators themselves call purely indicative.
description: GDACS is a cooperation framework between the United Nations, the European Commission and disaster managers that issues automated alerts and impact estimates after earthquakes, tropical cyclones, floods, volcanic eruptions, droughts and wildfires. The system is operated with the Commission's Joint Research Centre and provides maps and data feeds.
what_makes_it_distinct: Colour coded alerts arrive within minutes or hours of an event, with geodata feeds that can be loaded straight into a GIS.

name: UNHCR, the UN Refugee Agency
languages: Multi / EN / FR / ES / AR / RU / JA / ZH-Hans
owner: United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees
format: Reports, statistics, data portals, news stories
topics: Migration / Humanitarian Affairs / Data and Statistics / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Primary displacement data that no newsroom replaces
integrity_note: A United Nations agency funded by voluntary contributions from a few donor governments; its statistics follow published methods, while its communications advocate for its mandate.
description: The United Nations refugee agency, based in Geneva, which publishes displacement statistics, operational data portals, the annual Global Trends report and field stories. Use it as the primary source for refugee and asylum figures and maps, and check advocacy claims against its Refugee Data Finder.
what_makes_it_distinct: The primary source of global forced displacement statistics, with operational data portals covering each emergency.

name: UNOSAT
owner: United Nations Institute for Training and Research (UNITAR)
format: Satellite derived maps, damage assessments, geodata, reports
topics: Geography and Mapping / Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Operational satellite mapping at the core of humanitarian cartography
integrity_note: A United Nations body financed by voluntary contributions from member states; its analysis is technical, but activations and wording follow United Nations political constraints.
description: UNOSAT is the United Nations Satellite Centre, part of the United Nations Institute for Training and Research in Geneva. It produces satellite derived damage assessments, flood extent maps and geospatial data for humanitarian emergencies, conflicts and disasters, and trains national agencies in their use.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its rapid mapping products and downloadable geodata are primary inputs for humanitarian cartography and can be reused directly in a GIS.

name: Alt News
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Transparent verification methods in a polluted information space
integrity_note: Run by a nonprofit that lives on donations and grants, takes no corporate money and publishes its funding; critics say it mostly targets Hindu nationalist claims.
description: Alt News is an Indian fact checking site founded in 2017 and run by the nonprofit Pravda Media Foundation. It verifies claims by politicians, viral social media posts and mainstream media reports, and publishes its methodology, corrections policy and funding.
what_makes_it_distinct: Shows its verification steps for images and video, a practical reference for open source checking of material from South Asia.

name: Knowable Magazine
topics: Science / Health / Climate and Environment / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Nonprofit publisher; Spanish edition aids language practice
integrity_note: Published by the nonprofit Annual Reviews with foundation grants; editorially separate from the review journals, though it draws heavily on their authors as sources.
description: A free digital magazine launched in 2017 by Annual Reviews, the nonprofit publisher of scholarly review journals in California, with philanthropic support. Use it for explainers that translate review articles across the sciences and social sciences into plain language, and read the Spanish edition for language practice.
what_makes_it_distinct: Journalism built directly on scholarly review articles, with a parallel Spanish edition.

name: Undark
owner: Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT
format: Articles, longform investigations, essays, podcast, newsletter
topics: Science / Health / Climate and Environment / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Nonprofit with an academic host; accountability angle on science
integrity_note: Funded through the Knight Science Journalism Program at MIT, with stated editorial independence from the university and a published fact checking and corrections practice.
description: A nonprofit digital magazine published since 2016 by the Knight Science Journalism Program at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, with stated editorial independence. Use it for reported features and investigations on where science meets politics, environment, health and technology, and for its openly documented fact checking practice.
what_makes_it_distinct: Science journalism that treats research itself as a subject of accountability reporting, housed in a university journalism fellowship.

name: 7iber (حبر)
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Independent Arabic features; ownership diversity
integrity_note: A Jordanian limited company financed by named international media development donors, including Open Society and the European Endowment for Democracy, and by training services.
description: 7iber is an independent Arabic online magazine based in Amman, started in 2007 as a citizen media platform and later developed into a professional newsroom. Use it, through its English pieces or translation, for long reports and analysis on Jordan and the Levant covering labour, rights, cities and digital policy.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Jordanian independent magazine producing long reported features in Arabic outside state and party media.

name: E-Tangata
regions: Pacific and Oceania / Arctic and Indigenous
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy / History / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Indigenous Māori and Pacific voices, trust run, absent from mainstream press
integrity_note: Run by the nonprofit Mana Trust with a part time team; it writes openly from Māori and Pacific standpoints, and its funder mix is unconfirmed.
description: E-Tangata is an online Sunday magazine run by the Mana Trust to strengthen Māori and Pacific voices in New Zealand media. It publishes long interviews, essays, reflections, book extracts and commentary on identity, language, history, politics and the arts.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long form Māori and Pasifika writing on land, language and sovereignty, an Indigenous perspective that complements Canadian debates on reconciliation and community knowledge.

name: New Mandala
owner: Australian National University (Coral Bell School of Asia Pacific Affairs)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Development
modifier_reason: Scholar written Southeast Asia analysis that mainstream outlets rarely provide
integrity_note: Hosted and funded by the Australian National University; editors state they decide without university interference, and contributors are mostly academics writing in their own name.
description: New Mandala is an academic website on the politics and societies of Southeast Asia, hosted by the Coral Bell School of Asia Pacific Affairs at the Australian National University since 2006. It publishes analysis essays, field based commentary and book reviews by scholars from the region and beyond.
what_makes_it_distinct: Scholar written analysis of Indonesia, Myanmar, Thailand and the Philippines that explains village level politics and development rarely covered by news wires.

name: The Public Domain Review
owner: The Public Domain Review (independent nonprofit founded by Adam Green)
format: Essays, curated image and text collections, newsletter, prints
topics: History / Visual Arts / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Cartography history and digital curation gap; reader funded
integrity_note: An independent not for profit project sustained by annual donors and print sales, with no advertising; it names its supporters and links every item to its source archive.
description: An online journal founded in 2011 that curates images, books, maps and films in the public domain from libraries and archives and commissions essays by historians about them. Use it for the history of cartography, diagrams, scientific illustration and other symbolic systems, with every item linked to its source collection.
what_makes_it_distinct: Curated public domain images and maps with scholarly essays, each traceable to the holding archive and free to reuse.

name: Daraj (درج)
topics: Investigations / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Journalist owned Arab outlet outside state and party media
integrity_note: Owned by its founding journalists and financed largely by international donors it names; this frees it from Arab state and party money but ties it to grants.
description: Daraj is an independent digital outlet founded in Beirut in 2017 by the journalists Hazem al-Amin, Alia Ibrahim and Diana Moukalled, publishing in Arabic with a smaller English section. Use the English pages, or translation, for investigations into corruption, gender, minorities and the environment across the Arab world.
what_makes_it_distinct: Founded and owned by veteran Arab journalists instead of a state or party, and a regular partner in global leak investigations.

name: Grist
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Indigenous Affairs
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded by foundations and reader donations, with a declared climate justice perspective that shapes story selection more than accuracy.
description: Grist is a nonprofit newsroom founded in 1999 and based in Seattle, reporting on climate change, energy, environmental justice and solutions, mostly in the United States. Use it for accessible explainers and for its Indigenous affairs desk, which covers land, treaty and resource stories.
what_makes_it_distinct: A climate newsroom with a standing Indigenous affairs desk and a justice centred approach to solutions reporting.

name: Internet Policy Review
owner: Alexander von Humboldt Institute for Internet and Society (HIIG)
format: Research articles, concept papers, special issues, essays, opinion
topics: Technology and AI / Law / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Diamond open access European digital policy scholarship
integrity_note: An academic journal with no fees and transparent peer review; its host institute was founded with Google funding, and opinion pieces are not peer reviewed.
description: Internet Policy Review is a peer reviewed, diamond open access journal on internet regulation in Europe, published by the Alexander von Humboldt Institute for Internet and Society in Berlin. It publishes research articles, concept papers, special issues, essays, news and opinion on digital governance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Free scholarly analysis of platform governance and digital regulation in Europe, with an open review process where authors and reviewers are known.

name: Mediazona
owner: Unconfirmed; founded in 2014 by Nadezhda Tolokonnikova and Maria Alyokhina
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Conflict and Security / Law / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Open source casualty counting and court reporting scarce elsewhere
integrity_note: Funded mainly by reader donations and published from exile after Russia blocked it and labelled it a foreign agent; its founders are opposition activists.
description: Mediazona is an independent Russian outlet founded in 2014 that reports on courts, prisons, policing and political repression. Since 2022 it has also tracked the war in Ukraine, including a named count of Russian military deaths compiled from open sources.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its open source casualty count and mobilisation data apply a documented, repeatable method to a war where official figures are withheld.

name: The Rover
owner: The Rover, founded and led by Christopher Curtis; legal structure Unconfirmed
topics: Investigations / Indigenous Affairs / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Reader funded Montreal ground reporting absent from the chain owned dailies
integrity_note: About 80 percent of its funding comes from subscribers and it has no corporate owner, but the small team writes with open sympathy for its subjects.
description: The Rover is a reader funded investigative outlet founded in 2020 by former Montreal Gazette reporter Christopher Curtis. It reports from Montreal and across Quebec on housing, labour, policing, Indigenous communities and migrant workers, mainly in English with some French.
what_makes_it_distinct: It reports from the ground in the reader's own city on housing, labour and Indigenous communities that the corporate dailies cover thinly.

name: Yellowhead Institute
regions: Arctic and Indigenous / Canada and Quebec
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy / Law / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Indigenous led policy research on land fills a disciplinary gap
integrity_note: University housed and Indigenous led, it openly advocates for Indigenous sovereignty and land restitution, so read it as rigorous advocacy research rather than neutral analysis.
description: Yellowhead Institute is an Indigenous led research and education centre in the Faculty of Arts at Toronto Metropolitan University. It publishes reports and briefs on land, law, governance, status and reconciliation policy, and runs open courses such as Land Back.
what_makes_it_distinct: It gives the reader Indigenous authored analysis of land and jurisdiction, which bears directly on mapping and hazard work with First Nations.

name: Jom
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / History / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Independent member funded voice in a constrained media market
integrity_note: Owned by its founders and funded by paying members, it works under Singapore's restrictive media laws and has received government correction orders.
description: Jom is an independent weekly digital magazine about Singapore, launched in 2022 by Sudhir Thomas Vadaketh and colleagues and funded by paying members. Use its weekly digest and long essays for analysis of Singapore's politics, society, arts and history outside the state linked mainstream press.
what_makes_it_distinct: Member funded slow journalism on Singapore, published outside the government linked media groups.

name: MERIP Middle East Report
owner: Middle East Research and Information Project
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Research based political economy with five decades of archive
integrity_note: Independent nonprofit sustained by donations from readers and supporters, with no state or party ties; its perspective is openly critical and left of centre.
description: The Middle East Research and Information Project is a nonprofit founded in 1971 that publishes Middle East Report, a quarterly written largely by scholars. Issues examine the political economy, social movements, labour, culture and conflicts of the region.
what_makes_it_distinct: Thematic issues on topics such as sanctions, remittances and cultural production give structured, research based depth on political economy.

name: Neue Zürcher Zeitung (NZZ)
owner: NZZ-Mediengruppe (AG für die Neue Zürcher Zeitung)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Swiss paper of record for a priority geography
integrity_note: Owned by a company whose shares are widely held with voting limits, it keeps a classical liberal line historically close to the Swiss Free Democrats.
description: The Neue Zürcher Zeitung is the Zurich daily founded in 1780 and published by the NZZ media group, known for international correspondence, economics and a classical liberal editorial line. Read it in German, or through its English section, for Swiss politics, finance and European affairs.
what_makes_it_distinct: Switzerland's German language paper of record, publishing continuously since 1780.

name: Rappler
format: Articles, investigations, video, fact checks, newsletters
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Media and Information Integrity / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Journalist led independent in Southeast Asia
integrity_note: Journalist founded and controlled company financed by advertising, memberships and grants; it withstood years of legal action under Duterte and keeps a critical liberal outlook.
description: Rappler is a Manila based digital news organization founded in 2012 by Maria Ressa and fellow journalists and owned by Rappler Holdings Corporation. Use it for English language reporting on Philippine politics, disinformation networks, platform accountability and disasters, supported by an active fact checking desk.
what_makes_it_distinct: A journalist founded Philippine newsroom whose research on disinformation networks became an international reference for platform accountability.

name: Syria Direct
topics: Conflict and Security / Humanitarian Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Migration
modifier_reason: Nonprofit built on locally trained reporters; humanitarian relevance
integrity_note: A grant financed nonprofit now registered in Germany, with a stated mission of a democratic and just Syria, so donor priorities and that mission shape coverage.
description: Syria Direct is a nonprofit journalism organization founded in Amman in 2013 and now registered in Germany, publishing in English and Arabic and training Syrian reporters through a network of correspondents inside the country. Use it for local reporting on displacement, housing and property, services, reconstruction and transitional politics that international outlets cover only episodically.
what_makes_it_distinct: Reporting in English and Arabic by Syrian journalists it trains itself, with long attention to housing, land and property rights.

name: AlgorithmWatch
topics: Technology and AI / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Investigations
modifier_reason: Nonprofit AI accountability specialist with a Swiss branch
integrity_note: A grant funded advocacy organisation that campaigns for regulation of automated systems; its research is careful and its funders are published, but it is not a neutral observer.
description: AlgorithmWatch is a nonprofit research and advocacy organization based in Berlin, with a sister organization in Zurich, that investigates automated decision making and its effects on people. Use it for evidence on how AI systems are deployed in welfare, policing, workplaces and platforms across Europe.
what_makes_it_distinct: Combines investigative journalism, system audits and advocacy on automated decision making, with offices in Berlin and Zurich.

name: Climate Home News
topics: Climate and Environment / International Affairs / Energy / Investigations
integrity_note: Published by a small private company, Climate Change News Ltd; its mix of sponsorship, advertising and grant income is unconfirmed, and reporting presumes climate action is needed.
description: An independent London news site published by Climate Change News Ltd, reporting on the international politics of climate change with reporters who follow UN negotiations. Use it for COP talks, climate finance, loss and damage, carbon markets and the positions of developing country blocs, which general outlets cover mainly during summits.
what_makes_it_distinct: Year round reporting on UN climate negotiations and climate finance, including investigations into carbon credit schemes.

name: El Orden Mundial
owner: Unconfirmed (independent company controlled by its founders, directed by Fernando Arancón)
format: Analysis articles, original maps, infographics, podcasts, newsletters
topics: International Affairs / Geography and Mapping / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Original geopolitical cartography in Spanish matches the reader's mapping practice
integrity_note: Financed mainly by more than 9,000 subscribers and controlled by its founders; it describes itself as explanatory analysis, neither journalism nor a think tank.
description: El Orden Mundial is a Spanish language outlet for international analysis that began as a blog in 2012 and became a professional publication in 2018. It publishes explanatory articles, original maps, charts and podcasts on geopolitics, produced by staff analysts and about fifty contributors.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its original thematic maps of geopolitical questions are directly relevant to a cartographer and give the reader Spanish reading with visual support.

name: Carbon Brief
format: Explainers, data analysis, fact checks, newsletters
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Science / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Foundation funded specialist with open data; already among the assumed climate nonprofits
integrity_note: Funded mainly by the European Climate Foundation, a philanthropy that works for climate action; the single funder is disclosed and data and methods are published with each analysis.
description: Carbon Brief is a London based website on climate science, climate policy and energy policy, edited by Leo Hickman and funded mainly by the European Climate Foundation. Use it for explainers, data analysis and fact checks, and for its daily and weekly briefings that digest climate coverage elsewhere.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes its data and methods with each analysis, so its charts and emissions calculations can be checked and reused.

name: Le Grand Continent
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: French language geopolitics with original maps; independent association
integrity_note: Published by an association born at the École normale supérieure and supported by subscriptions, donations and partners not fully listed; its outlook is openly pro European.
description: Le Grand Continent is a French language review of geopolitics, law and ideas founded in 2019 by the Groupe d'études géopolitiques at the École normale supérieure in Paris, with editions in several European languages. Use it for long interviews, annotated primary documents and maps on European and global politics.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes the same European debate in several languages, with annotated source texts and in house cartography.

name: World Bank Open Data and Blogs
topics: Development / Data and Statistics / Economy and Finance
integrity_note: The World Bank answers to member state shareholders; the data are documented and open, while the blogs are institutional analysis by Bank staff.
description: The World Bank's free statistical portal and its staff blogs, covering development indicators for every country along with commentary by Bank economists. Use the data site for comparable national figures on labour, poverty and climate, and read the blogs as institutional analysis, not neutral reporting.
what_makes_it_distinct: The standard free source of comparable national development indicators, downloadable and mapped for every economy.

name: Nikkei Asia
regions: Japan and Korea / Southeast Asia / Taiwan and Greater China / South Asia
topics: Economy and Finance / International Affairs / Technology and AI / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Asian newsroom view; shares an owner with the FT
integrity_note: Owned by Nikkei Inc., whose shares are held by its employees; reporting is reliable, but the group is close to Japanese business and discloses little about itself.
description: English language Asian business and politics publication of Nikkei Inc. in Tokyo, drawing on Nikkei's bureaus across the region. Use it for supply chains, semiconductors, Japanese corporate and policy news, and reporting from Taiwan, China and Southeast Asia written from an Asian newsroom.
what_makes_it_distinct: Asia's largest business newsroom reporting in English, with particular strength on semiconductors and supply chains.

name: ReliefWeb
owner: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA)
format: Situation reports, maps, data, job listings, API
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Conflict and Security / Geography and Mapping
integrity_note: A service of OCHA, the UN humanitarian coordination office, funded by donor governments; it republishes reports from thousands of agencies, each reflecting its own institutional interest.
description: ReliefWeb is the humanitarian information service of the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs, collecting situation reports, maps and assessments from thousands of agencies and governments. Use it as the working reference for any active crisis, filtering by country, disaster type or map format.
what_makes_it_distinct: The largest curated archive of humanitarian situation reports and operational maps, searchable by crisis, country and source.

name: Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre
owner: Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre (reference centre of the IFRC)
topics: Climate and Environment / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Humanitarian Affairs
modifier_reason: Bridges hazard science and humanitarian practice
integrity_note: An IFRC reference centre hosted by the Netherlands Red Cross and funded by donor grants; it serves the Movement and does not scrutinise it.
description: The Climate Centre is the Red Cross and Red Crescent reference centre on climate and extreme weather, supporting National Societies with forecast based action, heatwave guides and climate risk analysis. Use it for practice notes on anticipatory action and early warning that connect science to humanitarian operations.
what_makes_it_distinct: Translates climate science into early action protocols used by Red Cross and Red Crescent societies worldwide.

name: FEWS NET
owner: United States Government (created by USAID; current managing agency Unconfirmed)
format: Food security outlooks, alerts, maps, data explorer
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Climate and Environment / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Early warning reference with open geodata; funding continuity uncertain
integrity_note: Funded wholly by the United States government and taken offline for months in 2025 when that funding stopped; analysis is technical and need not match national consensus.
description: The Famine Early Warning Systems Network was created by the United States Agency for International Development in 1985 to monitor and forecast acute food insecurity. It publishes food security outlooks, alerts, maps and a data explorer covering countries in Africa, Central America, the Caribbean and Asia.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its scenario based projections link climate, markets and conflict to mapped food insecurity outcomes, a working model for early warning analysis.

name: Taiwan Environmental Info Center (環境資訊中心)
owner: 自然保育與環境資訊基金會 (formerly Taiwan Environmental Information Association)
format: News, translated international reports, features, newsletter
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Fills a disciplinary gap in Traditional Chinese environmental news
integrity_note: Published by a conservation foundation that also does environmental trust and advocacy work and relies on public donations, so coverage carries a protection minded outlook.
description: The Environmental Info Center is a nonprofit online news service run by a Taiwanese conservation foundation, formerly the Taiwan Environmental Information Association, which has sent an environmental newsletter since 2000. Its reporters, translators and specialist reviewers cover energy, climate, biodiversity, pollution, land use and international environmental news in Traditional Chinese.
what_makes_it_distinct: Daily Traditional Chinese reporting on climate, energy transition, land use and conservation in Taiwan, checked by specialist reviewers, which few general dailies sustain.

name: The 19th
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Health / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Adds gender lens on policy, but centred on United States politics
integrity_note: Nonprofit funded by foundations, members and sponsors, with financials published; it reports through a declared gender and race equity lens.
description: The 19th is a nonprofit newsroom founded in 2020 that reports on gender, politics, policy and power in the United States. Its staff of nearly 60 covers elections, health, caregiving, work, justice and LGBTQ+ issues, and everything is free to read and republish.
what_makes_it_distinct: Covers caregiving, work and the gendered effects of policy, angles on labour and social protection that general political desks often miss.

name: BBC News Mundo
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Science
modifier_reason: Language service of the BBC already listed; Spanish practice value
integrity_note: Part of the BBC World Service, funded by the licence fee with a UK government grant, and bound by BBC editorial guidelines.
description: BBC News Mundo is the Spanish language service of the BBC World Service, serving Latin America and Spanish speakers in the United States under the BBC's editorial guidelines. Use its explainers and features as reading practice in clear, neutral Spanish and as a Latin American angle on world news.
what_makes_it_distinct: BBC standards applied to explanatory journalism in plain international Spanish, well suited to an intermediate reader.

name: NPR
format: News articles, radio programmes, podcasts, music and arts coverage
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Music and Performing Arts / Science
modifier_reason: Sound public anchor, but general news overlaps stronger listed sources
integrity_note: Independent nonprofit paid for by member station fees, sponsorship and donations; Congress ended federal public media funding in 2025 after sustained political attacks.
description: NPR is a nonprofit American media organisation that produces news, cultural programming and podcasts and distributes them through nearly 250 member stations. Its newsroom covers national and world news, politics, science, health, business, music and the arts.
what_makes_it_distinct: Strong audio formats plus music and arts coverage, with station reporters across the United States who cover disasters where they happen.

name: Environmental Humanities
format: Peer reviewed articles, special sections, living lexicon
topics: Climate and Environment / Philosophy and Ideas / History
modifier_reason: Open access journal in an interdisciplinary gap
integrity_note: Open access and peer reviewed, published by Duke University Press with support from partner universities; scholarship is interpretive and broadly aligned with critical environmental thought.
description: International open access, peer reviewed journal published by Duke University Press and founded in 2012. Read it for interdisciplinary scholarship that brings history, philosophy, anthropology and the arts to bear on climate, extinction, land and multispecies questions, useful background for work on climate adaptation.
what_makes_it_distinct: The field's main journal, free to read, joining humanities methods to environmental questions.

name: LatAm Journalism Review
owner: Knight Center for Journalism in the Americas, University of Texas at Austin
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Human Rights and Justice / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Helps assess Latin American media; narrow topical fit
integrity_note: Published by the Knight Center at the University of Texas at Austin, which depends on foundation grants; it reports on a media sector those same foundations fund.
description: LatAm Journalism Review is the digital magazine of the Knight Center for Journalism in the Americas at the University of Texas at Austin. It reports in English, Spanish and Portuguese on press freedom, media innovation, journalist safety and newsroom sustainability across Latin America and the Caribbean.
what_makes_it_distinct: A guide to who funds, owns and threatens journalism in Latin America, useful for judging the other regional sources in this directory.

name: Maldita.es
format: Fact checks, context pieces, scam alerts, explainers
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Spanish language verification from Europe; partly overlaps with Chequeado
integrity_note: A Spanish nonprofit foundation funded by grants, platform partnerships, services and community donations, which publishes an organisational transparency page.
description: Maldita is the journalism project of a nonprofit foundation of the same name, based in Spain. It debunks hoaxes and scams, adds context to viral claims on politics, science, migration and technology, and runs education, research and public policy work on disinformation.
what_makes_it_distinct: Daily Spanish language verification of viral claims, including scams and manipulated media, with a public transparency page on its organisation and funding.

name: arXiv
format: Preprints, daily listings, RSS feeds, API
topics: Science / Technology and AI / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Primary evidence source run as academic infrastructure
integrity_note: Run from Cornell and funded by the university, the Simons Foundation and member institutions; papers are moderated but not peer reviewed, so each must be judged alone.
description: arXiv is the open access preprint repository founded by Paul Ginsparg in 1991 and operated by Cornell Tech, hosting more than two million papers in physics, mathematics, computer science, statistics and related fields. Use subject feeds such as cs.AI, cs.CV and cs.CY to see research before peer review.
what_makes_it_distinct: The primary open repository where machine learning and physical science research appears months before journal publication.

name: De Correspondent
topics: Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment / Technology and AI / Economy and Finance
integrity_note: Funded almost entirely by paying members with no advertising; its correspondents openly declare their viewpoints, which lean progressive.
description: De Correspondent is a Dutch member funded news site launched in 2013 that rejects the daily news cycle in favour of explanatory and structural reporting on climate, technology, migration and inequality. Its model is worth knowing even without reading Dutch.
what_makes_it_distinct: Built on members rather than advertising, and on explaining systems rather than chasing the day's news.

name: Digital Scholarship in the Humanities
owner: Oxford University Press, for the European Association for Digital Humanities
format: Peer reviewed articles, reviews, conference special issues
topics: Technology and AI / Literature and Books / History / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Fills the digital humanities gap; scholarly association journal
integrity_note: Published by Oxford University Press for the European Association for Digital Humanities, with editors appointed by the scholarly community and standard peer review.
description: Digital Scholarship in the Humanities is a peer reviewed journal published by Oxford University Press for the European Association for Digital Humanities and the Alliance of Digital Humanities Organizations, formerly titled Literary and Linguistic Computing. Use it for methods papers on text analysis, digital editions, spatial humanities and cultural heritage data.
what_makes_it_distinct: The longest running journal of humanities computing, continuing Literary and Linguistic Computing, which began in 1986.

name: The Pudding
format: Interactive visual essays, newsletter, process notes
topics: Data and Statistics / Music and Performing Arts / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Data visualization craft from a small staff run studio
integrity_note: A small collective funded mainly by client work at its sister studio Polygraph and by reader memberships; it states its social justice values openly and publishes methods.
description: The Pudding is a digital publication of visual essays that explain debates in culture through original data analysis, interactive graphics and code, produced by a small team of journalist engineers. Use it as a craft reference for narrative data visualization, scrolling stories and transparent methods instead of as a news source.
what_makes_it_distinct: Each essay is an original data investigation rendered as interactive code, with methods and data shared.

name: VERA Files
format: Fact checks, long form reports, commentary, explainers, video
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Investigations
modifier_reason: Adds verification capacity for an underserved country
integrity_note: Governed by a journalist led board and funded by grants, story sales and donations; it screens donors but depends on foreign grant makers and platform partnerships.
description: VERA Files is a nonstock, nonprofit media organisation founded in 2008 by veteran Filipino journalists. It fact checks false and misleading claims, publishes long form reports and commentary on Philippine politics, rights and governance, trains journalists, and produced the Philippine Media Ownership Monitor with Reporters Without Borders.
what_makes_it_distinct: Documented fact checking with a public corrections log and stated methodology, useful for judging claims during Philippine typhoons, elections and disinformation surges.

name: Boston Review
format: Essays, forums, reviews, poetry, print issues, newsletter
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; forum format adds structured disagreement
integrity_note: A nonprofit magazine supported by readers and donors that publishes annual reports; the outlook is left liberal, tempered by a forum format that prints critical responses.
description: Boston Review is a nonprofit, reader supported magazine of politics, philosophy and literature founded in 1975 and published by Boston Critic, Inc. Use its forum format, in which a lead essay draws invited responses, to follow arguments about justice, technology, labour and democracy.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its forum format prints a lead argument beside invited critical responses, making disagreement the structure of each issue.

name: EJIL: Talk!
topics: Law / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Academic commentary on humanitarian and UN law
integrity_note: Run by the editors of an academic law journal published by Oxford University Press; posts are expert opinion checked by editors, not peer reviewed research.
description: EJIL: Talk! is the blog of the European Journal of International Law, edited by legal scholars and publishing expert commentary within days of major rulings and events. Use it for close analysis of International Court of Justice cases, the law of armed conflict, sanctions, climate litigation and UN institutional law.
what_makes_it_distinct: International law scholars debate rulings and crises in near real time, often ahead of the journal literature.

name: Folha de S.Paulo
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Climate and Environment / Investigations
modifier_reason: Brazilian paper of record; family owned and outside the anglophone press
integrity_note: Controlled by the Frias family through Grupo Folha, which has other commercial interests including UOL; an ombudsman, a public editorial manual and a daily corrections column offset this.
description: Folha de S.Paulo is a Brazilian daily newspaper founded in 1921 and owned by Grupo Folha, controlled by the Frias family, with selected articles in English and Spanish. Use it for national politics, economy and environment in Brazil, and for its ombudsman column and published editorial manual.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Brazilian paper of record with an independent ombudsman and a public editorial manual.

name: 404 Media
owner: 404 Media (owned by its four journalist founders)
topics: Technology and AI / Investigations / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Journalist owned and subscriber funded; adds ownership diversity in technology coverage
integrity_note: Owned by its four journalist founders and funded mostly by subscriptions with some advertising; it has no outside investors, though its finances are not published.
description: 404 Media is a technology news company founded in 2023 by four former Motherboard journalists who own it. It publishes investigations, scoops and features on surveillance, hacking, artificial intelligence, privacy and online culture, with a podcast and newsletters.
what_makes_it_distinct: Original reporting from public records on surveillance, location data and artificial intelligence harms, from a newsroom answerable to subscribers, not investors.

name: Chaire en fiscalité et en finances publiques (Université de Sherbrooke)
format: Research papers, briefs, election tools, bulletin
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Accessible fiscal analysis of Quebec in French, university based
integrity_note: A university research chair with named authors and an advisory committee; it has long acknowledged support from Quebec's finance ministry, which readers should keep in mind.
description: The Chaire de recherche en fiscalité et en finances publiques at Université de Sherbrooke, held by Luc Godbout, analyses tax policy and public finances in Quebec and Canada. It publishes research papers, short briefs, syntheses of party election platforms and plain language tools.
what_makes_it_distinct: It explains Quebec budgets and party platforms with numbers and methods in French, useful background for any public policy reading.

name: Kloop
owner: Kloop Media Public Foundation (liquidation ordered by a Bishkek court in 2024)
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Underserved Central Asian geography with data journalism
integrity_note: Grant and donation funded nonprofit that keeps publishing although Kyrgyz authorities blocked its site and a court ordered its foundation liquidated in 2024.
description: Kloop is a Kyrgyz news outlet founded in 2007 by Bektour Iskender and Rinat Tuhvatshin that also trains young journalists. It publishes news, investigations and data journalism in Russian and Kyrgyz, with some work in English and Uzbek.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the few independent investigative voices from Central Asia, with a data desk and cross border partnerships on corruption.

name: The Canadian Press
owner: Canadian Press Enterprises Inc. (Torstar, The Globe and Mail, Square Victoria Communications Group)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs
integrity_note: Owned by three Canadian media companies that are also its clients; its copy follows strict wire neutrality and a published stylebook.
description: The Canadian Press is Canada's national news agency, founded in 1917 and operated since 2010 by Canadian Press Enterprises, a company owned by Torstar, The Globe and Mail and a third media shareholder. Use its English and French copy, the latter as La Presse Canadienne, as a plain factual baseline on Canadian affairs.
what_makes_it_distinct: The bilingual national wire whose stylebook and straight news copy underlie much of Canadian daily journalism.

name: The Tyee
topics: Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment / Labour and Work / Indigenous Affairs
modifier_reason: Nonprofit, reader supported voice from Western Canada
integrity_note: A nonprofit society since 2022 that relies largely on reader contributions; reporting is original and careful but framed from a progressive British Columbia standpoint.
description: The Tyee is a Vancouver based online magazine founded in 2003 that became a nonprofit in 2022 and relies largely on reader contributions. Read it for original reporting on British Columbia politics, housing, labour, climate and Indigenous affairs that national outlets cover thinly.
what_makes_it_distinct: A reader supported nonprofit newsroom giving Western Canada the sustained regional scrutiny that Montreal and Toronto media rarely provide.

name: openDemocracy
owner: openDemocracy Foundation for the Advancement of Global Education
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Investigations
modifier_reason: Nonprofit with a dedicated forced labour and migration desk
integrity_note: A nonprofit funded mainly by foundations and reader donations, with funders published; it reports from an openly progressive, movement aligned position.
description: openDemocracy is a London based nonprofit media platform, funded by foundations and reader donations, that publishes investigations and commentary on democracy, rights, dark money, gender and labour. Use it for accountability reporting and for the Beyond Trafficking and Slavery section on forced labour, noting its openly progressive line.
what_makes_it_distinct: Publishes its funders in detail and runs a dedicated editorial section on trafficking, forced labour and migrant work.

name: LSE Cities / Urban Age
owner: London School of Economics and Political Science
format: Reports, essays, city data, conference recordings
topics: Urban Planning / Architecture / Politics and Policy / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Fills an urbanism research gap; university based
integrity_note: A London School of Economics research centre whose Urban Age programme is run with Deutsche Bank's Alfred Herrhausen Gesellschaft, a corporate foundation partner since 2005.
description: LSE Cities is a research centre at the London School of Economics, and Urban Age is its long running program of conferences and comparative studies of large cities, run with the Alfred Herrhausen Gesellschaft. Use its reports, essays and city data on density, transport, governance and climate.
what_makes_it_distinct: Comparable data and essays on cities across continents, gathered through two decades of conferences.

name: Myanmar Now
country: Myanmar (operating in exile from Melbourne, Australia)
topics: Investigations / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Exile newsroom covering underserved Myanmar
integrity_note: A donor funded newsroom banned by the junta and working from exile; it states that it is not neutral on fundamental rights but aims for fairness.
description: Myanmar Now is an independent news agency founded in 2015 and led by editor Swe Win, publishing in Burmese and English and working largely from exile since the 2021 military coup. Read it for investigations into the junta, armed resistance, displacement and the economy inside Myanmar.
what_makes_it_distinct: Investigative reporting sourced from inside Myanmar by a newsroom the junta has banned.

name: Novaya Gazeta Europe (Новая газета Европа)
owner: Novaya Gazeta Europe (independent, registered in Latvia)
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice / Investigations
modifier_reason: Exile independent newsroom; some overlap with other Russian exile media
integrity_note: An exile newsroom of former Novaya Gazeta staff funded by donations and grants; independent of the Russian state, openly antiwar, and unable to name all its authors.
description: Novaya Gazeta Europe is the exile newsroom founded in Riga in 2022 by former Novaya Gazeta journalists, led by editor in chief Kirill Martynov. Read its English edition for investigations and reporting on Russian politics, the war in Ukraine, repression and society that cannot be published inside Russia.
what_makes_it_distinct: The exile successor to the paper of Nobel laureate Dmitry Muratov, declared an undesirable organisation by Russia.

name: RFI (Radio France Internationale)
languages: Multi / FR / EN / ES / ZH-Hant / RU
regions: Global / Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa / Europe
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Francophone Africa and Sahel coverage in French
integrity_note: Funded by the French state through France Médias Monde, with statutory editorial independence but a French outlook, most visible in coverage of Africa.
description: RFI is the international public radio service of France, run by France Médias Monde, broadcasting in French and about sixteen other languages with a dense network of correspondents across Africa. Use it daily for news from Francophone Africa and for the Journal en français facile.
what_makes_it_distinct: The deepest daily radio coverage of Francophone Africa, alongside Chinese, Spanish and Russian services.

name: The Moscow Times
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Economy and Finance / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Exile newsroom under foundation ownership for a priority region
integrity_note: Owned by a Dutch foundation and run from Amsterdam after being banned in Russia; funded by grants and reader donations, with an openly anti war editorial stance.
description: The Moscow Times is an independent English and Russian language news outlet founded in Moscow in 1992 by Derk Sauer and run from Amsterdam since 2022, after wartime censorship laws forced the newsroom abroad. Use it for daily Russian politics, economy, society and regional coverage that state media will not carry.
what_makes_it_distinct: The oldest independent English language outlet on Russia, banned there as an undesirable organization and now reporting from exile.

name: Esprit
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / Literature and Books / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Independent French review linking philosophy and public policy
integrity_note: An independent review published by its own small house and sustained by subscribers and sales; centre left and humanist, with contributors across disciplines.
description: Esprit is a French review of ideas founded in 1932 by Emmanuel Mounier and published in Paris by Éditions Esprit. Read it in French for long essays and themed issues on democracy, religion, technology, cities and international affairs, written by philosophers, social scientists and practitioners.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French review founded in 1932 in the personalist tradition that pairs philosophy with current public questions.

name: Hakai Magazine
regions: Global / Canada and Quebec / Arctic and Indigenous
format: Archived longform features, news, audio editions, video
topics: Science / Climate and Environment / Indigenous Affairs
modifier_reason: Closed at the end of 2024; archive only, though relevant to coastal flooding
integrity_note: Funded entirely by the Tula Foundation, which also runs the Hakai Institute, with stated editorial independence; it ceased publishing in December 2024 and is now an archive.
description: Hakai Magazine was an online magazine of coastal science and societies published from Victoria, British Columbia from 2015 and funded by the Tula Foundation. It stopped publishing at the end of 2024; its archive of long features on shorelines, fisheries, coastal hazards and coastal communities remains online.
what_makes_it_distinct: A decade of long science journalism devoted solely to coastlines and the people who live on them.

name: Mekong Review
format: Quarterly magazine of essays, reviews, fiction, poetry
topics: Literature and Books / Politics and Policy / History / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Covers Cambodia, Myanmar and Vietnam; small independent publisher
integrity_note: A small independent quarterly that survives on subscriptions and donations; no outside owner directs it, but its finances and legal structure are not published.
description: Mekong Review is an independent quarterly of essays, reviews, fiction and poetry on Asian politics, history and literature, founded in Phnom Penh in 2015 by Minh Bui Jones. Read it for long essays by writers from Vietnam, Cambodia, Myanmar, Malaysia and Singapore that rarely appear in Western reviews.
what_makes_it_distinct: A literary review edited from within Asia, giving space to writers from mainland Southeast Asia.

name: Sumaúma
topics: Climate and Environment / Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Forest based newsroom with Indigenous voices; openly activist line limits the bonus
integrity_note: Founded in 2022 by Eliane Brum and colleagues and funded by philanthropy and readers; it openly campaigns for the forest and endorses electoral choices in its editorials.
description: Sumaúma is a journalism platform founded in 2022 and based in Altamira, in the Brazilian Amazon, publishing in Portuguese, English and Spanish. It reports on the forest, climate, Indigenous and riverine communities and Brazilian politics, with strong editorial commentary.
what_makes_it_distinct: Reports from within the forest rather than from capital cities and gives space to Indigenous and riverine voices, though its editorials are openly activist.

name: Canada's National Observer
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Politics and Policy / Investigations
integrity_note: Privately held by founder Linda Solomon Wood's Observer Media Group and paid for mainly by subscribers; climate is treated as a cause as well as a beat.
description: Canada's National Observer is an independent digital daily founded in 2015 by Linda Solomon Wood and published by Observer Media Group in Vancouver, with reporters in Ottawa and other Canadian cities. Use it for investigative and explanatory reporting on Canadian climate policy, energy, federal politics and disinformation.
what_makes_it_distinct: A subscriber supported Canadian daily that treats climate and energy as its central political beat.

name: IStories (Важные истории)
topics: Investigations / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Exile investigative nonprofit; adds depth on Russia
integrity_note: A nonprofit exile newsroom banned in Russia as undesirable and reliant on grants and foreign donations, which gives it independence from Moscow but dependence on Western donors.
description: A Russian investigative newsroom founded in 2020 by Roman Anin, working in exile since Russian authorities labelled it undesirable in 2022, and publishing in Russian with an English edition. Use the English pages for data driven investigations into the war economy, sanctions evasion, conscription and elite wealth.
what_makes_it_distinct: Exile reporters combining leaked Russian databases with cross border partners to document the hidden costs of the war.

name: Urban Omnibus
owner: The Architectural League of New York
topics: Urban Planning / Architecture / Landscape Architecture / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Urbanism and landscape gap; nonprofit publisher
integrity_note: Published by The Architectural League of New York, a nonprofit supported by members, grants and donors; authors' views are stated to be their own.
description: Urban Omnibus is the online publication of The Architectural League of New York, publishing essays, interviews and visual series on how the city is designed, built and governed. Use it for carefully edited case studies of infrastructure, housing, public space and urban landscape that transfer to other cities.
what_makes_it_distinct: Reads one city closely as a continuing case study in design, policy and everyday use.

name: MapAction
owner: MapAction (charity registered in the United Kingdom)
format: Emergency maps, response updates, case studies, annual reports
topics: Geography and Mapping / Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Humanitarian cartography practice, a gap among news sources
integrity_note: An independent charity with a trustee board that lists its funders and annual reports; its site is operational reporting and fundraising, not journalism.
description: MapAction is a British charity whose staff and about 80 volunteer geospatial specialists produce maps and data analysis for disaster response agencies. Its site carries emergency response updates, published response maps, preparedness project reports and accounts of its work in more than 150 emergencies.
what_makes_it_distinct: A working example of humanitarian cartography under field conditions, with map products and methods that can be compared directly with Red Cross information management practice.

name: Missing Maps
owner: Collective of member organisations with no separate legal owner (founded by the American Red Cross, British Red Cross, Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team and Médecins Sans Frontières)
format: Mapping tasks, training materials, blog, annual report
topics: Geography and Mapping / Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Central to community mapping practice, though it publishes little
integrity_note: A collective of humanitarian agencies with no separate legal owner; content is project communication by its members, guided by a published ethics statement.
description: Missing Maps is a collective of humanitarian organisations, founded in 2014 by the American Red Cross, British Red Cross, Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Team and Médecins Sans Frontières, that maps places at risk of disaster in OpenStreetMap. Its site offers mapping tasks, training material, a blog and an annual report.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the main coordination point for volunteer and community mapping in places where humanitarian agencies work, with open methods, tools and training material.

name: NASA Earth Observatory
format: Image of the Day, feature articles, satellite imagery, newsletter
topics: Science / Climate and Environment / Geography and Mapping / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Daily annotated satellite imagery supports cartographic practice
integrity_note: An outreach publication of a United States government agency; captions are accurate and sourced, but topics and framing follow agency priorities and budgets.
description: NASA Earth Observatory is the space agency's public outlet for satellite imagery and Earth science stories, published since 1999 and now hosted on the NASA Science site. It posts an Image of the Day with an explanatory caption, feature articles, and coverage of storms, fires, floods and landscape change.
what_makes_it_distinct: Daily annotated satellite images show how remote sensing reveals hazards and land change, and are useful models of cartographic explanation.

name: Nouveau Projet
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Independent Quebec ideas magazine in French
integrity_note: Published by Atelier 10, a small independent Montreal house sustained mainly by subscribers and sales; its essays carry a progressive, humanist outlook.
description: French language magazine of ideas, culture and society published in Montreal by Atelier 10 since 2012. Read it for long essays, reportage and commentary on how Quebec thinks about work, cities, climate and public life, in print issues and on the Atelier 10 site.
what_makes_it_distinct: Quebec's independent magazine of long essays, published by a small Montreal house that also issues books and plays.

name: Forensic Architecture
regions: Global / Middle East and North Africa / Europe
format: Investigations, video, 3D models, interactive platforms, exhibitions
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Investigations / Architecture / Geography and Mapping
modifier_reason: Fills the critical geography and spatial evidence gap; academic research agency
integrity_note: A university based agency funded by research grants and commissions from human rights groups and lawyers; it works openly for victims against state and corporate accounts.
description: Forensic Architecture is a research agency founded by Eyal Weizman in 2010 and based at Goldsmiths, University of London, which reconstructs state and corporate violence through spatial analysis, 3D modelling and open source evidence. Use it as a methods reference for cartography used as evidence in human rights work.
what_makes_it_distinct: Treats architecture and cartography as evidence, publishing the full methodology behind each reconstruction of a contested event.

name: Institute for Catastrophic Loss Reduction (ICLR)
owner: Institute for Catastrophic Loss Reduction (registered charity with insurer members)
format: Research papers, guides, webinars, annual report
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Climate and Environment / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Canadian disaster loss prevention research central to the reader's field
integrity_note: Insurers and reinsurers pay the dues, hold the votes and sit on the board, so priorities follow insured property losses, though research runs with Western University.
description: The Institute for Catastrophic Loss Reduction is a disaster prevention research institute established in 1998 by Canada's insurance community and affiliated with Western University. It studies losses from flood, wildfire, wind, hail and earthquake and publishes guidance for homeowners, builders and municipalities.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its research papers on flood, wildfire and wind resilience turn hazard science into building and municipal practice across Canada.

name: Sahan Journal
topics: Migration / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
integrity_note: A nonprofit newsroom funded by foundations, sponsors and reader members, with funders disclosed; it reports for immigrant communities in Minnesota from their standpoint.
description: Sahan Journal is a nonprofit digital newsroom in Minnesota founded in 2019 by Mukhtar Ibrahim to report for and about immigrants and communities of colour in that state. It is a United States local outlet, not an East African one, so use it mainly as a model of community centred reporting.
what_makes_it_distinct: A local newsroom built by and for immigrant communities, with Somali Minnesotans at its origin.

name: Full Fact
format: Fact checks, government tracker, policy reports, newsletters
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / Health / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Strong transparency; United Kingdom focus adds limited new perspective
integrity_note: A charity with a cross party board that publishes its funders in detail; income mixes individual donations, charitable trusts and payments from technology companies.
description: Full Fact is a London based charity that checks claims made by politicians, public institutions, the media and viral posts in the United Kingdom. It publishes fact checks, a tracker of government pledges and policy reports, and builds automated tools used by fact checkers in other countries.
what_makes_it_distinct: Shows its sources for every verdict and asks for corrections, a useful model for testing statistical claims in public policy debate.

name: Newstapa (뉴스타파)
format: Investigations, documentaries, data projects, weekly video programme
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Member funded investigative model in an underrepresented press system
integrity_note: Funded by member donations with no advertising or government money; a 2023 dispute over an election period interview brought a prosecution and criticism of its verification.
description: Newstapa is the newsroom of the Korea Center for Investigative Journalism, a nonprofit begun in 2012 by journalists who had left or been dismissed from major broadcasters. It publishes investigations, documentaries and data projects on political finance, the judiciary, corporate conduct, labour and technology policy, mostly in Korean.
what_makes_it_distinct: Member funded investigative reporting from South Korea, including cross border work on migrant fishing crews and on the public costs of AI data centres.

name: Haaretz
owner: Haaretz Group (Schocken family majority; Leonid Nevzlin minority shareholder)
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Distinct perspective offset by paywall and heavy opinion volume
integrity_note: Controlled by the Schocken family with a declared liberal line; the Israeli government moved in 2024 to cut official advertising and contact with it.
description: Haaretz is Israel's oldest daily newspaper, published since 1919 in Hebrew and with an English edition. It covers Israeli politics, security, the occupation, the Middle East and the Jewish world with a large stable of analysts and columnists.
what_makes_it_distinct: A major Israeli daily that reports critically on its own government and military, with Palestinian and Arab Israeli columnists on its pages.

name: Kyodo News
owner: Kyodo News (cooperative of Japanese newspapers and NHK)
format: Wire reports, daily digest, features, photos, video
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Solid wire baseline, little added perspective
integrity_note: A nonprofit cooperative paid for by dues from Japanese newspapers and NHK, so no single proprietor directs it, though press club access shapes its sourcing.
