description: Kyodo News is Japan's nonprofit cooperative news agency, established in 1945 and funded by member newspapers and the public broadcaster NHK. Its English site, renamed Japan Wire by Kyodo News in 2025, carries wire reports on Japanese politics, the economy, diplomacy, security, society and sports.
what_makes_it_distinct: A neutral English wire on Japan, quick on earthquakes, typhoons, weather records and residency policy, and a useful baseline against the Japanese dailies.

name: Delayed Gratification
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Subscriber funded and free of advertising; distinct retrospective method
integrity_note: Owned by its founders and funded entirely by subscribers with no advertising, so no advertiser or outside proprietor has a say in coverage.
description: Delayed Gratification is a quarterly print magazine from The Slow Journalism Company in London, founded in 2011, that returns to the news of the previous three months after the dust has settled. Read it for retrospective long features and infographics, funded by subscribers with no advertising.
what_makes_it_distinct: A magazine that reports the news three months late on purpose, with data graphics on what happened next.

name: Le Courrier
format: News, editorials, culture, international solidarity pages
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Reader financed ownership model; Swiss francophone left voice
integrity_note: Owned by a nonprofit association and financed mostly by subscribers and donations; its charter declares an opinion paper committed to social justice, and news framing reflects that.
description: Le Courrier is a Geneva daily founded in 1868 and published by the nonprofit Nouvelle Association du Courrier. It covers Geneva, Vaud and Swiss politics, labour and social movements, culture, religion and international solidarity from a declared humanist and social justice editorial line.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is a rare daily without a commercial owner or major advertisers, and it reports closely on labour disputes and civil society in Geneva.

name: Bruegel
format: Policy briefs, working papers, analysis, datasets, podcasts
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Energy / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: European political economy view beyond Anglo American think tanks
integrity_note: Funded by membership fees from European governments, corporations and institutions, disclosed in detail each year; those members also sit in its governance.
description: Bruegel is a Brussels economic policy think tank founded in 2005. Its scholars publish policy briefs, working papers, datasets and commentary on European macroeconomics, trade, energy and climate policy, digital regulation, labour markets and global economic governance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Gives a European rather than American reading of political economy, energy and technology regulation, with datasets the reader can reuse.

name: Der Spiegel
owner: Spiegel-Verlag Rudolf Augstein GmbH & Co. KG
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Employee ownership and a German vantage point on Europe
integrity_note: Staff hold a majority of the publisher through an employee partnership, alongside Bertelsmann and the Augstein heirs; the 2018 Relotius fabrication case led to tightened standards.
description: Der Spiegel is Germany's largest weekly newsmagazine, published in Hamburg since 1947 by Spiegel-Verlag, in which staff hold a majority stake through an employee partnership. Use the English Spiegel International section for investigations and German views of European politics, since most reporting stays in German behind a paywall.
what_makes_it_distinct: A major newsmagazine majority owned by its own employees, with a large in house fact checking department.

name: Hankyoreh (한겨레)
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Citizen shareholder ownership; progressive Korean daily in English
integrity_note: Owned by tens of thousands of citizen shareholders with no controlling proprietor; it holds a declared progressive line and depends on advertising from large Korean companies.
description: Hankyoreh is a South Korean daily founded in 1988 by journalists dismissed under military rule and owned by tens of thousands of citizen shareholders. Use its English edition for progressive Korean reporting and editorials on labour, democracy, regional politics and relations between the two Koreas.
what_makes_it_distinct: A national daily owned by citizen shareholders, founded to be independent of both government and conglomerates.

name: Center for Global Development (CGD)
format: Working papers, policy briefs, blog, data tools, podcasts
topics: Development / Economy and Finance / Health / Migration
integrity_note: An independent think tank that publishes its funders in detail; large foundation and government grants, notably from the Gates Foundation, support its work on aid policy.
description: The Center for Global Development is an independent think tank founded in Washington in 2001 by Edward Scott, Fred Bergsten and Nancy Birdsall, with a European office in London and published funder lists. Use it for research and blog analysis on aid budgets, development finance, migration, global health and multilateral reform.
what_makes_it_distinct: Economist led scrutiny of aid effectiveness and donor budgets, including an index ranking rich countries on development policy.

name: L'Orient Today / L'Orient-Le Jour
owner: L'Orient-Le Jour (Société Générale de Presse et d'Édition)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Francophone view of the Levant from a local newsroom
integrity_note: Owned by private Lebanese shareholders, it publishes an editorial charter and a transparency page and declares itself nonpartisan and nonsectarian in a polarised media market.
description: L'Orient Today is the English edition of L'Orient-Le Jour, the French language Lebanese daily published in Beirut. Use either edition for independent reporting and analysis on Lebanon, Syria and the wider Levant, with the French pages offering deeper culture and opinion coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Francophone Arab daily with a full English edition produced by its own newsroom.

name: Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
format: Alerts, investigations, annual index, live barometer
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Human Rights and Justice / International Affairs
modifier_reason: French language press freedom data; overlaps partly with CPJ
integrity_note: An advocacy nonprofit funded by donations, foundations and a large share of public grants, including French and European Union money; it campaigns as well as documents.
description: Reporters Without Borders is a Paris based nonprofit founded in 1985 that defends press freedom and the right to information. It publishes daily alerts, investigations, a running count of journalists killed or detained, and the annual World Press Freedom Index covering 180 countries.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its yearly index and country files give a mappable, multilingual record of press freedom conditions, written natively in French.

name: The Elephant
topics: Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas / History / Development
modifier_reason: African authored essays from an underrepresented region
integrity_note: Donor supported and openly Pan-Africanist; it lists funding partners including the Heinrich Boll Foundation and Diakonia, while its legal owner is not confirmed here.
description: The Elephant is a Kenyan platform for essays and analysis established in 2016 on Pan-Africanist principles. It publishes long form commentary by African writers and scholars on politics, governance, culture, history and society in Kenya and across the continent.
what_makes_it_distinct: Runs African authored series on themes such as Chinese migration in Africa, food systems and media freedom that widen the reader's non Western reading.

name: African Arguments
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: African expert voices on West Africa and Sahel; nonprofit
integrity_note: Long hosted by the Royal African Society, a membership charity with corporate and foundation backers; its current owner after the 2026 relaunch is unconfirmed.
description: African Arguments is a platform for analysis, commentary and investigation on African politics and society, long hosted by the Royal African Society in London and relaunched in 2026. Use it for arguments by African writers and scholars on elections, conflict, climate and the economy across the continent.
what_makes_it_distinct: Analysis of African politics written mainly by African scholars and journalists for a general audience.

name: Chatham House
regions: Global / Europe / Russia and Central Asia
format: Research papers, expert comment, events, podcast, The World Today magazine, International Affairs journal
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment
integrity_note: Independent charity funded by governments, corporations, foundations and members, with donors disclosed in bands; analysis reflects a British and Atlantic institutional outlook.
description: The Royal Institute of International Affairs, an independent policy institute founded in London in 1920 that publishes research papers, expert comment, the journal International Affairs and the magazine The World Today. Use its Russia and Eurasia, Africa and environment programs for British institutional analysis, and check its funder disclosures.
what_makes_it_distinct: Origin of the Chatham House Rule, pairing a century of British foreign policy convening with longstanding regional research programs.

name: Environment and Planning D: Society and Space
format: Peer reviewed journal, open companion magazine with essays, forums and book reviews
topics: Geography and Mapping / Philosophy and Ideas / Urban Planning / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Critical geography gap; open companion magazine widens access
integrity_note: Peer reviewed and edited by academics but owned by the commercial publisher SAGE; its openly critical theory stance shapes what it publishes.
description: A peer reviewed journal of critical human geography published by SAGE, examining how space, power and social life shape each other through theory and empirical work. Use the journal for scholarship on territory, borders, race and infrastructure, and the free companion site Society and Space for essays, forums and book reviews.
what_makes_it_distinct: A central theoretical journal of critical geography, paired with an open companion magazine of essays and forums.

name: Jeu, revue de théâtre
format: Reviews, essays, dossiers, interviews, quarterly print issue
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Sustained critical record of francophone theatre in Montreal
integrity_note: A subsidised nonprofit review independent of theatre companies, though it depends on arts council grants and writes from within a small artistic community.
description: Jeu is a quarterly review of the performing arts founded in Montreal in 1976. In print dossiers and frequent online reviews it analyses and records theatre and other stage work from Quebec and the wider francophone world, written by critics, researchers and artists.
what_makes_it_distinct: It reviews current Montreal stage productions online and keeps a critical memory of francophone theatre that few newspapers still maintain.

name: Performing Arts Reviews (表演藝術評論台)
owner: National Culture and Arts Foundation (國家文化藝術基金會)
format: Reviews, themed features, resident critic columns
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Rare open criticism platform for performing arts in Chinese
integrity_note: Run by Taiwan's publicly endowed arts foundation, which also funds many of the companies reviewed, a structural overlap that readers should keep in mind.
description: Performing Arts Reviews is an online criticism platform run since 2011 by Taiwan's National Culture and Arts Foundation. Invited, resident and open submission critics review theatre, dance, music and traditional opera across Taiwan, and themed issues examine cultural budgets, archives and the working conditions of the performing arts.
what_makes_it_distinct: Thousands of signed reviews make it a qualitative archive of Taiwanese theatre, dance and music, written in Traditional Chinese criticism of real intellectual range.

name: Plaza Pública
topics: Investigations / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Indigenous Affairs
integrity_note: Funded by a single Jesuit university that has historically left the newsroom alone; that dependence means its future rests on the university's decisions.
description: Guatemalan digital outlet for investigative and analytical journalism, founded in 2011 at the Jesuit Universidad Rafael Landívar. Read it in Spanish for long reporting on corruption, inequality, land and Indigenous rights in Guatemala; recent pages suggest a farewell or restructuring, so confirm it still publishes.
what_makes_it_distinct: University founded investigative journalism from Guatemala, a country few outlets in the directory cover.

name: Tech Policy Press
format: Analysis, commentary, podcast, newsletter, policy trackers
topics: Technology and AI / Politics and Policy / Media and Information Integrity / Law
modifier_reason: Nonprofit AI governance commentary; some overlap with other technology outlets
integrity_note: A foundation funded nonprofit that publishes mostly opinion and analysis with a declared aim of advancing a democracy movement in technology policy; author affiliations are disclosed.
description: Tech Policy Press is a nonprofit publication founded by Justin Hendrix and Bryan Jones in New York, publishing analysis and commentary from researchers, lawyers and advocates on technology and democracy. Use it for AI governance, platform regulation, surveillance and content moderation debates in the United States, Europe and the Global South.
what_makes_it_distinct: A nonprofit venue where academics and practitioners argue technology regulation in detail, with a weekly podcast.

name: Harvard Design Magazine
owner: Harvard University Graduate School of Design (Harvard Design Press)
format: Themed print issues, essays, interviews, roundtables
topics: Architecture / Landscape Architecture / Urban Planning / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Strong cross disciplinary essays, offset by elite institutional voice
integrity_note: Published by Harvard's design school and free of advertising; it reflects the outlook of an elite institution and runs commissioned essays, not reporting.
description: Harvard Design Magazine is a themed print and online magazine published by Harvard Design Press at the Harvard University Graduate School of Design. Each issue gathers essays, interviews and roundtables on architecture, landscape architecture and urban planning, with contributors from art, science and literature.
what_makes_it_distinct: It treats architecture, landscape and urbanism as one conversation, and its recent issue addresses reuse, repair and fire resilience.

name: OECD
owner: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development
format: Reports, datasets, country reviews, policy briefs
topics: Economy and Finance / Data and Statistics / Labour and Work / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Funded and governed by its member governments, mostly high income; statistics follow published methods, while policy advice reflects a market liberal consensus among members.
description: The OECD is an intergovernmental organization of mostly high income member countries, based in Paris, that publishes comparative statistics, country reviews and policy research in English and French. Use its data explorer and reports as primary evidence on labour markets, education, taxation, environment and the governance of artificial intelligence.
what_makes_it_distinct: Harmonized statistics that allow direct comparison of member countries, including Canada, Switzerland, France and Japan.

name: Vert
owner: Vert (independent press company founded by Loup Espargilière and Juliette Quef; legal form Unconfirmed)
topics: Climate and Environment / Politics and Policy / Energy / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Reader funded daily climate newsletter in French
integrity_note: Funded by donations from readers, including more than 12,000 monthly members, with no advertising; it openly rejects the idea of objectivity and publishes a manifesto of values.
description: Vert is a free French outlet founded in 2020 that covers current affairs through the lens of ecology, including climate, biodiversity, pollution, health, agriculture and disinformation. It publishes a daily newsletter, a news site, social media reporting and a podcast.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its short daily newsletter is an efficient French language digest of climate and environment news, including European regulation and pesticide policy.

name: Canadian Geographic
owner: Royal Canadian Geographical Society (through Canadian Geographic Enterprises)
format: Features, maps, photography, podcast, six print issues a year
topics: Geography and Mapping / Climate and Environment / Indigenous Affairs
modifier_reason: Adds Canadian geography and map based storytelling
integrity_note: Owned by a nonprofit geographical society but funded partly through sponsored partnerships with governments and industry, worth keeping in mind on resource and energy topics.
description: Canadian Geographic is the magazine of the Royal Canadian Geographical Society, published since 1930. It covers the landscapes, wildlife, environment, exploration, history and Indigenous geographies of Canada through long features, photography and commissioned maps, in six print issues a year and online.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its commissioned cartography and society projects such as the Indigenous Peoples Atlas of Canada make it a working reference for Canadian map design.

name: Geneva Solutions
owner: Unconfirmed (launched by the Heidi.news team; carries Le Temps reporting)
topics: International Affairs / Humanitarian Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Close coverage of Geneva humanitarian and labour institutions
integrity_note: Created after a call for projects by the Swiss Confederation, Canton and City of Geneva; it practises constructive journalism about institutions its backers want to promote.
description: Geneva Solutions is a nonprofit news platform launched in 2020 to cover International Geneva, the cluster of UN agencies, diplomatic missions and NGOs based in the city. It reports on humanitarian affairs, human rights, global health, climate, labour and technology, with a daily newsletter and many guest opinion pieces.
what_makes_it_distinct: It follows the ILO, the Red Cross Movement, the WHO and UN humanitarian bodies at the level of institutional detail the reader's work touches.

name: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC)
owner: International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies
format: Emergency appeals, operational updates, reports, press releases, data
topics: Humanitarian Affairs / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Health / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Primary operational source, but an institutional voice
integrity_note: A membership body answerable to its National Societies and dependent on donor governments; its communications are accurate but promote the work and appeals of the Movement.
description: The IFRC is the Geneva based federation of 191 National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. Its website publishes emergency appeals, operational updates, press releases, policy papers and recurring reports such as the World Disasters Report, in English, French, Spanish and Arabic.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the secretariat of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement's national societies, so it serves as a primary operational source for humanitarian work, not an outside view.

name: UN-SPIDER
owner: United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs (UNOOSA)
format: Knowledge portal, recommended practices, data guides, news
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Geography and Mapping / Science
modifier_reason: Practical remote sensing methods for hazard mapping in three languages
integrity_note: A programme of the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs that depends on a few donor states; content is technical guidance, not independent reporting.
description: UN-SPIDER is the United Nations platform for space based information for disaster management, established by the General Assembly in 2006 and run by the Office for Outer Space Affairs. Its knowledge portal offers recommended practices, data source guides, software lists, advisory mission reports and news.
what_makes_it_distinct: Step by step recommended practices for flood, drought and fire mapping from satellite data make it a practical reference for hazard cartography.

name: World Politics
owner: Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies (published by Johns Hopkins University Press)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Development / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Prestige journal; dense, paywalled and seldom tied to the reader's fields
integrity_note: Owned and edited at Princeton University with an independent editorial board and published by a university press; peer review governs what is accepted.
description: World Politics is a quarterly peer reviewed journal of comparative politics and international relations, founded in 1948 and edited at the Princeton Institute for International and Regional Studies. Use it for theory driven research on states, regimes, development and political economy, read selectively.
what_makes_it_distinct: A small number of long, heavily reviewed articles per issue that often define debates in comparative politics.

name: EUobserver
owner: EUO BV (part of Denník N since February 2026)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Migration / Human Rights and Justice
integrity_note: Its site says it joined the journalist owned Slovak publisher Denník N in February 2026 and relies mainly on subscribers, limiting outside owner and advertiser influence.
description: EUobserver is an independent news site founded in Brussels in 2000 that reports on European Union institutions, migration, rule of law, foreign policy and lobbying. Since February 2026 it has been part of the journalist owned Slovak publisher Denník N; use it as a smaller, subscriber supported counterweight to Politico Europe.
what_makes_it_distinct: A subscriber supported Brussels newsroom, owned by journalists, covering European Union institutions.

name: elDiario.es
owner: Diario de Prensa Digital S.L. (majority held by its journalists)
format: News, analysis, opinion blogs, regional editions, podcasts
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Investigations / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Journalist owned Spanish daily; adds Spanish language policy reading
integrity_note: Majority owned by people who work in the newsroom and financed by members and advertising; it publishes its accounts yearly and holds a clear progressive line.
description: elDiario.es is a Spanish digital daily founded in 2012 and directed by Ignacio Escolar, covering politics, the economy, society and culture with regional editions, analysis and opinion blogs. It is financed by paying members and advertising.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is a readable Spanish language daily for intermediate reading practice, with close coverage of housing, social policy and accountability stories.

name: Climate Action Tracker
format: Country assessments, briefings, data, global temperature updates
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Useful yardstick, but mitigation focus overlaps other climate sources
integrity_note: Run by two nonprofit research institutes on grant funding; methods are published, but its fair share ratings rest on explicit normative choices.
description: Climate Action Tracker is a scientific project run since 2009 by Climate Analytics and NewClimate Institute. It rates the climate targets, policies and finance of the major emitting countries and the European Union against the Paris Agreement goals and projects the global warming that results.
what_makes_it_distinct: Offers a consistent, documented yardstick for national mitigation effort, Canada included, that the reader can cite when framing adaptation needs.

name: Ember
format: Open datasets, data explorer, reports, insights
topics: Energy / Climate and Environment / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Strong open data, though energy is adjacent to the reader's core fields
integrity_note: Philanthropically funded nonprofit that openly argues for a faster shift to clean electricity; its datasets are open and its methods documented.
description: Ember is a nonprofit energy think tank based in London that compiles open data on electricity generation, capacity, emissions and prices for countries worldwide. It publishes the annual Global Electricity Review and regular analysis of coal, gas, solar, wind, batteries and grids.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its open, documented country level electricity data can be downloaded and mapped, which suits a Python and GIS workflow.

name: Current History
owner: Current History, Inc. (published by University of California Press)
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / History
integrity_note: A long established world affairs journal now published by University of California Press; essays are commissioned from scholars and edited, not conventionally peer reviewed.
description: Current History is a journal of contemporary world affairs founded in 1914 and now published by University of California Press, with nine issues a year that each focus on one region. Use the annual China, Russia and Eurasia, Africa and Latin America issues for overviews written by scholars.
what_makes_it_distinct: The oldest United States publication devoted solely to world affairs, organised as yearly issues on single regions.

name: Efecto Cocuyo
owner: Efecto Cocuyo (founder led; legal entity Unconfirmed)
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Humanitarian Affairs / Migration
modifier_reason: Independent reporting from inside Venezuela despite censorship
integrity_note: Founded in 2015 by Venezuelan journalists and sustained by donations and international grants; it works under state blocking and harassment.
description: Efecto Cocuyo is an independent Venezuelan digital news outlet founded in 2015 by journalists Luz Mely Reyes, Laura Weffer and Josefina Ruggiero. It covers politics, the economy, human rights, migration and the humanitarian emergency, and runs a fact checking service.
what_makes_it_distinct: Independent reporting from inside Venezuela on the humanitarian emergency and migration, useful where official data are scarce or withheld.

name: The Architectural League of New York
owner: The Architectural League of New York
topics: Architecture / Urban Planning / Landscape Architecture
modifier_reason: Nonprofit architecture institution; centred on New York
integrity_note: A membership nonprofit funded by members, foundations, public arts grants and sponsors from the design professions, and it publishes annual reports and financial statements.
description: The Architectural League of New York is a nonprofit membership organization founded in 1881 that runs lectures, exhibitions and competitions and publishes the online magazine Urban Omnibus. Use its lecture archive and Urban Omnibus essays for considered writing on architecture, landscape and city making, mostly grounded in New York.
what_makes_it_distinct: A forum more than a century old whose Urban Omnibus magazine treats one city as a laboratory for urban practice.

name: El País
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
integrity_note: Owned by the listed group PRISA, whose indebted finances and shareholder disputes have at times spilled into questions about editorial direction.
description: Spain's leading daily, published in Madrid by PRISA, with an Americas edition staffed from Mexico City and other Latin American bureaus and an English edition. Read it for Spanish and Latin American politics and culture, and as steady reading practice in clear journalistic Spanish.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Spanish language paper of record that treats Latin America as home territory.

name: MIT Technology Review
topics: Technology and AI / Science / Climate and Environment / Energy
integrity_note: Owned by MIT and editorially independent of it; revenue comes from subscriptions, advertising, events and sponsored content from technology firms it also covers.
description: MIT Technology Review is a magazine and website owned by the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and run with editorial independence, covering AI, computing, biotechnology, energy and climate technology. Use The Download newsletter for a daily scan and the long features for sober assessments of what new systems can do.
what_makes_it_distinct: A university owned technology magazine, founded in 1899, that tests industry claims against research evidence.

name: Openbook (閱讀誌)
format: Book reviews, publishing news, interviews, annual book awards
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Adds Traditional Chinese book criticism outside commercial publishers
integrity_note: A nonprofit review site that states a neutral, independent editorial process; its exact operator and funding mix are not confirmed.
description: Openbook is a Taiwanese nonprofit book review site launched in 2017 by former newspaper book page editors. It reports on publishing, reviews new titles, interviews authors and translators, follows international prize news, and runs the annual Openbook Good Books Award through a year long selection process.
what_makes_it_distinct: A dependable Traditional Chinese guide to new fiction, nonfiction and translation in Taiwan, with translator afterwords and criticism that support both reading choice and language upkeep.

name: Ricochet
regions: Canada and Quebec / Arctic and Indigenous
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Climate and Environment / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Reader funded; Indigenous land defence reporting others lack
integrity_note: Nonprofit funded mostly by small reader donations plus foundations and government programs; it reports from an openly left, progressive standpoint and mixes investigations with opinion.
description: Canadian reader funded outlet founded in 2014 out of Quebec's student movement, now publishing in English. Use it for field reporting on Indigenous land defence, policing, labour and press freedom that larger Canadian newsrooms cover thinly.
what_makes_it_distinct: Crowdfunded Canadian newsroom known for frontline reporting from Indigenous land defence actions and the press freedom cases that followed.

name: Tempo (Indonesia)
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Climate and Environment / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Indonesian investigative tradition widens Southeast Asia coverage
integrity_note: A listed company whose main shareholders are foundations and employee bodies tied to its founders, with a long record of resisting political pressure.
description: Tempo is an Indonesian news group in Jakarta, publisher of the weekly Tempo magazine founded in 1971 and banned under Suharto from 1994 to 1998. Use its English site for investigations into corruption, politics, environment and human rights in Southeast Asia's largest country.
what_makes_it_distinct: Indonesia's investigative newsweekly, a symbol of press freedom since surviving a ban under Suharto.

name: The Wire (UK Music Magazine)
format: Monthly magazine, reviews, features, digital archive, audio
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Fills the sound art gap; staff owned
integrity_note: Owned by its own staff since a buyout in 2000 and financed by subscriptions and advertising from record labels, whose releases it also reviews.
description: The Wire is an independent monthly music magazine founded in London in 1982 and owned by its staff since a buyout in 2000. Use it for criticism of experimental, electronic, improvised, jazz and sound art practice worldwide, and for its complete digitized archive available to subscribers.
what_makes_it_distinct: A staff owned monthly that has documented experimental music and sound art without a corporate parent since 2000.

name: Kontinentalist
owner: Kontinentalist (believed to be part of Potato Productions, Singapore)
format: Interactive data stories, maps, newsletter, method notes
topics: Data and Statistics / Geography and Mapping / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Data visualisation craft with an Asian standpoint
integrity_note: A commercial studio that also turns partner organisations' research into stories, so readers should check each piece for a partner or sponsor credit.
description: Kontinentalist is a Singapore based editorial studio, started in 2017, that publishes interactive data stories about Asia. Its writers, designers and developers work together on visual essays about culture, environment, history, cities and society, and state where the data comes from and how it was handled.
what_makes_it_distinct: A craft reference for narrative cartography and data visualisation, showing how research data becomes a public story told from an Asian standpoint.

name: Taiwan Insight
owner: Taiwan Research Hub, University of Nottingham
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / History
modifier_reason: Academic Taiwan commentary; university run
integrity_note: An online magazine hosted by the University of Nottingham's Taiwan Research Hub; essays are editor curated, not peer reviewed, and any external programme funding is unconfirmed.
description: Online magazine of the Taiwan Research Hub at the University of Nottingham, publishing short analytical essays by scholars of Taiwan. Use it for accessible academic commentary on Taiwanese politics, society, culture and cross strait relations, often arranged as special issues on one theme.
what_makes_it_distinct: Academic Taiwan studies written as short essays for general readers, edited from a British university.

name: The Arctic Institute
owner: The Arctic Institute, Center for Circumpolar Security Studies
format: Analysis articles, reports, article series, newsletter, podcast
topics: Climate and Environment / Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Indigenous Affairs
modifier_reason: Arctic policy focus relevant to Canada; complements news coverage
integrity_note: An independent nonprofit think tank whose researchers work largely as a distributed network; its funding sources are not confirmed.
description: The Arctic Institute is a nonprofit research organisation founded in 2011 and registered in Washington, with a network of researchers in several countries. It publishes analysis, reports and article series on Arctic security, governance, climate change, shipping and northern communities.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its policy analysis of Arctic governance, shipping and climate security gives context for Canadian northern hazards and adaptation work.

name: AOC (Analyse Opinion Critique)
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Subscriber funded French ideas daily written by researchers
integrity_note: Funded by subscriptions with no advertising; it publishes signed, argued essays by academics and writers, most from the French centre left, not news reporting.
description: AOC is an independent French online daily of ideas founded in 2018 by Sylvain Bourmeau, publishing one analysis, one opinion and one critique each day by researchers, writers and artists. Use it for considered French language essays on politics, society, ecology, technology and culture.
what_makes_it_distinct: Three long texts a day by academics and writers, and nothing else.

name: The Nature of Cities
owner: The Nature of Cities (United States nonprofit)
topics: Urban Planning / Landscape Architecture / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Fills a landscape and urban ecology gap with contributors from many cities
integrity_note: A small United States nonprofit whose contributors are mostly practitioners and scholars writing as advocates for greener cities; its current funders could not be confirmed.
description: The Nature of Cities is a nonprofit essay platform on urban ecology, green infrastructure, design and environmental justice in cities. It publishes essays, roundtables and reviews by a large international network of scientists, planners, designers, artists and community practitioners.
what_makes_it_distinct: Brings ecologists, landscape architects, planners and artists into one conversation, with many contributors from cities outside North America and Europe.

name: China Digital Times (中国数字时代)
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Censorship archive nobody else maintains; nonprofit
integrity_note: A grant funded nonprofit led by founder Xiao Qiang with a declared mission against censorship; it documents what Beijing removes and does not aim for neutrality.
description: Bilingual nonprofit site founded by Xiao Qiang and based in California, which archives censored Chinese posts, leaked propaganda directives and online slang, and translates them into English. Use it to see what is being removed from the Chinese internet and how people write around censorship.
what_makes_it_distinct: A running archive of deleted Chinese posts and leaked censorship instructions, translated into English.

name: UN-Habitat
format: Flagship reports, urban data, technical guides, news
topics: Urban Planning / Development / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Useful flagship reports; institutional voice overlaps other United Nations sources
integrity_note: Governed by member states and financed largely by earmarked donor contributions; it publishes donor and funding status pages but speaks as an institution.
description: UN-Habitat is the United Nations Human Settlements Programme, based in Nairobi and mandated by the General Assembly to promote sustainable towns and cities. It publishes the World Cities Report, housing and urban indicator data, technical guides and news from projects in more than 90 countries.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its flagship reports and urban indicators cover informal settlements, housing and urban climate action in regions that planning media seldom reach.

name: FactCheck.org
owner: Annenberg Public Policy Center, University of Pennsylvania
format: Fact checks, science and health checks, newsletter
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / Health / Science
modifier_reason: United States politics only; overlaps with other fact checkers
integrity_note: Funded mainly by the Annenberg endowment and individual donors, and it states it takes no money from unions, partisan organisations or advocacy groups.
description: This nonpartisan fact checking site is a project of the Annenberg Public Policy Center at the University of Pennsylvania, founded in 2003. It checks the accuracy of claims in United States politics, including advertising, debates and speeches, and runs a science and health desk.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long, fully sourced checks of American political and health claims, with detailed public disclosure of its funding sources.

name: Notes from Poland
topics: Politics and Policy / Law / Economy and Finance / Energy
modifier_reason: Reliable Poland coverage, but limited overlap with the reader's fields
integrity_note: Published by a nonprofit foundation and funded through donations from readers and supporters; it aims to present all sides and has an advisory board of varied views.
description: Notes from Poland is an English language news site about Poland, founded in Kraków in 2014 by Stanley Bill and published by a nonprofit foundation. It offers daily news with context on politics, law, business, energy, society and history, plus analysis by outside experts.
what_makes_it_distinct: It gives concise daily coverage of a country that matters for European policy, with background that wire reports usually leave out.

name: BBC News Arabic (بي بي سي نيوز عربي)
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Language service of the BBC, which is already listed
integrity_note: Part of the BBC World Service, funded by the licence fee and a Foreign Office grant; its Israel and Gaza coverage has drawn documented criticism and corrections.
description: BBC News Arabic is the Arabic language service of the BBC World Service, publishing online and on television for audiences across the Middle East and North Africa. Use it through browser translation to see how regional stories are framed for Arabic speakers, alongside BBC English coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: The oldest foreign language service of the BBC, broadcasting in Arabic since 1938.

name: Kosovo 2.0
format: Long form explainers, perspectives, interviews, video
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Western Balkans voice otherwise nearly absent from English language media
integrity_note: Independent of political parties but dependent on institutional donors such as Civil Rights Defenders, Luxembourg's development agency and the European Union, which it lists publicly.
description: Kosovo 2.0 is an independent media organisation in Pristina, established in 2010, that publishes explanatory, contextual and narrative journalism on politics, human rights, arts and culture. It also runs public programmes, training for young journalists and small grants for local media.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is a rare long form voice from Kosovo, with contributors from across the Western Balkans writing on justice, memory and culture.

name: Le Droit
owner: Les Coops de l'information (Coopérative nationale de l'information indépendante)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Minority language francophone press outside Quebec, cooperatively owned
integrity_note: Owned by the Coops de l'information cooperative of employees and community members; advertising, subscriptions and public journalism tax credits fund the newsroom.
description: Le Droit is the French language daily of Ottawa and Gatineau, founded in 1913 to defend Franco-Ontarian rights and now published online by the same cooperative as Le Soleil. It covers local news, courts, business, arts and sports on both sides of the Ottawa River.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the main French language newsroom in the federal capital region and a steady voice for the Franco-Ontarian minority.

name: Review of International Political Economy
topics: Economy and Finance / International Affairs / Development
integrity_note: Owned by the commercial publisher Taylor and Francis and edited by an independent academic board; peer reviewed, with a declared openness to heterodox approaches.
description: Review of International Political Economy is a peer reviewed journal published by Taylor and Francis under the Routledge imprint, covering global finance, trade, development, labour and the politics of markets. Use it for theory and evidence behind debates on globalization, sanctions, supply chains and technology governance.
what_makes_it_distinct: A core journal for interdisciplinary and heterodox international political economy.

name: Social Studies of Science
format: Peer reviewed articles, discussion papers, reviews
topics: Science / Technology and AI / Philosophy and Ideas
integrity_note: Published by the commercial house Sage with an independent academic editorial board and peer review; access is mostly through institutional subscription.
description: Social Studies of Science is a peer reviewed journal published by Sage, founded in 1971, and a core venue for science and technology studies. Consult it for empirical and theoretical research on how scientific knowledge, data infrastructures, algorithms and expert systems are made, mostly through institutional subscription.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the founding journals of science and technology studies, with over fifty years of back issues.

name: The Hindu
owner: THG Publishing Private Limited (The Hindu Group, Kasturi family)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs / Science
modifier_reason: Solid national daily; adds an Indian mainstream view without scarcity value
integrity_note: Owned by the Kasturi family through The Hindu Group; it keeps a Readers' Editor and corrections column, and leans centre left in its editorials.
description: The Hindu is an English language daily founded in 1878 and published from Chennai by The Hindu Group. It offers national and state reporting, international news, business, science and an extensive editorial and opinion section.
what_makes_it_distinct: State by state Indian coverage backed by an independent Readers' Editor and a regularly published corrections column.

name: Article 14
topics: Law / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Investigations
modifier_reason: Law focused reporting with open case databases
integrity_note: Named for the equality clause of the Indian Constitution, it reports from a declared rule of law position; owner and funders are not confirmed here.
description: Article 14 is an Indian reporting and research project launched in 2020 by journalists, lawyers and academics. It publishes investigations, reportage and analysis on failures of justice, the rule of law, civil liberties and democratic institutions, and maintains databases such as a sedition case tracker.
what_makes_it_distinct: Combines legal expertise with field reporting and case databases, giving documented depth on rights and institutions in India.

name: En attendant Nadeau
owner: Unconfirmed (believed to be a nonprofit association of its contributors)
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / History / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Free contributor run French book criticism outside commercial media
integrity_note: A free critical journal run by its contributors and supported by reader donations, with no advertising visible; its ownership structure could not be confirmed.
description: En attendant Nadeau is a free French online journal of literature, ideas and the arts, founded in 2016 by former contributors to La Quinzaine littéraire. It publishes daily reviews of fiction, poetry, history, philosophy and social science, gathered into numbered fortnightly issues.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its long reviews of new French and translated books in history, philosophy and literature are free to read and written by specialists.

name: JSTOR Daily
format: Short essays, features, newsletter, reading lists
topics: History / Science / Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Nonprofit bridge from news into open scholarship
integrity_note: Published and paid for by JSTOR, part of the nonprofit ITHAKA, and built to lead readers to JSTOR holdings; articles are fact checked but not peer reviewed.
description: Online magazine published by JSTOR, part of the nonprofit ITHAKA, that explains news and curiosities through peer reviewed scholarship and links each piece to free source articles. Use it as a daily bridge from general reading into humanities and social science research.
what_makes_it_distinct: Every article cites scholarship held on JSTOR and opens those sources free to readers.

name: La Converse
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Migration / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Underrepresented Montreal communities reported in French by a nonprofit newsroom
integrity_note: A nonprofit supported by grants and partners, with a funding page that gives little detail; it openly takes the side of the communities it covers.
description: La Converse is a Montreal nonprofit newsroom led by its founder Lela Savić that practises what it calls dialogue journalism. It reports in French on racialised, immigrant and low income neighbourhoods, covering policing, social justice, youth and local politics.
what_makes_it_distinct: It brings voices from Montreal neighbourhoods such as Montréal-Nord and Lachine that rarely appear in the main French language dailies.

name: Le Soleil
owner: Les Coops de l'information (Coopérative nationale de l'information indépendante)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Investigations
modifier_reason: Cooperative ownership adds diversity to Quebec's concentrated daily press
integrity_note: A cooperative of employees and community members has owned it since Groupe Capitales Médias collapsed in 2019; it still relies on advertising, sponsored content and public tax credits.
description: Le Soleil is a French language daily of Quebec City, founded in 1896 and now published online by a cooperative of its employees and community members. It covers the capital region, Lévis, Charlevoix, Beauce and eastern Quebec, with provincial politics, courts, business, arts and sports.
what_makes_it_distinct: It follows the National Assembly and the Quebec City region closely, from a newsroom that answers to cooperative members rather than a chain.

name: Al-Jumhuriya
topics: Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Syrian intellectual voices scarce in the reader's other languages
integrity_note: A writers' collective born of the Syrian uprising and long run from exile; its funders are not confirmed here and its stance is openly pro democracy.
description: Al-Jumhuriya is a platform for essays, analysis and reportage founded in 2012 by Syrian writers and academics, among them Yassin al-Haj Saleh. It publishes mainly in Arabic, with an English section, on Syrian politics, society, culture and the wider region.
what_makes_it_distinct: Offers Syrian intellectuals writing about their own country at essay length, a perspective rarely available in English or French media.

name: Esse arts + opinions
format: Thematic essays, exhibition reviews, artist portfolios, three issues a year
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Bilingual Montreal art criticism with international contributors
integrity_note: Published by a nonprofit art publisher supported mainly by arts council grants; its writing is theoretically committed and it carries advertising from galleries and museums.
description: Esse arts + opinions is a bilingual contemporary art magazine founded in Montreal in 1984. Each thematic issue pairs essays with exhibition reviews and artist portfolios, covering Quebec, Canadian and international practices in visual art and performance in French and English.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its main essays appear in both French and English, which makes it useful for reading art criticism across the reader's two daily languages.

name: IEEE Spectrum
owner: Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE)
topics: Technology and AI / Energy / Science
integrity_note: Published by the IEEE, the engineers' professional association, with a staff newsroom funded by member dues and advertising from the technology industry.
description: IEEE Spectrum is the magazine of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, written by staff journalists and practising engineers on computing, artificial intelligence, robotics, energy and semiconductors. Read it for technically grounded reporting on how systems actually work, as a check on industry claims.
what_makes_it_distinct: Technology journalism edited for and by engineers, published by the profession's own association.

name: Prachatai
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Labour and Work / Law
modifier_reason: Nonprofit Thai newsroom on rights and labour under legal pressure
integrity_note: Run by a Thai nonprofit foundation on grants and donations, including foreign foundations, and it has faced prosecution and blocking under Thai law.
description: Prachatai is a nonprofit Thai online newspaper founded in 2004 and run by the Foundation for Community Educational Media, with a separate English edition. Use it for reporting on Thai politics, labour, courts and civil society that the mainstream press treats cautiously.
what_makes_it_distinct: Sustained coverage of royal defamation prosecutions and protest movements that Thai mainstream media handle sparingly.

name: Basta!
topics: Labour and Work / Climate and Environment / Investigations / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Useful labour reporting, but overlaps with other French left outlets
integrity_note: Run by a nonprofit association and funded mainly by reader donations with no advertising; it openly describes itself as a media of resistance and transformation.
description: Basta! is a free French online outlet launched in 2008 and run by a nonprofit association with nine staff. It publishes investigations, reportage and analysis on social and environmental questions, with attention to labour, inequality, the far right and corporate conduct.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its labour and social justice reporting comes with an openly stated aim of social transformation, useful as a declared counterpoint to business coverage.

name: Maisonneuve
format: Quarterly magazine, long features, essays, fiction
topics: Literature and Books / Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Independent Montreal nonprofit quarterly; local English language voice
integrity_note: Published by a small nonprofit association in Montreal with no corporate owner; a mix of subscriptions, advertising and public arts grants supports it.
description: Maisonneuve is an English language quarterly of arts, opinion and ideas founded in Montreal in 2002 and published by a nonprofit association. Use it for long reported features, essays and fiction that look at Canadian life from Montreal, at a pace that suits weekend reading.
what_makes_it_distinct: An independent general interest quarterly edited in Montreal, known for long reported pieces by emerging Canadian writers.

name: Québec Science
format: Magazine features, science news, annual discoveries list
topics: Science / Technology and AI / Health / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: French language science reporting rooted in Quebec research
integrity_note: Published since 2008 by Vélo Québec Éditions, the publishing arm of the nonprofit Vélo Québec, and supported by subscriptions, advertising and public magazine grants.
description: Québec Science is a French language science magazine published since 1962, with eight issues a year and a news site. It covers research, health, environment and technology for a general audience and is known for its annual list of ten Quebec discoveries.
what_makes_it_distinct: It reports on Quebec research in French with a magazine's depth, including work from universities and laboratories the reader is likely to draw on.

name: Rhizome
topics: Visual Arts / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Digital art preservation gap; nonprofit arts organization
integrity_note: A nonprofit arts organisation affiliated with the New Museum and funded by grants and donors; its writing serves its own curatorial and preservation programme.
description: Rhizome is a New York nonprofit founded in 1996 and affiliated with the New Museum, which commissions, presents and preserves born digital art and writes about internet culture. Use it for its ArtBase archive, Net Art Anthology and preservation tools when thinking about digital curatorial practice.
what_makes_it_distinct: An arts organization that also builds web archiving software and keeps a public archive of net art since the 1990s.

name: The Asahi Shimbun (朝日新聞)
format: News, investigations, editorials, features, video, podcasts
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Hazards and Disaster Risk / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Japanese reading practice with strong disaster coverage
integrity_note: Privately held by The Asahi Shimbun Company with founding family and employee shareholders; its liberal editorial line and press club access both shape coverage.
description: The Asahi Shimbun is one of Japan's national daily newspapers, founded in Osaka in 1879, with a largely paywalled Japanese news site and an English edition called Asia and Japan Watch. It covers politics, the economy, society, science, culture, disasters and weather, and runs an investigative desk.
what_makes_it_distinct: A full Japanese language daily for reading practice, with a dedicated disaster and weather section and a liberal counterweight to the conservative national papers.

name: Jadaliyya
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Urban Planning / History
modifier_reason: Scholarly Arab world urbanism and political economy
integrity_note: Run largely by volunteer academics through the nonprofit Arab Studies Institute; it openly combines scholarship with advocacy, so expect a critical left perspective.
description: Jadaliyya is an independent online magazine produced by the Arab Studies Institute since 2010. It publishes analysis, essays, interviews and reviews by scholars and writers on the politics, political economy, cities and culture of the Middle East and North Africa, in English and Arabic.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its Cities page and political economy coverage bring academic urban and spatial research on the Arab world into accessible essays.

name: La Revue nouvelle
format: Print issues, thematic dossiers, essays, online articles
topics: Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas / Migration
modifier_reason: Francophone vantage outside France; independent nonprofit association
integrity_note: Published by an independent nonprofit association with a volunteer editorial committee; it holds a declared progressive line and its funding detail is not confirmed here.
description: La Revue nouvelle is a Belgian French language review of politics, society and culture founded in Brussels in 1945 and published by an independent nonprofit association with an editorial committee of academics and practitioners. Use it for essays and thematic dossiers on Belgian federalism, Europe, social policy, migration and ideas from a progressive pluralist position.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Belgian Francophone general review publishing reasoned dossiers since 1945, outside both Paris and the party press.

name: Next City
owner: Next City, a nonprofit organisation based in Philadelphia
topics: Urban Planning / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Useful practice reporting, but one editorial line and mostly American
integrity_note: A foundation and member funded nonprofit with a declared justice mission; reporting is accurate but selects for solutions that fit that mission.
description: Next City is a nonprofit news organisation based in Philadelphia that reports on solutions for more equitable cities. It covers housing, transport, inclusive finance, labour, environment and culture through daily stories, a podcast, webinars and newsletters, mainly in the United States.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its reporting on community finance, cooperatives, housing and local labour policy shows planning ideas as they are tried in practice.

name: Premium Times
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: West African investigative depth from an independent Nigerian newsroom
integrity_note: Privately owned company led by publisher Dapo Olorunyomi, financed by advertising with donor support for investigations; staff have faced arrest and a police raid over reporting.
description: Premium Times is a Nigerian online newspaper based in Abuja, launched in 2011 and published by Dapo Olorunyomi through Premium Times Services Limited. Use it for investigations into corruption, security and elections in Nigeria, and as a West African partner in cross border reporting projects.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Nigerian digital newsroom built around investigations, with a sister centre for fact checking and data journalism.

name: Momus
region_label: Canada and the international art world
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Independent Canadian art criticism; small publisher
integrity_note: An independent publication led by its founder Sky Goodden and supported by readers, patrons and advertisers; criticism is evaluative by design, with no institutional owner.
description: Momus is an independent online publication of art criticism founded in Toronto in 2014 by Sky Goodden, with an accompanying podcast. Use it for long reviews and essays that evaluate contemporary art and its institutions, with regular attention to Canadian artists and exhibitions.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Canadian founded publication devoted to evaluative, long form art criticism.

name: L'actualité
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Science / Health
modifier_reason: Quebec magazine depth in French complements the dailies
integrity_note: Owned by Mishmash Média, a company tied to investor Alexandre Taillefer, whose 2018 role in a Quebec Liberal campaign raised conflict of interest questions; reporting is measured.
description: L'actualité is a Montreal current affairs magazine in French, founded in 1976, covering Quebec and Canadian politics, society, science, health and culture. Read it for explanatory features, political columns and its annual rankings, as a slower complement to Le Devoir, La Presse and Radio-Canada.
what_makes_it_distinct: The main French language general interest newsmagazine in Quebec, with long explanatory features on public policy.

name: Labor Notes
format: Monthly magazine, web reporting, books, training material
topics: Labour and Work / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Worker level labour reporting, a gap in mainstream coverage
integrity_note: A nonprofit sustained by subscribers, donors, book sales and conferences, independent of union leaderships but openly partisan for militant unionism run by members.
description: Labor Notes is a media and organising project founded in 1979 that reports on unions and workplace struggles from the viewpoint of rank and file workers. It publishes a monthly magazine, web reporting, books and training material, and holds conferences for union activists.
what_makes_it_distinct: Ground level reporting on strikes, contracts and organising in North America and abroad, covering labour stories that general news rarely follows.

name: Urbanisme
topics: Urban Planning / Architecture / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: French planning culture; fills a gap
integrity_note: A French planning review funded by subscriptions and sector advertising, bringing researchers and practitioners into the same pages; its current shareholders are unconfirmed.
description: Urbanisme is a French review published since 1932 that debates cities, territories, housing, mobility and ecological transition with planners, architects and researchers. Read it in French for European planning debates that rarely reach English language outlets.
what_makes_it_distinct: Nearly a century of French debate on the city, with planners, architects and geographers in the same pages.

name: PLANAT, National Platform for Natural Hazards
owner: Swiss Confederation (extraparliamentary commission, secretariat at the Federal Office for the Environment)
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Climate and Environment / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Integrated risk management doctrine relevant to Canadian practice
integrity_note: An advisory commission appointed by the Swiss Federal Council and housed in the federal environment office; it presents agreed official strategy, not independent scrutiny.
description: PLANAT is the Swiss National Platform for Natural Hazards, an extraparliamentary commission created by the Federal Council in 1997 and the national focal point for the Sendai Framework. It publishes strategies, reports and guidance on integrated management of natural hazard risks and on adaptation to climate change.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its papers on appropriate levels of safety and integrated risk management give a compact model for comparing national disaster risk governance.

name: Spacing
format: Print magazine, city blogs, podcast, books
topics: Urban Planning / Architecture / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Canadian urbanism gap; independent publisher
integrity_note: A small independent Toronto magazine owned by its publisher and funded by subscriptions, sales and advertising; it writes as an advocate for public space.
description: Spacing is an independent Toronto magazine about Canadian cities, covering public space, transit, planning, housing and urban design in print and through city blogs. Use it for locally informed writing on how Canadian streets, parks and neighbourhoods are planned and contested.
what_makes_it_distinct: A print magazine devoted entirely to the public realm of Canadian cities.

name: PreventionWeb (UNDRR)
owner: United Nations Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR)
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Climate and Environment / Development
modifier_reason: Fills the disaster risk reduction gap at its institutional core
integrity_note: Run by the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, so it reflects the Sendai Framework agenda and answers to member states; much content is submitted by outside organisations.
description: PreventionWeb is the knowledge platform of the UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction, collecting research, policy documents, news and events on disaster risk and the Sendai Framework. Use it to find the evidence base and country policies behind flood preparedness, early warning and resilience work.
what_makes_it_distinct: The central clearinghouse for global disaster risk reduction literature, policy and Sendai Framework monitoring.

name: PBS News
owner: NewsHour Productions LLC (nonprofit subsidiary of WETA)
format: Nightly broadcast, video segments, articles, podcasts, newsletters
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Science / Health
modifier_reason: Overlaps with wires and public broadcasters likely already listed
integrity_note: Nonprofit owned by public station WETA and paid for by PBS, foundations, viewers and named corporate sponsors, all listed on its funders page.
description: PBS News produces the nightly PBS News Hour, Washington Week and related specials for American public television. It is run by NewsHour Productions, a nonprofit subsidiary of the Washington station WETA, and publishes video, articles and podcasts online.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long, calm studio interviews and field reports give more context per story than commercial television, and full episodes are free online.

name: Brookings Institution
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Urban Planning / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Prestige institution adding little new perspective
integrity_note: Funded by foundations, companies and governments and publishes its donors and audited accounts; scholars are nonpartisan by policy but reflect an establishment centre left outlook.
description: The Brookings Institution is a Washington think tank founded in 1916 that publishes research and commentary on economics, governance, metropolitan policy, technology and foreign affairs. Use it for baseline American policy analysis and data, keeping in mind its establishment vantage point and its funding from foundations, corporations and governments.
what_makes_it_distinct: A century old general purpose American think tank, useful mainly as a baseline of establishment policy thinking.

name: Just Security
owner: Reiss Center on Law and Security, New York University School of Law
format: Analysis articles, document trackers, podcast, newsletter
topics: Law / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Overlaps Lawfare and EJIL: Talk! on law and security
integrity_note: Housed at New York University's law school and supported by foundations and donors; contributors are mainly lawyers and former officials writing from a rule of law position.
description: Just Security is an online forum on national security, international law and human rights based at the Reiss Center on Law and Security at New York University School of Law. Use it for expert analysis of the law of armed conflict, sanctions, accountability and technology governance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Legal analysis written by practitioners and scholars, with document trackers and timelines for major cases.

name: The Lancet
format: Research articles, commissions, reviews, editorials, podcasts
topics: Health / Science / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Health and climate work adds value; otherwise a prestige journal
integrity_note: Owned by the commercial publisher Elsevier, part of RELX; its editors act independently and campaign openly, and two prominent papers were retracted.
description: The Lancet is a weekly general medical journal founded in 1823 and published by Elsevier, with a family of specialty titles that includes Lancet Planetary Health and Lancet Global Health. It publishes peer reviewed research, commissions, reviews and editorials on medicine and global health.
what_makes_it_distinct: The Lancet Countdown on health and climate change and Lancet Planetary Health tie heat, hazard exposure and displacement to health outcomes.

name: Afterall
owner: University of the Arts London (Central Saint Martins)
topics: Visual Arts / History / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Fills a curatorial practice gap; academic publisher
integrity_note: A research centre of University of the Arts London that also seeks individual and institutional donors; editorial choices reflect a critical curatorial outlook.
description: Afterall is a journal of contemporary art published twice a year by the Afterall research centre at Central Saint Martins in London and distributed by the University of Chicago Press. Read it for long essays on single artists and on exhibition histories that inform curatorial practice.
what_makes_it_distinct: Pairs essays on each artist and treats exhibition history as a field of study.

name: ChinaFile
format: Essays, reporting, expert conversations, photography, video
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Good debate format, but an American institutional vantage
integrity_note: Published by the Asia Society and paid for by grants and donations without advertising; current funders are disclosed only on request.
description: ChinaFile is a nonprofit online magazine published by the Asia Society. It carries original reporting, essays, photography and the ChinaFile Conversation, in which scholars, journalists and analysts debate current questions on Chinese politics, society, law, technology and relations with the United States.
what_makes_it_distinct: The Conversation format sets several named experts against one another on each China question, so the reader sees a range of informed views instead of one line.

name: ONFR
owner: Groupe Média TFO (Ontario French Language Educational Communications Authority)
format: News, investigations, video reports, weekly current affairs programme
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Franco-Ontarian coverage; partly overlaps Francopresse and Radio-Canada
integrity_note: Owned by TFO, an Ontario Crown agency funded mainly by the province whose legislature ONFR covers; it publishes a code of ethics and a complaints mechanism.
description: ONFR is the news service of Groupe Média TFO, the French language public educational broadcaster of Ontario. Its reporters cover Queen's Park, Parliament Hill, language rights, education and culture for francophone Ontario in text and video, with a weekly current affairs programme.
what_makes_it_distinct: It offers daily reporting in French on Ontario politics and minority language rights, subjects that Quebec centred media cover only occasionally.

name: STAT
topics: Health / Science / Technology and AI / Investigations
integrity_note: Owned by Boston Globe Media Partners, controlled by John Henry; revenue includes pharmaceutical industry advertising and sponsored events, alongside a published ethics policy and supporters list.
description: American health, medicine and life sciences news outlet founded in 2015 and owned by Boston Globe Media. Use it selectively for reporting on biotech, public health agencies, drug regulation and artificial intelligence in medicine; much analysis sits behind the STAT+ subscription.
what_makes_it_distinct: A dedicated newsroom for biomedicine and health policy, with reporters covering regulators and industry daily.

name: Windspeaker
regions: Arctic and Indigenous / Canada and Quebec
format: News articles, arts and book coverage, statements
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Indigenous owned national coverage adds ownership and perspective diversity
integrity_note: Owned by an Indigenous communications society incorporated in Alberta in 1983, not by a political organisation; it also republishes statements from Indigenous leadership bodies.
description: Windspeaker is an online Indigenous news service published by the Aboriginal Multi-Media Society of Alberta, which began printing it in 1983. It covers First Nations, Métis and Inuit politics, rights, culture, books and arts across Canada.
what_makes_it_distinct: It carries national Indigenous news written from an Indigenous worldview, with steady coverage of land, rights and cultural revival.

name: Aeon
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Science / History
modifier_reason: Donor funded charity; philosophy essays in an accessible free format
integrity_note: A registered charity founded and long financed by Paul and Brigid Hains, with reader donations and foundation grants; free to read, without advertising, written mostly by academics.
description: Aeon is a free digital magazine of philosophy, science, psychology, history and culture, published by the charity Aeon Media Group, which also runs the sister site Psyche. Use it for one long essay or short documentary at a time, written mostly by academics and edited for general readers.
what_makes_it_distinct: A registered charity publishing long philosophical essays and curated short documentaries with no paywall and no advertising.

name: Africa Uncensored
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: African owned independent investigative house
integrity_note: Owned by its Kenyan journalist founders and financed largely by donor grants and commissioned productions; investigations target Kenyan officials and institutions without a party line.
description: Africa Uncensored is an independent investigative media house in Nairobi, founded in 2015 by John-Allan Namu and colleagues, that produces documentaries and written investigations on corruption, policing and public services in Kenya and East Africa. Use it for locally produced video investigations and its Piga Firimbi fact checking desk.
what_makes_it_distinct: Investigative documentaries made and owned by Kenyan journalists, not by a foreign broadcaster.

name: Lawfare
topics: Law / Conflict and Security / Technology and AI / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Published by the nonprofit Lawfare Institute in cooperation with Brookings and funded by donors and foundations; contributors are largely lawyers and former officials with an institutionalist outlook.
description: Lawfare is a nonprofit publication of the Lawfare Institute, produced in cooperation with the Brookings Institution and led by Benjamin Wittes, covering national security law and policy. Use it for close legal reading of cybersecurity, AI governance, surveillance, executive power and the law of armed conflict.
what_makes_it_distinct: Lawyers and former officials analyze national security questions within hours, with the primary documents attached.

name: NACLA Report on the Americas
owner: North American Congress on Latin America (NACLA)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Long record on labour and extractivism; one declared political line
integrity_note: Published by a nonprofit founded in 1966 by activists and scholars; it writes from a declared left and solidarity perspective, with print issues distributed by Taylor and Francis.
description: The NACLA Report on the Americas is the quarterly magazine of the North American Congress on Latin America, a nonprofit founded in 1966. It publishes critical analysis of Latin American and Caribbean politics, social movements, labour, extractive industries and United States policy.
what_makes_it_distinct: Decades of English language analysis on labour, extractive industries and social movements in the Americas, written by scholars and journalists from a declared left perspective.

name: Revue du MAUSS
owner: Association MAUSS (Mouvement anti-utilitariste dans les sciences sociales)
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: French social theory run by a scholarly association
integrity_note: Published by an independent association of academics with Éditions La Découverte, it argues a declared anti utilitarian programme and is not neutral on that question.
description: French social science and philosophy review founded in 1981 by Alain Caillé and the Mouvement anti-utilitariste dans les sciences sociales, published twice a year. Read it in French for debates on gift economies, convivialism and critiques of economic reasoning, following the anthropology of Marcel Mauss.
what_makes_it_distinct: The home of the French critique of utilitarianism and of the gift paradigm in social theory.

name: Scroll.in
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Climate and Environment / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Independent Indian newsroom outside the conglomerates
integrity_note: Owned by Scroll Media Inc. and backed by investors and reader memberships, outside India's large conglomerates, while its reporters have faced police complaints.
description: Indian digital news outlet founded in 2014, publishing reporting, analysis and culture writing in English. Read it for field reporting on Indian politics, rights, environment and labour from a newsroom independent of the country's large media conglomerates, supported by members and investors.
what_makes_it_distinct: An Indian digital native known for ground reports and for its books and culture pages.

name: The Brooklyn Rail
format: Monthly journal in print and online, criticism, interviews, poetry, live conversations
