topics: Visual Arts / Literature and Books / Music and Performing Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Artist run nonprofit; strengthens arts and curatorial coverage
integrity_note: An independent nonprofit supported by donors, foundations and art world advertisers, led for years by publisher Phong Bui; its criticism comes from inside the artist community.
description: A nonprofit journal of arts, culture and politics published in Brooklyn since 2000 under artistic director Phong Bui, free in print and online ten times a year. Use it for long artist interviews, exhibition criticism, experimental writing and guest edited critics pages that follow curatorial debates closely.
what_makes_it_distinct: Free, artist run and built around very long conversations between artists, which few art magazines still publish.

name: The Economist
format: Weekly edition, articles, podcasts, newsletters, data
topics: International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Science
modifier_reason: Prestige title whose lens overlaps the FT already listed
integrity_note: Exor, the Agnelli family holding company, is the largest shareholder, while independent trustees protect the editor; articles are unsigned and argue a consistent market liberal line.
description: The Economist is a London weekly founded in 1843 and published by The Economist Group, offering unsigned analysis of politics, business, science and technology from every region. Use it for comparative framing and data journalism, keeping its market liberal editorial line in mind when reading conclusions.
what_makes_it_distinct: A weekly with one collective voice and no bylines, backed by a large data journalism team.

name: The Wire (India)
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Reader funded nonprofit adding South Asia coverage
integrity_note: Published by a nonprofit foundation funded by reader donations and grants; openly critical of the Modi government, sued and raided, and it retracted its Meta stories in 2022.
description: The Wire is a nonprofit Indian news site founded in 2015 by Siddharth Varadarajan, Sidharth Bhatia and MK Venu and published by the Foundation for Independent Journalism in New Delhi. Use it for reporting on Indian politics, civil liberties, caste, labour and media freedom, keeping in mind the Meta stories it retracted in 2022.
what_makes_it_distinct: India's best known reader funded nonprofit newsroom, repeatedly sued over reporting critical of the government.

name: Bon Pote
owner: Bon Pote (founded by Thomas Wagner; states it has no shareholders; legal form Unconfirmed)
topics: Climate and Environment / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Good climate graphics and tools, but overlaps with other French ecology outlets
integrity_note: Entirely reader funded with no advertising or shareholders and a published declaration of interests; it declares an anticapitalist and antiracist editorial line.
description: Bon Pote is a free French outlet founded by Thomas Wagner that covers ecology, digital technology and democracy through explainers, investigations, infographics and data tools. Articles draw on recent scientific literature and are reviewed by scientists where possible.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its climate explainers are sourced to the scientific literature and paired with graphics and tools such as city level climate futures.

name: International IDEA
owner: International IDEA (governed by its member states)
format: Reports, indices, databases, handbooks, policy papers
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Useful electoral databases; overlaps with V-Dem on democracy measurement
integrity_note: Governed and largely funded by its member states, so it speaks as an institution of governments committed to democracy and can be cautious about members.
description: International IDEA is an intergovernmental organisation based in Stockholm, founded in 1995, with a mandate to support sustainable democracy worldwide. It publishes the Global State of Democracy report and indices, electoral and constitutional databases, handbooks and policy papers, and advises on democratic reform.
what_makes_it_distinct: Comparative databases on elections, political finance and constitutions, plus work on climate change and democracy, available in English, French and Spanish.

name: New Naratif
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Labour and Work / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Member funded outlet on Singapore and Malaysia
integrity_note: Member supported and independent of any state or party, but it describes itself as a democracy movement, so its journalism is advocacy by design.
description: New Naratif is a member funded platform for journalism, research, comics and podcasts on democracy, labour and rights across Southeast Asia, started in 2017 by historian Thum Ping Tjin and colleagues. Read it for long explainers on Singapore and Malaysia, while checking how recently it has published.
what_makes_it_distinct: Treats Southeast Asia as one shared political space and publishes comics alongside research.

name: Revista Anfibia
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: University published essays pairing scholars with journalists; Southern Cone perspective
integrity_note: Published by the Universidad Nacional de San Martín, a public Argentine university; its essays lean progressive, and its budget depends on national university funding.
description: Revista Anfibia is a digital magazine of narrative journalism and essays created in 2012 at the Universidad Nacional de San Martín in Argentina. It pairs academics with journalists to write long pieces on politics, society, culture, gender and work in Latin America.
what_makes_it_distinct: Pairs researchers with reporters, producing essays that bring social science to current Argentine and regional debates in literary Spanish.

name: United Nations
languages: EN / FR / ZH-Hans / ES / RU / AR
format: Official documents, reports, treaties, data, press releases, webcasts
topics: International Affairs / Development / Human Rights and Justice / Law
modifier_reason: Overlaps UN News and the agency sites already listed
integrity_note: The official portal of an organisation that answers to its member states; it is the authoritative record of decisions, not an independent assessment of them.
description: The United Nations website is the official portal of the organization, giving access to resolutions, reports of the Secretary General, treaty texts, statistics and meeting records in the six official languages. Use it as the primary source to check what a UN body actually decided or published.
what_makes_it_distinct: The authoritative record of UN decisions and documents, with parallel texts in six official languages.

name: VAN Magazine
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Independent music criticism funded by subscribers
integrity_note: Independently owned by VAN Verlag and funded by subscriptions, with Bank Julius Baer as declared development partner since 2019; its criticism is openly opinionated.
description: Independent online classical music magazine based in Berlin, published weekly in separate English and German editions by VAN Verlag. Read it for long interviews, criticism and reporting on orchestras, composers, institutions and working conditions in music, written without promotional deference.
what_makes_it_distinct: Reader supported classical music journalism that investigates the industry as well as reviewing it.

name: Montreal AI Ethics Institute
topics: Technology and AI / Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Montreal based civic voice on AI ethics, outside industry
integrity_note: A small nonprofit that relies on donations, paid newsletter subscribers and corporate sponsorships; much of its content comes from students and volunteers and is not peer reviewed.
description: The Montreal AI Ethics Institute is an international nonprofit founded in 2018 by Abhishek Gupta and Renjie Butalid to widen public literacy in AI ethics. It publishes The AI Ethics Brief every two weeks, State of AI Ethics reports, policy commentary and plain language research summaries.
what_makes_it_distinct: It condenses AI governance research and policy into short readable briefs, written from Montreal with contributors from many countries.

name: Nexos
owner: Nexos Sociedad, Ciencia y Literatura S.A. de C.V.
topics: Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Urban and data blogs add value; overlaps partly with Letras Libres
integrity_note: Directed by Héctor Aguilar Camín; a centre left liberal monthly that the López Obrador government sanctioned over an advertising contract in 2020, amid mutual hostility.
description: Nexos is a Mexican monthly magazine of politics, society, science and literature founded in 1978 and directed by Héctor Aguilar Camín. Alongside long essays it hosts specialist blogs on law, cities, data, the environment and the economy.
what_makes_it_distinct: Essay length analysis of Mexican public policy, with specialist blogs on cities and data that touch the reader's planning and visualisation interests.

name: Phenomenal World
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Development / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Heterodox political economy gap; nonprofit institute; Brazil analysis
integrity_note: Published by the Jain Family Institute, a research nonprofit financed mainly by one family, so funding is concentrated; essays are scholarly and lean left heterodox.
description: Phenomenal World is a publication of political economy and social analysis produced by the Jain Family Institute in New York, with essays, interviews and research summaries. Read it for careful work on finance, industrial policy, energy transition, labour and development, including regular analysis of Brazil and Latin America.
what_makes_it_distinct: Essays that turn current academic political economy into readable analysis, edited inside an applied research institute.

name: High North News
owner: High North Center for Business and Governance, Nord University
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Climate and Environment / Energy
modifier_reason: Underserved Arctic geography; university based publisher
integrity_note: Published by a research centre at Norway's state Nord University whose purpose is to promote High North development; it follows the Norwegian press code and editors' charter.
description: High North News is an independent online newspaper published by the High North Center at Nord University in Bodø, Norway, in English and Norwegian. Use it for daily reporting on Arctic politics, security, shipping, resources and northern communities written from inside the region.
what_makes_it_distinct: A newsroom housed in an Arctic university that covers the circumpolar North daily in English and Norwegian.

name: The Irrawaddy
topics: Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Humanitarian Affairs
modifier_reason: Myanmar is underserved; exile newsroom funded by donors
integrity_note: An exile newsroom dependent on foreign donor grants, including United States democracy funding in the past; reliable on events but openly opposed to the military regime.
description: Independent news outlet on Myanmar founded in 1993 by exiled journalists and edited by Aung Zaw, publishing in English and Burmese. Use it for daily reporting on the military regime, the resistance, ethnic armed groups and humanitarian conditions, produced largely from outside the country since the 2021 coup.
what_makes_it_distinct: Three decades of independent reporting on Myanmar, sustained through two periods of exile.

name: Indigenous Climate Action
regions: Canada and Quebec / Arctic and Indigenous
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Climate and Environment / Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Indigenous led nonprofit voice on climate in Canada
integrity_note: An Indigenous led advocacy organisation funded by foundations and individual donors under published funding principles; its reports argue a position and are not neutral analysis.
description: Indigenous Climate Action is an Indigenous led organization in Canada, founded in 2015, that publishes reports, toolkits and a podcast on climate policy and Indigenous sovereignty. Use its Decolonizing Climate Policy reports as a primary source on how federal plans treat Indigenous rights, read as advocacy and not as neutral reporting.
what_makes_it_distinct: An Indigenous led organization that analyses Canadian climate policy from the standpoint of Indigenous rights and knowledge systems.

name: Plan Canada
topics: Urban Planning / Indigenous Affairs / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Canadian planning practice in both languages
integrity_note: Published by the Canadian Institute of Planners, the national professional body funded by member dues; it presents the profession's own view of planning, not outside scrutiny.
description: Plan Canada is the magazine of the Canadian Institute of Planners, publishing practitioner articles in English and French on housing, Indigenous planning, climate adaptation and rural and northern communities. Use it to see how Canadian planners frame risk and land use in practice.
what_makes_it_distinct: The professional voice of Canadian planning, published bilingually by the national institute.

name: J-Source
owner: Collaboration of journalism schools led by Toronto Metropolitan University and Carleton University
format: Articles, commentary, research, press freedom tracker
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Law / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Tracks press freedom and media ownership, aiding source evaluation
integrity_note: Produced by university journalism programmes with support from J-Schools Canada and donors; contributors are often industry insiders writing about their own field.
description: J-Source is a publication about Canadian journalism produced by journalism schools led by Toronto Metropolitan University and Carleton University, launched in 2007. It covers newsroom closures, press freedom, media law and ethics, journalism education and research.
what_makes_it_distinct: It tracks press freedom and the health of Canadian newsrooms, which helps the reader judge the other sources in this directory.

name: Science Friday
format: Radio show, podcast, articles, educational resources
topics: Science / Technology and AI / Climate and Environment / Health
integrity_note: Produced by a nonprofit supported by listeners, foundations and sponsors and distributed to public radio stations; it publishes an ethics policy and lists sponsors.
description: Science Friday is a public radio program and podcast produced by the nonprofit Science Friday Initiative, hosted since 1991 by Ira Flatow and distributed to stations by WNYC Studios. Use it as a weekly listening digest of new research in climate, health, space and technology, built on interviews with working scientists.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running public radio science show built on direct weekly conversations with working scientists.

name: Tempo (Cambridge Music Journal)
format: Peer reviewed articles, performance, recording and book reviews
topics: Music and Performing Arts / History
modifier_reason: Academic journal for new music; narrow fit with the themes
integrity_note: Published by Cambridge University Press, a department of the university, with peer review; it began as Boosey and Hawkes's house magazine but is now editorially independent.
description: Tempo is a quarterly journal of new music founded in 1939 as the house magazine of the publisher Boosey & Hawkes and published since 2003 by Cambridge University Press. Use it for scholarly articles on living composers and for reviews of premieres, festivals, recordings and books in contemporary concert and experimental music.
what_makes_it_distinct: The longest running English language journal devoted to contemporary composition, mixing scholarship with reviews of first performances.

name: Dawn
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Climate and Environment / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: South Asian paper of record under press freedom pressure
integrity_note: Owned by the Haroon family through Pakistan Herald Publications; it has kept an independent liberal line despite repeated military and government pressure, including advertising bans.
description: Dawn is the oldest English language daily in Pakistan, founded in 1941 and published in Karachi by Pakistan Herald Publications. Use it for reporting and editorials on Pakistani politics, the economy, climate and flood impacts, and relations with India, Afghanistan and China.
what_makes_it_distinct: The Pakistani paper of record, with detailed reporting on floods and climate vulnerability.

name: Francopresse
owner: Réseau.Presse (formerly Association de la presse francophone)
format: News, analysis, columns, member paper stories, newsletter
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Migration
modifier_reason: Francophone minority communities outside Quebec are otherwise underserved
integrity_note: Run by an association of minority francophone newspapers that relies on federal programme support, so official languages coverage comes from an interested community standpoint.
description: Francopresse is the national news service created in 1988 by the Association de la presse francophone, now Réseau.Presse, which groups French language community newspapers outside Quebec. It reports on federal politics, official languages, immigration and the economy from a minority francophone standpoint and republishes member papers' stories from Acadie to Nunavut.
what_makes_it_distinct: It gathers local reporting from francophone communities in every region of Canada, a view of the country that Quebec and English language media rarely carry.

name: Newslaundry
topics: Media and Information Integrity / Politics and Policy / Investigations
modifier_reason: Subscriber funded media watchdog adds ownership diversity
integrity_note: Subscriber funded and free of advertising, though held as a private company with outside investors; its opinionated house style shows in its media critique.
description: Newslaundry is an Indian digital news company founded in 2012 that is funded by subscribers and carries no advertising. It publishes media criticism, ground reports, investigations, podcasts and video in English and Hindi.
what_makes_it_distinct: Scrutinises Indian television, wire and state media output, which helps the reader judge the reliability of other Indian sources.

name: The Eastern Door
regions: Arctic and Indigenous / Canada and Quebec
owner: Steve Bonspiel (owner, editor and publisher since 2008)
topics: Indigenous Affairs / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Indigenous community press beside Montreal, a perspective otherwise missing
integrity_note: An independently owned community paper, not an organ of the Mohawk Council of Kahnawake; it depends on local advertising and subscriptions.
description: The Eastern Door is the weekly community newspaper of Kahnawake, the Kanien'kehá:ka (Mohawk) territory on the south shore opposite Montreal, founded in 1992 by Kenneth Deer. It covers council politics, land and language issues, culture and sports, and also reports on Kanesatake.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is an Indigenous community newsroom a short drive from Montreal, reporting on Mohawk communities from the inside rather than from outside.

name: Deutsche Welle (DW)
languages: Multi / EN / FR / ES / ZH-Hant / ZH-Hans / RU / AR / DE
owner: Deutsche Welle (public law broadcaster funded by the German federal budget)
format: Articles, video, radio, podcasts, language courses
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Climate and Environment
integrity_note: Funded from the German federal budget under a law that guarantees editorial independence; reporting is professional, but its mandate is to convey German and European perspectives.
description: Germany's international broadcaster, a public law institution in Bonn and Berlin funded from the federal budget and publishing in about thirty languages. Use it for a German and European reading of world events, for its Africa and Asia desks, and for editions in French, Spanish and Chinese.
what_makes_it_distinct: A continental European public voice in roughly thirty languages, including French for Africa and a Chinese service.

name: France 24
regions: Global / Europe / Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security
integrity_note: Owned and funded by the French state through France Médias Monde; daily reporting is professional, but its mandate is to carry a French view of the world.
description: France 24 is the international news broadcaster of France Médias Monde, the French state owned media group, publishing around the clock in French, English, Arabic and Spanish. Use it for rolling coverage of Francophone Africa, the Maghreb and Europe, and for reading one story across several languages.
what_makes_it_distinct: Four parallel language newsrooms under one public mandate, with particular reach in Francophone Africa and the Maghreb.

name: Hetq
topics: Investigations / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Underserved geography with a long investigative record
integrity_note: Published by a journalists' association funded largely by grants; its finance section also carries bank announcements that read like press releases.
description: Hetq is the online newspaper of Armenia's Investigative Journalists NGO, published since 2001 in Armenian, English and Russian. It runs a daily news feed alongside investigations into public spending, mining, utilities and corruption.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running investigative record from Armenia, including scrutiny of mining and water utilities relevant to resource governance.

name: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Development / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Owned by Elsevier, a commercial publisher earning from subscriptions and author fees; editors are independent academics and articles are peer reviewed, though quality varies across a large output.
description: A peer reviewed Elsevier journal covering the full disaster risk reduction field, from risk perception and governance to recovery, insurance and community resilience. Use it to scan new empirical studies, keeping in mind that many articles sit behind a paywall.
what_makes_it_distinct: The widest single journal on disaster risk reduction, spanning engineering, social science and policy.

name: New Eastern Europe
owner: Jan Nowak-Jeziorański College of Eastern Europe
format: Bimonthly magazine, web analysis, podcast, weekly newsletter
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / History
modifier_reason: Regional authors on Eastern Europe and the Caucasus; underserved in English
integrity_note: Published by a Polish nongovernmental organisation in partnership with the European Solidarity Centre and the City of Gdańsk, and financed by subscriptions, grants and partnerships.
description: New Eastern Europe is an English language bimonthly magazine on Central and Eastern European affairs, published since 2011 from Kraków by the Jan Nowak-Jeziorański College of Eastern Europe. It offers analysis, reportage and commentary online, the Talk Eastern Europe podcast and a weekly newsletter.
what_makes_it_distinct: Many of its authors write from within the region, covering Belarus, Ukraine, the Caucasus and the Balkans in depth.

name: Edge Effects
owner: Center for Culture, History, and Environment, University of Wisconsin-Madison
topics: Climate and Environment / History / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Environmental humanities gap, academic and student run
integrity_note: Run by graduate students at a University of Wisconsin-Madison research centre with faculty oversight; no commercial pressure, but an environmental justice outlook shapes its selection.
description: Edge Effects is a digital magazine produced by graduate students at the Center for Culture, History, and Environment in the Nelson Institute, University of Wisconsin-Madison. Read its short essays, interviews and podcast episodes for environmental humanities scholarship on landscape, climate, food and justice written for a general audience.
what_makes_it_distinct: A graduate student edited magazine turning environmental humanities research into short public essays and audio.

name: Inkstick Media
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Nonprofit newsroom with a human centred view of security
integrity_note: Nonprofit newsroom funded by foundations and donors in the peace and security field; reporting leans toward military restraint and scrutiny of the arms industry.
description: Inkstick Media is a nonprofit newsroom founded by Laicie Heeley that reports on foreign policy, weapons, the arms industry and the human costs of security decisions. Use it for accessible reporting and commentary that brings affected people and younger writers into national security debates.
what_makes_it_distinct: Security journalism written for general readers, with a reporting beat on the military industrial complex.

name: New Lines Magazine
regions: Middle East and North Africa / Global
owner: New Lines Institute for Strategy and Policy
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / History / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Local writers add range; single backer limits independence
integrity_note: Published by the New Lines Institute, a Washington think tank with a concentrated funding base, so the magazine depends on one institutional backer.
description: New Lines Magazine is a Washington based magazine launched in 2020 that publishes long form reportage, essays and arguments by writers close to the places they cover. It began with the Middle East and now ranges across Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas.
what_makes_it_distinct: Commissions local reporters for narrative pieces on labour, migration and conflict, such as its investigation of Turkish textile supply chains.

name: Vie des arts
owner: La Société La Vie des Arts
format: Exhibition reviews, artist interviews, thematic dossiers
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Solid exhibition coverage; overlaps with Esse on contemporary art
integrity_note: An independent nonprofit cultural review that lists its team and partners; it depends on arts grants, subscriptions and advertising from galleries and museums.
description: Vie des arts is a quarterly French language review of visual arts in Quebec and Canada, published since 1956. It offers exhibition reviews, artist interviews and thematic dossiers on current and contemporary practices, with attention to the social and political sides of artistic creation.
what_makes_it_distinct: It describes itself as the oldest arts review in Canada and is a steady French language guide to exhibitions in Montreal and across Quebec.

name: CityGeographics
topics: Urban Planning / Geography and Mapping / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Urban cartography practice; one author, infrequent posts
integrity_note: The personal research blog of one University College London academic, with no commercial interest and no editorial review beyond the author.
description: Personal research blog of Duncan A. Smith of the Centre for Advanced Spatial Analysis at University College London, on urban form, density and interactive mapping. Use it for worked examples of city scale data visualization and for the open web maps he builds; posts are infrequent.
what_makes_it_distinct: An urban geographer's own notebook of interactive city maps, with methods explained alongside results.

name: New Left Review
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Economy and Finance / International Affairs / History
modifier_reason: Independent journal with a distinct political economy tradition
integrity_note: Independent journal run by its own editorial committee and financed mainly by subscriptions; it argues from a declared Marxist left position with scholarly depth.
description: New Left Review is an independent London journal founded in 1960 that publishes six issues a year of long essays on political economy, world politics, history and culture. Read it selectively for structural analysis from the Marxist left, and follow its Sidecar blog for shorter pieces.
what_makes_it_distinct: The main English language journal of the intellectual left, with decades of archived essays on capitalism and world politics.

name: World Health Organization (WHO)
languages: EN / FR / ES / AR / RU / ZH-Hans
format: Outbreak notices, guidance, situation reports, data
topics: Health / Humanitarian Affairs / Data and Statistics / Science
integrity_note: Governed by member states and funded largely by earmarked voluntary contributions, so its public statements are careful toward governments and major donors.
description: The World Health Organization is the United Nations specialized agency for health, based in Geneva, and publishes outbreak notices, technical guidance, situation reports and the Global Health Observatory data. Use it as a primary source in health emergencies, reading its statements as those of an agency answerable to member states.
what_makes_it_distinct: Disease Outbreak News gives the official, dated record of each notified public health event.

name: Pivot
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Independent Quebec newsroom in French; ownership diversity
integrity_note: A small independent Quebec nonprofit that states openly it is progressive and does not claim neutrality; it publishes its editorial policy and funding page.
description: Independent French language news site in Quebec, launched in 2021 by journalists from Ricochet's French edition, with an openly progressive line. Read it for reporting on housing, labour, policing and social movements in Montreal and Quebec, alongside La Presse and Le Devoir.
what_makes_it_distinct: Quebec's openly progressive independent newsroom, publishing original reporting in French without a paywall.

name: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL)
regions: Russia and Central Asia / Europe / Middle East and North Africa / South Asia

topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Conflict and Security

integrity_note: Funded by the United States Congress with editorial independence set in statute; its mission to promote democratic values shapes which countries and stories it covers.
description: Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty is a broadcaster funded by the United States Congress and headquartered in Prague, reporting in more than twenty languages for countries where the press is restricted. Use its English site and Russian service for reporting from Central Asia, the Caucasus, Russia, Iran and Afghanistan.
what_makes_it_distinct: Local language bureaus across Central Asia and the Caucasus that few other outlets can match.

name: Repeating Islands
format: Blog posts, news digests, reviews, calls for papers
topics: Literature and Books / Visual Arts / Music and Performing Arts
modifier_reason: Underserved Caribbean arts coverage by scholars; reduced because it aggregates
integrity_note: An unfunded blog run by two Caribbean studies scholars who mostly repost and excerpt items from other outlets; reliability depends on the original source of each post.
description: Repeating Islands is a blog founded in 2009 and edited by the Caribbean studies scholars Ivette Romero and Lisa Paravisini-Gebert, who gather news and commentary on the region's culture. Use it as a daily digest of Caribbean literature, visual art, film, music, environment and scholarly events across the island language areas.
what_makes_it_distinct: A scholar run daily digest covering the Anglophone, Hispanic, Francophone and Dutch Caribbean together.

name: Social Europe
topics: Labour and Work / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: European labour and social policy debate rarely covered in North American media
integrity_note: A small independent publisher with a social democratic outlook, supported by partners close to the labour movement and by advertising that includes the European Parliament's S&D Group.
description: Social Europe is a Berlin based digital publisher of free daily commentary and analysis on European politics, economics, employment and social policy, written mainly by academics and policy experts. It also produces dossiers, books, podcasts and newsletters.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its steady coverage of European labour markets, platform work and industrial policy speaks directly to the reader's interest in decent work and SDG 8.

name: Terrestres
topics: Climate and Environment / Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: French political ecology gap; donation funded association
integrity_note: Run by a small association and funded mainly by reader donations, it argues openly for radical ecology and does not claim neutrality.
description: Terrestres is a free French language online review of political ecology founded in 2018 and run by an editorial collective through the association Les Terrestres, supported by reader donations. Use it for essays, book reviews and translations on radical ecology, land struggles, technology critique and environmental philosophy.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French review that joins environmental humanities scholarship with accounts from land and climate struggles.

name: The Insider
topics: Investigations / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Exile investigative outlet; independent of state and oligarch owners
integrity_note: A founder led exile outlet that asks readers for donations and does not detail its other funding; it reports with an openly adversarial stance toward the Kremlin.
description: The Insider is a Russian investigative outlet founded in 2013 by Roman Dobrokhotov and operated in exile from Latvia, publishing in Russian and English. Use the English edition for investigations into Russian intelligence operations, corruption and disinformation, often produced with partners such as Bellingcat and Der Spiegel.
what_makes_it_distinct: Exile investigative journalism known for identifying Russian intelligence officers through leaked data and open source methods.

name: iPolitics
topics: Politics and Policy / Law
integrity_note: Owned by Torstar, itself held by investor Jordan Bitove's NordStar Capital, and funded by subscriptions and advertising aimed at Ottawa insiders.
description: Ottawa based digital outlet covering Parliament, federal departments, committees and party politics, founded in 2010 and owned by Torstar since 2018. Use it for daily detail on legislation and federal policy files that national papers summarize.
what_makes_it_distinct: Daily reporting from Parliament Hill at the level of committees, bills and departmental files.

name: Anticipation Hub
owner: German Red Cross (host), with the IFRC and the Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre
format: Case studies, guidance, evidence database, blog, events, newsletter
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Humanitarian Affairs / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Core disaster risk practice field with strong Global South case material
integrity_note: Hosted by the German Red Cross and funded by Germany's Federal Foreign Office; it promotes anticipatory action, so expect advocacy alongside the evidence.
description: The Anticipation Hub is a knowledge platform on anticipatory action, founded in 2020 by the German Red Cross, the IFRC and the Red Cross Red Crescent Climate Centre. It gathers case studies, trigger methods, guidance, working group outputs and event material from more than 170 partners.
what_makes_it_distinct: It documents how forecasts and agreed triggers release funds before a hazard strikes, which bears directly on early warning and flood preparedness work.

name: Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency (CDEMA)
owner: Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency, an agency of the Caribbean Community (CARICOM)
format: Situation reports, press releases, strategy documents, databases
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Humanitarian Affairs / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Caribbean small island disaster management, an underserved geography
integrity_note: An agency of Caribbean governments that also relies on external donors; its reports are official accounts and do not criticise member states.
description: The Caribbean Disaster Emergency Management Agency is the intergovernmental disaster management body of the Caribbean Community, established in 1991 and based in Barbados, with 20 Participating States. It publishes situation reports, press releases, regional strategy documents and links to risk information databases.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its situation reports give the regional coordination picture during hurricanes, a small island perspective that global outlets cover only briefly.

name: NRC
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Investigations / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Dutch only; overlaps other European papers of record
integrity_note: Owned since 2015 by the Belgian commercial group Mediahuis; an editorial statute and a standing ombudsman shield a liberal, centrist newsroom from owner direction.
description: NRC is a Dutch daily newspaper of record based in Amsterdam, formed in 1970 from two older liberal papers and now owned by the Belgian group Mediahuis. It publishes only in Dutch, so use it through translation for coverage of the Netherlands, European Union politics and long investigations.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Dutch paper of record with a long standing ombudsman and public corrections practice.

name: The Point
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Nonprofit philosophy magazine with a wide political range
integrity_note: Small nonprofit magazine sustained by subscriptions, donations and institutional sponsors; it declares no political agenda and publishes writers from across intellectual traditions.
description: The Point is a nonprofit magazine of philosophical essays on politics, culture and everyday life, founded in Chicago in 2009 by graduate students from the University of Chicago. Read it when you want slow, reflective essays and symposiums that ask what a good life or a good society requires.
what_makes_it_distinct: Each issue builds a symposium around one plain question about what something is for.

name: C Magazine
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: English Canadian art criticism; some overlap with Esse
integrity_note: Published by a registered charity supported by arts councils; it labels sponsored items and takes openly political, anticolonial editorial positions.
description: C Magazine is a Toronto based magazine of contemporary art and criticism published since the 1980s by a charitable foundation. Its thematic print issues and website carry essays, exhibition reviews and artist projects on Canadian and international practices and their political contexts.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the English language counterpart to Esse, offering criticism of exhibitions in Toronto and beyond with an explicit political reading.

name: Radical Philosophy
format: Journal issues, essays, reviews, interviews, open archive
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Collective run and open access, with a full archive from 1972
integrity_note: Run by an unpaid editorial collective of academics with no publisher or owner; open access and supported by donations, it is explicitly socialist and feminist.
description: Radical Philosophy is a British journal of socialist and feminist philosophy founded in 1972, run by an editorial collective and published open access since its 2018 relaunch. Use its articles and complete free archive for critical theory, continental philosophy and theoretically serious writing on borders, labour, technology and ecology.
what_makes_it_distinct: Over fifty years of socialist and feminist philosophy, with the whole archive free to read online.

name: The Hedgehog Review
owner: Institute for Advanced Studies in Culture, University of Virginia
format: Essays, reviews, web features, print issues
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Humanistic ideas journal outside the usual left and right magazines
integrity_note: Published by a University of Virginia research institute that says it rejects politicised scholarship; the institute does not detail its donors in the pages reviewed.
description: The Hedgehog Review is a journal of essays and criticism published three times a year by the Institute for Advanced Studies in Culture at the University of Virginia. Each issue takes up a theme in contemporary cultural change, such as higher education, technology, work or meaning.
what_makes_it_distinct: Slow, humanistic essays on technology, moral life and institutions, written by scholars for general readers rather than for a political camp.

name: Philosophie magazine
format: Monthly magazine, essays, interviews, web articles, newsletter
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: French philosophy for general readers from an independent publisher
integrity_note: Published by the independent company Philo Éditions and financed by sales, subscriptions and advertising; its accounts and shareholders could not be confirmed.
description: Philosophie magazine is a French monthly founded in 2006 that brings philosophy to a general readership through essays, interviews with philosophers, dossiers on current questions and book reviews. Its website adds shorter pieces that read the news through philosophical ideas.
what_makes_it_distinct: It gives the reader accessible French language philosophy tied to current events, from an independent publisher rather than a large press group.

name: Public Books
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / History
modifier_reason: Academic nonprofit; some overlap with other review magazines
integrity_note: A nonprofit magazine run by academics and supported by universities, foundations and donors; contributors are scholars, and the outlook is progressive.
description: Public Books is a nonprofit online magazine founded in 2012 by scholars Sharon Marcus and Caitlin Zaloom, in which academics write review essays on books, technology, cities and culture for general readers. Read it for accessible entry points into current humanities and social science debates.
what_makes_it_distinct: Academic specialists reviewing new books and ideas in plain language, edited to magazine standards.

name: The Logic
owner: The Logic Inc. (founder David Skok; Postmedia Network holds a minority stake taken in 2019; other investors Unconfirmed)
topics: Technology and AI / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Strong on Canadian technology, but paywalled and business focused
integrity_note: Privately held and led by founder David Skok, it lives mainly on subscriptions, limiting advertiser influence; Postmedia took a minority stake in 2019 and other investors are unconfirmed.
description: The Logic is a subscription newsroom founded in 2018 by David Skok that reports on Canadian business, technology and the innovation economy. It covers artificial intelligence, startups, large technology firms, industrial policy and federal and provincial economic decisions.
what_makes_it_distinct: It reports closely on Canadian AI policy and the technology sector with original reporting rather than aggregation.

name: The Republic
format: Essays, long reads, interviews, print issues
topics: Politics and Policy / History / Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: West African essays and criticism, an ownership and regional gap
integrity_note: Founder led independent journal supported partly by subscriptions; its ownership and any grant funding are not confirmed.
description: The Republic is a Lagos based journal founded by Wale Lawal that publishes essays, criticism, interviews and long reads on Nigerian and African politics, history, economy and culture. It appears online and in themed print issues, supported in part by subscriptions.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Nigerian edited magazine of ideas where African scholars and writers set the terms of debate on history and political economy.

name: AI Now Institute
topics: Technology and AI / Politics and Policy / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Critical AI policy voice; advocacy stance, overlaps with Data & Society
integrity_note: Funded by foundations and refuses corporate money, including from technology firms; it is an advocacy institute that argues openly against the current industry trajectory.
description: The AI Now Institute is a policy research institute founded in 2017 that studies the social consequences of artificial intelligence and the industry behind it. It publishes reports, policy toolkits and testimony on market concentration, labour, security and data centre expansion.
what_makes_it_distinct: A critical counterweight to industry narratives on artificial intelligence, with work on labour, data centres and concentration of power.

name: Asia Sentinel
regions: Southeast Asia / Taiwan and Greater China / South Asia
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Independent Southeast Asia analysis, including Malaysia and Singapore
integrity_note: Owned by its veteran editors and funded by Substack subscribers, with no corporate owner; it was blocked in Singapore in 2023 over a correction order.
description: Asia Sentinel is an independent news and analysis site founded in Hong Kong in 2006 by veteran correspondents including John Berthelsen and Philip Bowring, now funded by subscribers. Use it for informed commentary on Southeast Asian politics, business and corruption, especially Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and the Philippines.
what_makes_it_distinct: Veteran former regional editors writing independent analysis of Asian politics and business without a corporate owner.

name: Hyperallergic
region_label: United States and the global art world
topics: Visual Arts / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Independent founder owned arts newsroom with membership support
integrity_note: Owned by its two founders and paid for by memberships and art world advertising, so it covers institutions that also buy its advertising, from a progressive stance.
description: Hyperallergic is an independent online arts publication founded in Brooklyn in 2009 by Veken Gueyikian and Hrag Vartanian, supported by members and sponsors. Use it for daily art news, reviews and reporting on museum labour, restitution and cultural politics, mostly from a United States vantage.
what_makes_it_distinct: Treats museum labour disputes, restitution and protest as core art news.

name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
owner: International Energy Agency (autonomous body within the OECD framework)
topics: Energy / Climate and Environment / Data and Statistics / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Reference energy data, but an institutional voice of member states
integrity_note: Answers to its member governments, mostly wealthy energy importers, and has faced United States pressure over its scenarios; much detailed data is paywalled.
description: The International Energy Agency is a Paris based intergovernmental body created in 1974 within the OECD framework. It publishes the World Energy Outlook, market reports, country reviews and statistics on energy supply, demand, emissions, critical minerals and clean technology.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its statistics and scenarios are the baseline most governments use, so reading them directly helps the reader test claims about energy transition.

name: Africa Is a Country
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa / Global
topics: Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas / Music and Performing Arts / History
modifier_reason: African authored criticism under an open licence; grant funded
integrity_note: Founded by academic Sean Jacobs and supported by foundations including Open Society, it states plainly that it writes from an African left perspective.
description: Africa Is a Country is a site of opinion, analysis and criticism founded in 2009 by Sean Jacobs of The New School in New York, publishing African and diaspora writers under a Creative Commons licence. Use it for left perspectives on politics, labour, football, film and music that challenge Western media framing of the continent.
what_makes_it_distinct: African and diaspora writers contesting how the continent is framed, published under an open licence.

name: NHK World-Japan
languages: Multi / EN / FR / ZH-Hant / ZH-Hans / JA / ES / AR / RU

integrity_note: International arm of NHK, funded by receiving fees plus a government grant; the Broadcasting Act lets the government request coverage of specified matters, so the tone stays official.
description: NHK World-Japan is the international service of NHK, the Japanese public broadcaster, offering news, documentaries and radio in many languages. Use it for a reliable overview of Japanese and Asian affairs and disaster information, and pair its language lessons with Japanese reading practice.
what_makes_it_distinct: Japanese public broadcasting in many languages, with free Japanese lessons and strong disaster reporting.

name: Volume
topics: Architecture / Urban Planning / Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Architecture beyond building; nonprofit foundation publisher
integrity_note: Published by the nonprofit Archis Foundation, since 2023 jointly with the publicly funded Nieuwe Instituut; an experimental, critical stance guides themes and contributors.
description: Volume is an English language magazine published by the Archis Foundation in Amsterdam, launched in 2005 with AMO and Columbia University's C-Lab as a project to go beyond architecture's usual limits. Use its themed issues for essays on the politics, economics and territories that shape the built environment.
what_makes_it_distinct: A themed magazine that treats architecture as a tool for analysing politics and territory, not only buildings.

name: CABAR.asia

topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Central Asia is underserved; nonprofit platform for local analysts
integrity_note: A project of the Institute for War and Peace Reporting paid for by Western government and foundation donors; authors are local analysts working under restrictive regimes.
description: The Central Asian Bureau for Analytical Reporting is a platform run by the Institute for War and Peace Reporting, publishing analysis by local journalists and researchers in English, Russian and Central Asian languages. Use it for policy analysis on Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and Uzbekistan written from inside the region.
what_makes_it_distinct: Analysis of all five Central Asian states written mainly by local authors trained through its own media school.

name: Le Nouvelliste (Haïti)
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Economy and Finance / Humanitarian Affairs
modifier_reason: The Haitian paper of record in French; essential humanitarian context
integrity_note: Owned by the Chauvet family since the early twentieth century and financed by advertising in a very small market; its tone is cautious and institutional.
description: Le Nouvelliste is the oldest daily newspaper in Haiti, founded in Port-au-Prince in 1898 and long owned by the Chauvet family. It covers government, security, the economy, justice, culture and sport, and serves as the national newspaper of record in French.
what_makes_it_distinct: The daily record of Haitian institutions, security deployments and public finances in French, essential background for humanitarian planning in the Caribbean.

name: The Diplomat
regions: Taiwan and Greater China / Japan and Korea / Southeast Asia / South Asia / Russia and Central Asia
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Regular Central Asia coverage fills an underserved geography
integrity_note: A small privately owned magazine funded by subscriptions and advertising; it relies on outside contributors with their own affiliations, so quality and angle vary by author.
description: The Diplomat is an online current affairs magazine on the Asia Pacific, published by Diplomat Media Inc. and written largely by regional scholars, journalists and analysts. Use it for regular analysis of Taiwan, China, Japan, Southeast Asia and Central Asia, checking individual authors since quality varies by contributor.
what_makes_it_distinct: One magazine covering all of the reader's Asian priorities, including a standing Central Asia section.

name: Inter Press Service (IPS)
regions: Global / Sub-Saharan Africa / Latin America and Brazil
owner: IPS Inter Press Service International Association
topics: Development / International Affairs / Humanitarian Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Nonprofit cooperative wire with Global South correspondents
integrity_note: Nonprofit agency that depends on project grants from United Nations bodies, governments and foundations, so its coverage of the development agenda is sympathetic more than adversarial.
description: Inter Press Service is a nonprofit international news agency founded in 1964 and headquartered in Rome, organized as a cooperative of journalists reporting on development, the United Nations, civil society and the Global South. Use it for UN and SDG coverage written by correspondents in Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean.
what_makes_it_distinct: A wire service built around development and civil society, staffed largely by journalists from the countries they cover.

name: New Bloom Magazine (破土)
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Volunteer collective; Taiwanese left view absent from larger outlets
integrity_note: A volunteer collective born from the Sunflower Movement that writes from a declared left and pro social movement position.
description: New Bloom is an online magazine founded in Taipei in 2014 by activists and writers after the Sunflower Movement, published in English and Traditional Chinese under founding editor Brian Hioe. Use it for left perspectives on Taiwanese politics, labour disputes, social movements and cross strait relations.
what_makes_it_distinct: A volunteer run bilingual magazine giving a Taiwanese left and social movement reading of events in English and Traditional Chinese.

name: Reliefs
topics: Geography and Mapping / Science / History / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Fills a French geography and exploration gap; independent publisher
integrity_note: Published by a small independent French press and sold by the issue, with no known outside owner; a curated literary and scientific revue, not a news source.
description: Reliefs is a French revue from Reliefs Éditions devoted to explorers past and present, now published as an annual collection of themed issues such as Soleils that weave geography, natural science, history, literature, maps and photography. Read each issue slowly as a French companion to site studies and to the geographic imagination behind fieldwork.
what_makes_it_distinct: Treats exploration as a meeting point of geography, science, literature and image, one territory or element per issue.

name: Global Facility for Disaster Reduction and Recovery (GFDRR)
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Development / Economy and Finance / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Overlaps with the World Bank entry but adds hazard data
integrity_note: A trust fund administered by the World Bank and paid for by donor governments; its publications are rigorous but promote the Bank's own approach to disaster risk finance.
description: GFDRR is a World Bank partnership that funds and studies disaster risk management in low and middle income countries, publishing reports, open risk data initiatives and tools such as ThinkHazard. Use it for risk financing, resilient infrastructure and open hazard data perspectives.
what_makes_it_distinct: Pairs disaster risk research with open data tools built for planners in developing countries.

name: Intact Centre on Climate Adaptation
topics: Climate and Environment / Hazards and Disaster Risk / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Fills the Canadian flood resilience gap
integrity_note: A University of Waterloo institute founded and funded by Intact Financial, Canada's largest property insurer, whose commercial interest in reducing losses aligns with the centre's research agenda.
description: The Intact Centre at the University of Waterloo produces applied research and practical guidance on reducing flood, wildfire and heat risk for Canadian homes, communities and infrastructure, often feeding national standards. Read it as Canadian adaptation evidence, noting its founding funding from an insurer.
what_makes_it_distinct: Turns Canadian flood and heat risk research into checklists and standards for homeowners and municipalities.

name: Public Understanding of Science
topics: Science / Media and Information Integrity / Technology and AI
integrity_note: Published by the commercial house Sage with an independent academic editorial board and peer review; most articles sit behind institutional subscription.
description: Public Understanding of Science is a peer reviewed journal published by SAGE since 1992 on how publics, media and institutions engage with science and technology. Use it for research on science communication, trust in expertise, risk perception and public attitudes toward emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence.
what_makes_it_distinct: A scholarly journal devoted entirely to how science is communicated, perceived and contested in public.

name: Lapham's Quarterly
owner: American Agora Foundation (reported move to Bard College unverified)
format: Thematic quarterly, source excerpts, essays, podcast
topics: History / Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Unique format, but publication may be paused
integrity_note: Published by a small nonprofit foundation built around its late founder Lewis Lapham; print appears paused and the reported move to Bard College is unconfirmed.
description: Lapham's Quarterly is a magazine of history and ideas founded in 2007 by Lewis Lapham, with each issue assembling historical texts and new essays around one theme. Use its archive for primary source readings across centuries, and confirm its publishing status, which could not be verified here.
what_makes_it_distinct: Each issue reads one theme through excerpts from several thousand years of writing.

name: The Christian Science Monitor
owner: The First Church of Christ, Scientist
format: Daily digital edition, weekly magazine, articles, newsletters, podcasts
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Distinct ownership and tone, but general news overlaps other anchors
integrity_note: Owned and partly funded by the Christian Science church, whose board appoints the editor; its news pages are secular and known for restraint.
description: The Christian Science Monitor is a Boston news organisation founded in 1908 by Mary Baker Eddy and owned by her church. It publishes a daily digital edition and a magazine with reporting from correspondents in the United States and abroad, aiming to inform rather than persuade.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its international reporting looks for causes and constructive responses rather than conflict alone, a tone close to humanitarian practice.

name: The Dance Current
owner: Dance Media Group / Groupe Danse Média
format: Profiles, reviews, features, commentary, event listings
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: National dance coverage; a narrow field for this reader
integrity_note: A registered charity funded by arts grants, subscriptions and donations; it writes from within the dance community and its latest posted annual report dates from 2020.
description: The Dance Current is a Canadian dance magazine founded in Toronto in 1998 and published by Dance Media Group, a charitable nonprofit. It runs four print issues a year plus online news, performance reviews, artist profiles, commentary by practitioners and free event listings from across the country.
what_makes_it_distinct: It covers dance across Canada in many forms and communities, including commentary by practitioners, well beyond the large ballet companies.

name: Les Jours
owner: Les Jours SAS (founding journalists hold the majority)
format: Serial investigations, long form reporting, podcasts
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Distinct serial format, but limited overlap with the reader's specialist fields
integrity_note: Financed by subscribers with no advertising and controlled by its founding journalists, with minority outside investors; the tone is left leaning and narrative.
description: Les Jours is a French subscription news site created in 2016 by former Libération journalists, which follows current affairs through long running series it calls obsessions. Recent series cover the budget, the far right, private Catholic schooling and United States politics.
what_makes_it_distinct: The serial format lets the reader follow one French political or social story in depth over months rather than through scattered daily items.

name: Actu Philosophia
owner: Actu Philosophia (founded by Thibaut Gress; edited by Romain Debluë)
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: French language philosophy criticism is thin elsewhere in the portfolio
integrity_note: A volunteer review with no owner or advertiser behind it, though the books it reviews arrive as free press copies from publishers.
description: A French online review of philosophy publishing, run by a volunteer team of academics and teachers, founded by Thibaut Gress and edited by Romain Debluë, with long critical reviews and author interviews. Use it to follow new French language philosophy books across traditions, from the history of philosophy to phenomenology and analytic work.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long French reviews of new philosophy titles written by specialists, with extended author interviews, all free to read.

name: Commentaire
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / International Affairs / History
modifier_reason: Credible centre right liberal voice adds viewpoint diversity in French
integrity_note: An independent quarterly published by its own company with a declared mission to defend liberal principles; its shareholders and funding could not be confirmed.
description: Commentaire is a French quarterly review founded in 1978 around Raymond Aron, covering politics, international affairs, economics, history, literature and the arts. It publishes long essays and book criticism and states that it defends the principles of liberal societies.
what_makes_it_distinct: It offers a serious liberal, centre right French perspective in the tradition of Raymond Aron, with essays by academics and senior officials.

name: Journal of Urban Technology
topics: Urban Planning / Technology and AI / Geography and Mapping
integrity_note: A peer reviewed journal published commercially by Routledge behind a paywall; editorial decisions rest with academic editors, not the publisher.
description: The Journal of Urban Technology is a peer reviewed journal published by Routledge, part of Taylor & Francis, on how digital and physical technologies shape cities, planning and urban governance. Use it for scholarly studies of smart cities, urban data and infrastructure, mostly through a library subscription.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running scholarly journal devoted specifically to technology in cities, including critical studies of smart city programs.

name: Los Angeles Review of Books (LARB)
format: Essays, reviews, interviews, quarterly print journal, podcast
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / History
integrity_note: Nonprofit review supported by members, donors and grants; contributors are mostly academics writing from a liberal humanities outlook, with wide latitude given to section editors.
description: A nonprofit review founded in 2011 by Tom Lutz in Los Angeles, publishing daily essays, interviews and criticism online alongside a quarterly print journal. Use it for long reviews of new work in philosophy, history, technology and the arts written by scholars for general readers, from a West Coast vantage.
what_makes_it_distinct: A member funded review built online first, giving academic authors long space outside the New York and London review circuit.

name: Quanta Magazine
topics: Science / Technology and AI
integrity_note: Paid for entirely by the Simons Foundation, a major funder of mathematics and basic science; the magazine is editorially independent and discloses that tie.

name: Liberté
