name: The Intercept
topics: Investigations / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice / Technology and AI
integrity_note: An independent nonprofit since separating from Pierre Omidyar's First Look in 2023, now reliant on donations and openly adversarial in stance.
description: The Intercept is a New York based investigative newsroom founded in 2014 with backing from Pierre Omidyar and run since 2023 as an independent nonprofit. Use it for document based reporting on surveillance, war, policing and technology companies, keeping in mind its openly adversarial stance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Built on the Snowden archive, it still specializes in leaked documents about surveillance and national security.

name: The Jakarta Post
owner: The Jakarta Post Group (publishing company PT Niskala Media Tenggara, formerly PT Bina Media Tenggara)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Indonesian national perspective on a hazard prone archipelago
integrity_note: Commercial daily founded in 1983 by a consortium of Indonesian media groups; its editorials are independent in tone but ownership ties to business and political elites remain.
description: The Jakarta Post is Indonesia's main English language daily, founded in 1983 and published in Jakarta. It covers national politics, the provinces of the archipelago, business, regional affairs and culture, with a substantial editorial and opinion section.
what_makes_it_distinct: Daily English coverage of Indonesian eruptions, floods, decentralisation and urban policy across an archipelago that is central to disaster risk work.

name: The Observer (Tortoise Media)
topics: Politics and Policy / Investigations / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Now folded into The Observer; overlaps United Kingdom anchors
integrity_note: Backed by private investors and corporate partners, it bought The Observer in 2025 and now publishes mainly under that title, with the Scott Trust holding a minority stake.
description: The Observer, Britain's oldest Sunday newspaper, has been published since 2025 by Tortoise Media, a London company founded in 2019 by James Harding and Matthew Barzun around slow news, investigative podcasts and data indices. Use it for long investigations, narrative podcasts and cultural coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: A slow news company built on narrative podcasts that now publishes Britain's oldest Sunday newspaper.

name: Vlast
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Underserved geography and an independent Kazakh voice
integrity_note: Privately held independent outlet working in a restricted press environment; its ownership and revenue split are not confirmed.
description: Vlast is an Almaty based online magazine founded in 2012 that covers politics, the economy, cities and society in Kazakhstan. It combines a daily news feed with analysis and reportage from the regions, mainly in Russian.
what_makes_it_distinct: Carries regional reportage and Almaty urban and air quality coverage that is rare in sources about Central Asia.

name: Sustainable Development Goal 8 (UN DESA)
owner: United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)
topics: Labour and Work / Development / Economy and Finance / Data and Statistics
modifier_reason: Primary SDG 8 reference, partly redundant with ILO and UN entries
integrity_note: An official page of a UN department accountable to member states; indicator data follow agreed methods but depend on national reporting and carry the institution's framing.
description: This is the Goal 8 page of the sustainable development site run by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs, gathering targets, indicators, yearly progress summaries and related reports on decent work and economic growth. Use it as the primary reference when checking labour claims against agreed indicators.
what_makes_it_distinct: The official record of targets, indicators and annual progress for the decent work goal.

name: Yonhap News Agency
languages: EN / KO / JA / ZH-Hans / ES / FR / AR
owner: Yonhap News Agency (largest shareholder: Korea News Agency Commission)
format: Wire reports, photos, video, multilingual editions
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Useful wire, but close to the state's framing
integrity_note: Designated the national news agency by law, it receives government subscription money and its president is chosen through a commission that includes political appointees.
description: Yonhap is South Korea's national news agency, supplying real time reports to newspapers, broadcasters, government bodies, businesses and portals, with correspondents in major cities abroad. Its free English service covers relations between the two Koreas, politics, the economy, industry and culture, beside editions in Chinese, Japanese, Arabic, Spanish and French.
what_makes_it_distinct: A fast multilingual wire on the Korean peninsula, with French, Spanish, Japanese and Chinese editions that double as parallel reading practice.

name: Raseef22 (رصيف22)
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Independent Arab voices including North Africa; ownership diversity
integrity_note: Founded and published by Lebanese businessman Kareem Sakka, with grant support and a membership scheme; editorially progressive and blocked by several Arab governments.
description: Raseef22 is an independent Arabic digital outlet founded in Beirut in 2013, publishing reporting, essays and opinion on politics, rights, gender, culture and daily life across the 22 Arab states. Use its English section for voices from North Africa and the Levant that state aligned media exclude.
what_makes_it_distinct: An independent platform for the whole Arab world, named for the 22 Arab states and blocked in several of them.

name: The Art Newspaper
format: Monthly newspaper, daily web news, podcasts
topics: Visual Arts / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Owned since 2023 by the Hong Kong finance group AMTD, through a media arm that also holds fashion titles; editorial independence is asserted but rests on that owner.
description: The Art Newspaper is an international publication on the visual arts founded in 1990, edited in London and New York, and owned since 2023 by AMTD Group. Use it for news on museums, the art market, heritage and cultural policy, with sister editions in French, Italian and other languages.
what_makes_it_distinct: Covers the art world as a news beat, including its annual survey of museum attendance.

name: Geographical
owner: Syon Geographical Ltd, under licence from the Royal Geographical Society (with IBG)
topics: Geography and Mapping / Climate and Environment / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Popular geography is thin elsewhere in the portfolio
integrity_note: Published commercially by Syon Geographical under licence from the Royal Geographical Society; it depends on subscriptions and advertising, and carries the Society's name without being its journal.
description: Geographical is the monthly magazine of the Royal Geographical Society (with IBG), founded in 1935 and published under licence by Syon Geographical in London. Use it for accessible features on environment, geopolitics, exploration and places, treating it as popular geography with occasional map stories, not as a cartography journal.
what_makes_it_distinct: The general readership monthly of a national geographical society, bridging academic geography and travel writing.

name: UN News
languages: Multi / EN / FR / ZH-Hans / ES / AR / RU / PT
owner: United Nations Department of Global Communications
format: News, audio, video, interviews, daily newsletter
topics: International Affairs / Humanitarian Affairs / Development / Human Rights and Justice
integrity_note: Produced by the UN Secretariat's communications department and answerable to member states, so it records official positions accurately but does not scrutinise the organisation.
description: UN News is the official news service of the United Nations, produced by the Department of Global Communications in the six official languages and several others, including Portuguese, Kiswahili and Hindi. Use it as a primary record of what UN bodies and officials said and decided, then turn to independent reporting for scrutiny.
what_makes_it_distinct: The UN's own daily record, published in parallel in all six official languages and several others.

name: Equal Times
region_label: Global, with a Global South focus
topics: Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice / Migration / Development
modifier_reason: Fills the labour and SDG 8 gap; union funded model
integrity_note: Created and funded by the International Trade Union Confederation, so it spoke for the labour movement; the site itself says publication ended in December 2025.
description: Equal Times was a news and opinion site in English, French and Spanish supported by the International Trade Union Confederation and based in Brussels, published from 2012 to December 2025. Use its archive for reported features on work, migration, inequality and just transition, written largely by freelance journalists across the Global South.
what_makes_it_distinct: Global labour reporting commissioned from local freelancers and published in three parallel languages.

name: Citizen News (眾新聞)
owner: Citizen News (founded by veteran Hong Kong journalists)
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Believed closed since 2022; archive availability unconfirmed
integrity_note: Founded and funded by journalists and readers, it closed itself in January 2022 citing staff safety under Hong Kong's national security climate.
description: A Hong Kong news site founded in 2017 by veteran journalists and funded by readers, which stopped publishing in January 2022, days after the closure of Stand News. Its address now shows only a farewell message, so treat it as a historical marker of reader funded Hong Kong journalism.
what_makes_it_distinct: A record of reader funded Hong Kong journalism from the years just before and after the national security law.

name: France 24 Español
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Language Learning
modifier_reason: Overlaps France 24 in French and BBC News Mundo
integrity_note: Owned by France Médias Monde and funded by the French state; editorial independence is set in law but the outlook reflects French public diplomacy priorities.
description: France 24 Español is the Spanish language channel and website of the French state funded broadcaster France Médias Monde, launched in September 2017 with a newsroom in Bogotá. Use it for free rolling news in Spanish with a European and Latin American outlook, as language practice alongside BBC News Mundo.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French public international channel with a Bogotá newsroom, giving Latin American news a European frame.

name: Niskanen Center
topics: Politics and Policy / Migration / Climate and Environment / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Heterodox moderate voice, but narrowly focused on United States policy
integrity_note: Donor funded nonprofit that both researches and lobbies for its own policies; it publishes annual reports and a current list of funders.
description: The Niskanen Center is a Washington think tank founded in 2014 that combines policy research with direct advocacy to lawmakers. It publishes studies, commentary, testimony and podcasts on immigration, climate and energy, housing, healthcare, social policy and state capacity in the United States.
what_makes_it_distinct: A heterodox moderate voice on state capacity, permitting and infrastructure delivery, questions that bear on planning and climate adaptation.

name: Scientific American
topics: Science / Health / Climate and Environment / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Prestige title overlapping stronger science sources
integrity_note: Owned by Springer Nature, a commercial publisher; reporting is sound, but its opinion pages and presidential endorsements in 2020 and 2024 drew criticism for partisanship.
description: Scientific American is a popular science magazine published since 1845 and owned by Springer Nature, with daily online news and a regular print edition. Use it for accessible explanations of research in climate, artificial intelligence, health and physics, checking important claims against the original papers.
what_makes_it_distinct: The oldest continuously published magazine in the United States, with working scientists among its regular authors.

name: n+1
format: Print issues, online essays, fiction, reviews, books
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Published by the nonprofit n+1 Foundation and sustained by subscribers, donors and grants; its editors write from an openly left literary position.
description: n+1 is a Brooklyn magazine of literature, culture and politics founded in 2004 by Keith Gessen, Mark Greif, Benjamin Kunkel, Marco Roth and others, published three times a year by the nonprofit n+1 Foundation. Use it for long essays, fiction and criticism that connect intellectual life with left politics and everyday experience.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long unsigned editorials under the heading The Intellectual Situation, diagnosing the cultural moment in a collective voice.

name: Foreign Policy
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Overlaps Foreign Affairs and other geopolitics titles; prestige brand
integrity_note: Owned by Graham Holdings, it earns from subscriptions, advertising and sponsored events and research for governments and companies, so commercial partnerships sit close to its analysis.
description: Foreign Policy is a Washington based magazine of global affairs founded in 1970 and owned by Graham Holdings. Use it for daily analysis and argument on diplomacy, security and the world economy, with regional briefings by newsletter, while filtering its more provocative opinion headlines.
what_makes_it_distinct: Weekly regional newsletters such as China Brief and Africa Brief, each written by a named specialist.

name: Log
region_label: Global architecture discourse, New York base
topics: Architecture / Philosophy and Ideas / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: Architecture theory gap; nonprofit print journal
integrity_note: Published by the nonprofit Anyone Corporation, whose board and benefactors include architect Peter Eisenman, husband of editor Cynthia Davidson; a small circle shapes its outlook.
description: Log is an independent print journal of architecture and the contemporary city, founded in 2003 and published three times a year by the Anyone Corporation in New York under editor Cynthia Davidson. Use it for essays and criticism on architectural theory and practice that are not available online.
what_makes_it_distinct: A print journal of architectural criticism that deliberately favours text over images.

name: The New York Review of Books
format: Review essays, twenty print issues a year, online pieces
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / History
modifier_reason: Prestige review; overlaps other Anglo American literary reviews
integrity_note: Privately owned by publisher Rea Hederman since 1984, with a long record of editorial autonomy; essays argue from a liberal intellectual standpoint and are not news reporting.
description: The New York Review of Books is a privately owned literary and political review founded in 1963, publishing twenty issues a year of long essays on books, history, politics, science and art. Use it for considered essay length argument and its deep archive, not for news.
what_makes_it_distinct: Review essays long enough to become standalone arguments, with a continuous archive back to 1963.

name: Addis Standard
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Humanitarian Affairs / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Scarce domestic reporting from Ethiopia under pressure
integrity_note: Privately owned outlet that has faced suspension, raids and staff detentions by Ethiopian authorities, which limits what it can safely report.
description: Addis Standard is an Ethiopian English language news publication founded in 2011 and published by Jakenn Publishing. It reports and analyses federal and regional politics, armed conflict, humanitarian conditions, the economy and rights, with additional editions in Ethiopian languages.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the few independent domestic sources on conflict, displacement and humanitarian access in the regions of Ethiopia.

name: Agencia EFE
regions: Europe / Latin America and Brazil / Global
owner: Agencia EFE (owned by the Spanish state through SEPI)
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Adds a Hispanophone wire beside the three global agencies
integrity_note: Owned by the Spanish state through SEPI, with a president appointed by the government; wire copy is sober, but coverage of Spanish politics deserves a second source.
description: Spain's national news agency, founded in 1939, based in Madrid and owned by the state holding company SEPI, with a large Spanish language correspondent network in Latin America. Use it for plain wire Spanish suited to a B1 reader and for Latin American coverage beyond what Reuters and AFP carry.
what_makes_it_distinct: The main Spanish language wire, with bureaus across Latin America and clear agency prose useful for language practice.

name: The New Atlantis
owner: Center for the Study of Technology and Society
topics: Technology and AI / Philosophy and Ideas / Science
modifier_reason: Nonprofit; adds a perspective on technology absent elsewhere in the list
integrity_note: Published by a small nonprofit sustained by donors and subscriptions, with roots in conservative policy circles; it argues from a declared conservative humanist position.
description: The New Atlantis is a quarterly journal of technology and society founded in 2003 and published in Washington by the nonprofit Center for the Study of Technology and Society. Use it for long essays on bioethics, AI, science policy and the philosophy of technology, written from a conservative humanist position unlike most technology criticism.
what_makes_it_distinct: A conservative humanist journal of technology criticism, useful as a counterweight to left and industry perspectives.

name: Institut Montaigne
owner: Institut Montaigne (association under the French law of 1901)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: French right of centre policy voice widens the reader's range of views
integrity_note: Financed by member companies with no public subsidy, so its positions tend to track the interests of large French business.
description: Institut Montaigne is a Paris think tank founded in 2000 by Claude Bébéar, former head of the insurer AXA. It publishes reports, notes and commentary in French and English on French and European public policy, the economy, security, technology, health and education.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French language window on right of centre and business thinking about public policy, useful as a counterweight to the reader's other French sources.

name: Multitudes
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / Visual Arts / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: French language theory from a collective; philosophy gap
integrity_note: Run by an association and editorial collective and sold by subscription, it speaks from one post autonomist intellectual tradition.
description: Multitudes is a French quarterly review of politics, philosophy and art founded in 2000 by Yann Moulier-Boutang and run by an editorial collective. Use it for themed dossiers on cognitive capitalism, ecology, digital culture and the commons, read as argument from one intellectual tradition.
what_makes_it_distinct: A French theory quarterly that pairs political philosophy with commissioned artworks in each issue.

name: ARTouch (典藏)
owner: Art and Collection Group (典藏藝術家庭)
format: Art news, criticism, market reports, podcast, online viewing rooms
topics: Visual Arts / History / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Traditional Chinese art criticism with heritage and city themes
integrity_note: Owned by a commercial art publishing group that depends on galleries, auction houses and art fairs as advertisers, so market coverage sits close to its revenue.
description: ARTouch is the online platform of Taiwan's Art and Collection Group, a publisher of art magazines for more than twenty years. It combines art news, criticism, market and industry coverage, commentary on cultural policy and heritage, a podcast and online exhibition rooms, with a section for children.
what_makes_it_distinct: Substantive Traditional Chinese criticism on Taiwanese art history, cultural policy, heritage conservation and the city as a visual environment, beyond market news.

name: Al Jazeera English
regions: Global / Middle East and North Africa
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Non Western network with bureaus across Africa and the Middle East
integrity_note: Funded by the state of Qatar through Al Jazeera Media Network; Global South field reporting is strong, but coverage of Qatar and its Gulf rivals follows state interests.
description: Al Jazeera English is the English language news channel and website of the Al Jazeera Media Network, based in Doha and funded by the state of Qatar. Use it for field reporting from the Middle East, Africa and Asia, and read its Gulf coverage knowing who pays for it.
what_makes_it_distinct: A large correspondent network headquartered in the Global South, framing world news from outside the Atlantic capitals.

name: African Climate Foundation
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: Climate and Environment / Development / Energy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: African led climate policy voice; nonprofit foundation
integrity_note: A grant maker that redistributes money from large international climate philanthropies, so its publications advance an African climate and development agenda and are advocacy, not journalism.
description: The African Climate Foundation is an African led grant maker and policy organisation based in Cape Town, working where climate action meets development, energy, trade and finance. Use its newsletter and reports for African perspectives on adaptation finance, energy transitions and industrial policy across the continent.
what_makes_it_distinct: The first African led strategic climate philanthropy, publishing policy research from within the continent.

name: DeSmog
regions: Global / United States / Canada and Quebec / Europe
region_label: North America, United Kingdom and Europe
topics: Climate and Environment / Media and Information Integrity / Investigations / Energy
modifier_reason: Unique actor databases; overlaps partly with climate nonprofits
integrity_note: Founded by a public relations executive to counter climate denial and funded by donors and foundations; accurate on documents, but it investigates only one side of the debate.
description: DeSmog is an investigative outlet founded in Vancouver in 2006 that tracks climate disinformation, fossil fuel lobbying and the public relations networks behind them. Use its reporting and searchable databases to check who funds and repeats a claim before you rely on it.
what_makes_it_distinct: Maintains searchable databases profiling the people and organizations that spread climate disinformation.

name: Landscape Architecture Magazine
format: Monthly magazine, features, criticism, project reviews
topics: Landscape Architecture / Urban Planning / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Fills the landscape architecture gap named in the brief
integrity_note: Published by the American Society of Landscape Architects as a member benefit and carries supplier advertising, so it reflects the profession's view of itself.
description: Landscape Architecture Magazine is the monthly magazine of the American Society of Landscape Architects, published since 1910 and covering built projects, planning, ecology and professional practice. Use it to follow how the profession responds to flooding, heat, coastal retreat and public space, mostly through North American cases.
what_makes_it_distinct: The magazine of record for landscape architecture practice in North America, published by the profession's own society since 1910.

name: Disaster Management in Japan, Cabinet Office (内閣府防災情報)
format: White papers, damage reports, guidelines, council papers, press releases
topics: Hazards and Disaster Risk / Politics and Policy / Law
modifier_reason: Primary policy documents for a reference disaster governance system
integrity_note: This is the central government's own voice on disaster policy: reliable on facts, figures and legal measures, but it does not critique its own response.
description: The disaster management pages of Japan's Cabinet Office publish national disaster policy, damage situation reports, notices applying the Disaster Relief Act, council papers and the annual White Paper on Disaster Management. Most material is in Japanese, with an English section that summarises the national system.
what_makes_it_distinct: Shows how a national government documents each disaster and structures relief law, evacuation guidance and preparedness, in Japanese that matches the reader's professional vocabulary.

name: NewMusicBox
format: Essays, interviews, audio and video profiles
topics: Music and Performing Arts / History
integrity_note: The house magazine of New Music USA, a grant making and advocacy nonprofit funded by foundations and donors, so it promotes the field it covers.
description: NewMusicBox is the online magazine of the nonprofit New Music USA, launched in 1999, with composer interviews and essays written largely by working musicians. Use its archive for first person writing on contemporary composition and sound practice in the United States; whether it still commissions new articles could not be confirmed.
what_makes_it_distinct: Decades of long conversations with American composers, written and recorded by practitioners.

name: RTVE Noticias
owner: Corporación de Radio y Televisión Española (Spanish state)
format: News, live television and radio, video, podcasts, fact checks
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Useful Spanish listening practice; general news adds little distinct perspective
integrity_note: A state owned public corporation financed by the state budget and levies, whose board is chosen by parliament; its newsroom councils have repeatedly denounced political pressure.
description: RTVE Noticias is the news service of Spain's national public radio and television corporation, offering continuous text, video and audio coverage of Spain and the world. It includes weather alerts, regional news, a verification unit and live broadcasts of its channels.
what_makes_it_distinct: Free video and radio news in clear standard Spanish makes it practical listening practice, alongside coverage of Spanish storms and floods.

name: boundary 2
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas
integrity_note: Published by Duke University Press and run by an editorial collective that commissions much of its content, within a critical theory tradition.
description: boundary 2 is a quarterly journal of literature and culture founded in 1972 and published by Duke University Press, with a strong tradition in critical theory and postcolonial thought. Consult it selectively for demanding theoretical essays, and see its open online companion b2o for shorter reviews.
what_makes_it_distinct: A journal that helped define postmodern literary theory and still publishes long theoretical interventions.

name: Ukrainska Pravda
topics: Conflict and Security / Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Investigations
modifier_reason: English edition is mostly short items; overlaps with Kyiv Independent
integrity_note: Owned since 2021 by investment banker Tomáš Fiala of Dragon Capital under an editorial independence pledge; it has publicly reported pressure from the presidential office.
description: Ukrainska Pravda is a Ukrainian online newspaper founded in 2000 by Georgiy Gongadze, publishing rolling news, investigations, interviews and columns on politics, the economy and the war. Its English edition carries translated news items and selected long articles.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the domestic newspaper Ukrainians themselves read, so its English and Russian editions show the country's internal political debate.

name: Semafor
regions: Global / United States / Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Venture funded generalist; mostly overlaps the larger outlets
integrity_note: A venture backed company that relies on sponsorship and live events with corporate partners; its story format separates reported facts from the reporter's view.
description: Global news company founded in 2022 by Ben Smith and Justin Smith, publishing newsletters and articles that separate reported facts from the reporter's view. Use its Africa, Gulf, technology and business newsletters as a quick briefing layer, not as a source of depth.
what_makes_it_distinct: A story format that labels news, analysis and opposing views as separate sections.

name: The East African
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Regional East African view absent from larger outlets
integrity_note: Published by Nation Media Group, a listed company whose largest shareholder is the Aga Khan Fund for Economic Development, in markets where governments press advertisers and editors.
description: The East African is a weekly regional newspaper published in Nairobi by Nation Media Group, covering Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda and their neighbours. Use it for politics, trade and integration in the East African Community and for regional views of the Horn and the Great Lakes.
what_makes_it_distinct: A newspaper edited for the East African Community as one region.

name: I Care If You Listen
format: Concert and album reviews, interviews, profiles, essays
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Fills a contemporary music gap and features marginalised composers
integrity_note: A programme of the American Composers Forum, a composer service organisation; called editorially independent, yet its editor is forum staff and follows the forum mission.
description: I Care If You Listen is an online publication about contemporary classical and experimental music by living composers, founded in 2010 by Thomas Deneuville and owned since 2020 by the American Composers Forum. It publishes concert and album reviews, interviews, profiles and guest essays.
what_makes_it_distinct: Covers living composers and new music scenes that general arts pages skip, with attention to artists outside the classical establishment.

name: Le Figaro
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Main French conservative daily; widens the range of French viewpoints
integrity_note: Owned by the Dassault family, whose aerospace and defence group has interests the paper covers; the editorial line is conservative and past owner interference is documented.
description: Le Figaro is a French national daily founded in 1826, with continuous online news on politics, international affairs, the economy and culture alongside prominent editorials and opinion pages. It is the principal conservative national newspaper in France.
what_makes_it_distinct: It shows the reader how the French right frames politics, security and the economy, in a daily written to a high professional standard.

name: The Syllabus
owner: The Syllabus (founder and publisher Evgeny Morozov)
topics: Technology and AI / Philosophy and Ideas / Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Founded and directed by the critic Evgeny Morozov and funded by subscribers and institutional clients, its selections reflect his critical view of technology.
description: The Syllabus is a curation project founded in 2019 by the technology critic Evgeny Morozov, which uses a mix of algorithms and human editors to select academic papers, essays, talks and podcasts from across the web. Use its themed weekly lists to find serious work on technology, political economy and culture that ranking feeds bury.
what_makes_it_distinct: Human and machine curation that ranks academic and long work by intellectual merit instead of popularity.

name: ArtReview
format: Criticism, reviews, art news, podcasts, print magazine
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Asia edition and Japanese site widen a field dominated by Western titles
integrity_note: Owned by China's Meta Media Group and reliant on art market advertising and brand partnerships, so coverage of galleries, fairs and Chinese topics deserves some caution.
description: ArtReview is a London contemporary art magazine founded in 1949, publishing criticism, reviews, art world news and artist projects in seven issues a year and online. Sister titles include ArtReview Asia, a quarterly Chinese edition and a Japanese language digital publication.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its Asia edition and its Chinese and Japanese language publications give the reader art criticism that looks well beyond London and New York.

name: E3G
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
integrity_note: A climate think tank funded by philanthropic foundations and governments, which it lists; its analysis is competent but consistently argues for faster climate action.
description: E3G, short for Third Generation Environmentalism, is an independent climate change think tank founded in 2004 with offices in London, Brussels, Berlin and Washington. Use its briefings and blog for the politics of UN climate talks, coal phase out, public finance reform and European energy security.
what_makes_it_distinct: Political economy reading of climate diplomacy, with frequent briefings around UN climate summits.

name: IranWire
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Media and Information Integrity
modifier_reason: Citizen reporting from inside Iran; opaque funding
integrity_note: A donor funded exile outlet with an opposition and human rights outlook; its funders are not confirmed.
description: IranWire is a news site founded in 2013 by journalist Maziar Bahari and run by Iranian journalists in the diaspora with citizen reporters inside Iran. It focuses on human rights, minorities, daily life and fact checking of official claims, in Persian, English and other languages.
what_makes_it_distinct: Pairs citizen journalists inside Iran with professional editors abroad, giving granular reporting on minorities, women and labour that larger outlets skip.

name: Lausan Collective (流傘)
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Human Rights and Justice / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Volunteer collective adds diversity; output believed slow or dormant
integrity_note: A volunteer collective with no owner or advertiser, writing from a declared decolonial left position, with some writers using pseudonyms for their safety.
description: A volunteer collective of writers, translators, artists and organizers from Hong Kong and its diaspora, formed during the 2019 protests and publishing in English and Chinese. Use its essays and translations for left perspectives on Hong Kong that criticize both Chinese state power and Western imperialism, and check how recently it has published.
what_makes_it_distinct: Translates Hong Kong left and labour writing between Chinese and English from an explicitly internationalist position.

name: Noema
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Technology and AI / International Affairs / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Published and funded by the Berggruen Institute, the think tank of investor Nicolas Berggruen, so one philanthropist's interests frame the magazine's agenda.
description: Noema is a magazine of ideas published by the Berggruen Institute in Los Angeles, with long essays and interviews on technology, philosophy, governance, climate and geopolitics. Read it selectively for planetary scale thinking about AI and political order, keeping in mind that one philanthropist's institute sets its agenda.
what_makes_it_distinct: Treats AI, planetary governance and comparative civilizational philosophy as one conversation, with contributors from well beyond the Anglosphere.

name: The Public Source
format: Investigations, long reads, visual essays, comics
topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Human Rights and Justice / Labour and Work
modifier_reason: Local Lebanese voices; openly partisan framing
integrity_note: Declares itself a magazine of the left writing in solidarity with Global South publics; its owner and funders are not confirmed.
description: The Public Source is a Beirut based online magazine that publishes accountability reporting, long essays, photo essays and comics from an openly left perspective. Its series follow Lebanon's economic collapse, war, displacement, labour and the privatisation of the coast and public domain, in English and Arabic.
what_makes_it_distinct: Covers infrastructure collapse, coastal privatisation, displacement and migrant labour in Lebanon through local writers, with strong visual storytelling.

name: Disconnect

description: Disconnect is a reader supported newsletter by Canadian technology critic Paris Marx, host of the podcast Tech Won't Save Us, offering essays on Silicon Valley, AI, platforms and digital sovereignty. Use it as a weekly critical counterweight to industry narratives, remembering that it is one author's argued position.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Canadian critic's newsletter arguing for digital sovereignty and public alternatives to United States technology firms.

name: IRIS (Institut de recherche et d'informations socioéconomiques)
owner: Institut de recherche et d'informations socioéconomiques (independent nonprofit)

description: IRIS is an independent nonprofit research institute founded in 2000 that analyses Quebec public policy and the economy from a declared progressive position. It publishes studies and short posts on public finances, health and education, housing, inequality, work and the ecological crisis.
what_makes_it_distinct: It offers French language analysis of housing, work and public services from the left, best read alongside IEDM and the Institut du Québec.

name: Les Affaires
format: Articles, print editions, newsletters, events, rankings
topics: Economy and Finance / Labour and Work / Politics and Policy

description: Les Affaires is Quebec's main French language business publication, founded in 1928 and owned since 2019 by Groupe Contex, a Montreal company led by Pierre Marcoux. Use it for Quebec companies, labour shortages, regional economies, real estate and industrial policy that national English business media rarely cover.
what_makes_it_distinct: Quebec's long standing French language business paper, covering small and medium enterprises and regional economies.

name: ArcticToday
topics: International Affairs / Climate and Environment / Conflict and Security / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Underserved Arctic geography; partly overlaps High North News
integrity_note: A small commercial site whose current ownership is not clearly disclosed; it mixes original reporting, syndicated partner stories and corporate announcements, so check each item's label.

Use it to follow Arctic shipping, security, resource development, climate change and Indigenous governance in one place.
what_makes_it_distinct: A single circumpolar news desk pooling reporting from Alaska, Canada, the Nordic countries, Greenland and Russia.

name: Caixin Global
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Rare reporting from inside China; privately run newsroom

what_makes_it_distinct: Investigative business reporting produced inside mainland China by a privately run newsroom with a record of testing official limits.

name: Topos
topics: Landscape Architecture / Urban Planning / Architecture

integrity_note: Published by the commercial trade house Georg Media and supported by industry advertising, so project coverage tends to be appreciative.
description: International review of landscape architecture and urban design, published quarterly in English from Munich by Georg Media. Read it for themed issues on public space, climate adaptation, water and planning practice, with project criticism from European and global offices.
what_makes_it_distinct: A quarterly devoted to landscape architecture as a discipline, with each issue built around one theme.

name: EU DisinfoLab

topics: Media and Information Integrity / Technology and AI / Politics and Policy / Investigations

description: EU DisinfoLab is a Brussels nonprofit founded in 2017 that researches disinformation campaigns and platform accountability in Europe. It publishes investigations, policy analysis, factsheets and a newsletter, and convenes researchers, journalists and regulators through webinars and an annual conference.
what_makes_it_distinct: Tracks how European rules on platforms and artificial intelligence are enforced, and documents influence operations with open source methods.

name: The Atlantic
owner: Emerson Collective (Laurene Powell Jobs), majority owner
format: Essays, reporting, criticism, print magazine, podcasts, newsletters
topics: Politics and Policy / Philosophy and Ideas / Technology and AI / Literature and Books

description: The Atlantic is an American magazine founded in Boston in 1857 and now based in Washington. It publishes daily reporting, essays and criticism online and a print magazine covering politics, foreign affairs, technology, science, culture and ideas.
what_makes_it_distinct: Well edited long essays on technology, artificial intelligence, democracy and culture, though the viewpoint stays close to the American liberal consensus.

name: The Breach
owner: The Breach (Breach Media); legal form Unconfirmed
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Climate and Environment / Investigations
modifier_reason: Left counterpart to The Hub; advocacy limits its evidentiary use

description: The Breach is an independent Canadian outlet launched in May 2021 that publishes investigations, analysis and video from a left perspective. It covers corporate power, climate, Indigenous rights, labour, militarism and foreign policy.
what_makes_it_distinct: It covers labour rights and corporate influence on Canadian policy from the left, the mirror image of The Hub.

name: The Gradient
topics: Technology and AI / Science / Philosophy and Ideas
integrity_note: Run by volunteer researchers with no owner or advertiser, but contributors often work in the AI industry or labs they discuss, and publication is now infrequent.
description: The Gradient is a volunteer run publication started in 2017 by researchers at the Stanford Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, offering essays, interviews and a podcast on machine learning research. Use its archive for clear technical overviews, and check how recently it has published before relying on it for news.
what_makes_it_distinct: Long explanatory essays on machine learning written by working researchers for a wider audience.

name: The Hub
owner: Unconfirmed (cofounded by Rudyard Griffiths and Sean Speer)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Credible right of centre Canadian voice balances the list
integrity_note: It discloses a free market viewpoint and sells subscriptions and advertising; its legal owner and any donor or foundation support are not confirmed.
description: The Hub is a Canadian online outlet founded in 2021 that covers politics and economics through news, commentary, podcasts and video. It states its viewpoint plainly, favouring free markets, economic competition and free speech.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is a declared right of centre voice on Canadian economic and public policy, useful for testing arguments the reader meets elsewhere.

name: The China Project (formerly SupChina)
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Technology and AI / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Closed in 2023; archive only
integrity_note: A privately financed New York company that closed in November 2023 when funding ran out, after accusations of bias from both American and Chinese sides.
description: The China Project, launched in New York in 2016 as SupChina by Anla Cheng and edited by Jeremy Goldkorn, published daily China news, explainers and the Sinica podcast until it closed in November 2023 for lack of funding. Use the archive for background on business, society and politics; Sinica continues independently under Kaiser Kuo.
what_makes_it_distinct: A closed outlet whose archive holds seven years of plain English explanation of Chinese society and business.

name: The Japan Times
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Partly wire copy; overlaps Nikkei Asia and NHK World
integrity_note: Owned since 2017 by the public relations firm News2u Holdings; a 2018 change in wording on wartime forced labour drew staff protests over perceived government alignment.
description: Japan's oldest English language daily, founded in 1897 and published in Tokyo, owned by News2u Holdings since 2017. Use it for accessible daily coverage of Japanese politics, society and culture, with staff reporting supplemented by wire copy, and as context for Japanese language reading.
what_makes_it_distinct: The longest running English language newspaper in Japan, with a deep archive of domestic coverage.

name: Apollo Magazine
topics: Visual Arts / History / Architecture
modifier_reason: Overlaps The Art Newspaper; collector oriented prestige
integrity_note: A commercial art magazine reliant on advertising from dealers, fairs and auction houses; it is reported to have been sold with The Spectator to Paul Marshall in 2024.
description: Apollo is a London art magazine founded in 1925, covering museums, exhibitions, art history, architecture, heritage and the art market in monthly issues and online. Read it for exhibition reviews, museum politics and collection histories, with a perspective closer to curators and collectors than to contemporary theory.
what_makes_it_distinct: A monthly founded a century ago that joins art historical scholarship with reporting on museums and collecting.

name: Atmos

format: Biannual print magazine, essays, photography, newsletters, podcast
topics: Climate and Environment / Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas

description: A climate and culture magazine founded in 2019 by Jake Sargent and Willow Defebaugh, publishing a biannual print volume and frequent online essays, photography and newsletters. Use it for visual storytelling about ecology, Indigenous knowledge, fashion and art, as a complement to policy and science reporting on climate.
what_makes_it_distinct: Treats the climate crisis as a cultural and aesthetic question through commissioned photography and art direction.

name: The Africa Report
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs

description: The Africa Report is an English language news site and magazine on African politics, business and finance published in Paris by Jeune Afrique Media Group. Use it for country coverage across the continent, especially West, North and Central Africa, alongside its French sister title Jeune Afrique.
what_makes_it_distinct: The English counterpart to Jeune Afrique, with strong sources in Francophone African capitals.

name: MacroPolo

description: MacroPolo is the in house think tank of the Paulson Institute in Chicago, known for data driven analysis of China's economy, technology sector and political elite, including its Global AI Talent Tracker. Treat it mainly as a reference archive, since new publication appears to have stopped after 2024.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its Global AI Talent Tracker and elite personnel databases remain widely cited data on China's technology workforce.

name: Planetizen
topics: Urban Planning / Politics and Policy

integrity_note: Owned by Urban Insight, a private Los Angeles web firm, and funded by course subscriptions, advertising and job listings; mostly summaries of reporting done by other outlets.
description: Planetizen is a planning news site that curates and summarizes stories on housing, transportation, land use and climate adaptation, with op eds and training for planners. Use it as a fast scan of planning debates, mainly in North America, then follow links to the original reporting.
what_makes_it_distinct: A daily digest written for working planners, linking each summary to its original source.

name: South China Morning Post
regions: Taiwan and Greater China / Southeast Asia
format: News, analysis, explainers, infographics, newsletters, podcasts
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Technology and AI
integrity_note: Owned by Alibaba Group since 2016, a company exposed to Beijing's regulators, and working under Hong Kong's national security law, which constrains sensitive political coverage.
description: The South China Morning Post is Hong Kong's English language daily, founded in 1903 and owned since 2016 by Alibaba Group, with a large newsroom covering mainland China, Hong Kong and Asia. Use it for detailed China policy, technology and economy reporting and its infographics, while watching for caution on sensitive politics.
what_makes_it_distinct: The largest English language newsroom reporting on China from inside Chinese jurisdiction, known for infographics and visual explainers.

name: Tokyo Art Beat

format: Exhibition listings, news, reviews, interviews, video, map

integrity_note: A commercial art site earning from advertising and paid membership, with museums and galleries as both subjects and advertisers; its operator is not confirmed.
description: Tokyo Art Beat is a bilingual Japanese and English art media site, online since 2004, that lists exhibitions across Japan and publishes news, reviews and interviews on the Japanese and international art scene. It is supported by advertising and a low cost paid membership that includes museum discount coupons.
what_makes_it_distinct: Parallel Japanese and English texts on exhibitions make it both a map based guide to Japan's art scene and steady reading practice in art vocabulary.

name: Atlas of Places
topics: Architecture / Landscape Architecture / Geography and Mapping / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Fills the cartography, landscape and architecture gap in one source
integrity_note: A noncommercial personal project linked to Thomas Paturet that discloses little about funding, authorship or image rights, and whose address now shows a publishing house.
description: Atlas of Places is an independent online collection that gathers architecture projects, cartography, satellite imagery, photography, painting and essays into carefully sequenced visual entries. Use it as a reference library for site studies and territorial drawing, where maps, buildings and landscapes are shown side by side.
what_makes_it_distinct: Places cartography, landscape and architecture in one visual archive, treating maps and satellite images as design material.

name: Nippon.com

description: Nippon.com is a multilingual website about Japan run by the Nippon Communications Foundation in Tokyo, publishing features, data notes and commentary on society, politics, economy and culture. Use the parallel Japanese, English, French and Chinese versions of one article for reading practice and for background on Japan.
what_makes_it_distinct: The same Japan features published in eight languages, including Traditional Chinese, French and the Japanese original.

name: Asterisk Magazine
topics: Technology and AI / Science / Economy and Finance / Philosophy and Ideas
integrity_note: Funded largely by effective altruism aligned philanthropy, it reflects the Bay Area rationalist milieu while publishing careful, quantified essays that state their uncertainty.
description: Asterisk is a quarterly online and print magazine launched in 2022 and edited by Clara Collier, supported by philanthropy aligned with effective altruism. Use it for long, quantitative essays on AI forecasting, biosecurity, global health, economic growth and science policy, read with its intellectual milieu in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: Quantitative, forecasting minded essays in which authors show their uncertainty and their numbers.

name: Gramophone
topics: Music and Performing Arts / History

integrity_note: Owned by the privately held Mark Allen Group and partly funded by advertising from the record labels whose releases it reviews.
description: Gramophone is a British monthly magazine on classical music founded in 1923 and published by Mark Allen Group, known for its recording reviews and annual awards. Use it to choose recordings and follow performers, with a searchable review archive reaching back a century for subscribers.
what_makes_it_distinct: A century of classical recording reviews in one searchable archive.

name: OhmyNews (오마이뉴스)
topics: Politics and Policy / Media and Information Integrity / Labour and Work
integrity_note: Founder controlled commercial site with a declared progressive line; staff edit submissions from citizen reporters, so the reliability of individual pieces varies.
description: OhmyNews is a South Korean online newspaper founded in 2000 by Oh Yeon-ho on the motto that every citizen is a reporter, combining staff journalists with thousands of citizen contributors. It publishes in Korean, so use it through translation for progressive and grassroots views of Korean politics.
what_makes_it_distinct: The pioneering citizen journalism newsroom, where staff editors check and publish reports from ordinary contributors.

name: Riddle Russia
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance / Conflict and Security

description: Riddle Russia is an online journal of analysis on Russian politics, economy, society, security and foreign policy, published in English and Russian. It commissions essays from international and Russian researchers and runs weekly political and economic summaries.
what_makes_it_distinct: Useful for expert reading of Russian regions, sanctions and official statistics, including pieces on how to treat Russian data with care.

name: Responsible Statecraft

integrity_note: The magazine of the Quincy Institute, a think tank funded by donors from left and right to argue for military restraint; it is advocacy with a declared line.
description: The online magazine of the Quincy Institute for Responsible Statecraft, a Washington think tank founded in 2019 that argues for military restraint and diplomacy. Use it as a deliberate counterweight to interventionist commentary on United States foreign policy, arms spending and lobbying, and read it as advocacy with a declared line.
what_makes_it_distinct: A transpartisan restraint school outlet joining left and conservative critics of United States military intervention.

name: The Gleaner (Jamaica Gleaner)

description: The Gleaner, founded in Kingston in 1834, is Jamaica's oldest daily newspaper and part of the publicly listed RJRGLEANER Communications Group. Use it for daily reporting on Jamaican politics, economy, hurricanes and diaspora affairs, and as one English language window on the wider Caribbean alongside Barbadian sources.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the oldest newspapers in the Caribbean, with an archive reaching back to 1834.

name: Dunia (두니아)

description: Dunia is a Korean language independent outlet, online at thedunia.org, that presents itself as investigating Asia and publishes reports, a newsletter and video. Treat it as a secondary source read through translation, useful for a Korean vantage on Asian affairs that the large English language outlets seldom provide.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Korean language newsroom devoted to investigating the rest of Asia, a vantage rarely available in other media.

name: Heatmap News

modifier_reason: Overlaps climate nonprofits already listed; United States focus

description: Heatmap News is a New York based climate and energy publication launched in 2023 by editors who came from The Week and The Atlantic, with Robinson Meyer as founding executive editor. Use it for daily reporting on clean energy deployment, climate technology, permitting fights and American climate policy.
what_makes_it_distinct: A newsroom built only around the energy transition, tracking project level fights over clean energy deployment.

name: The Nation (Barbados)

topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Hazards and Disaster Risk
modifier_reason: Underserved Barbados geography named in the brief

description: The Nation is the leading daily newspaper of Barbados, founded in 1973 and published in Bridgetown by the Nation Publishing Company, part of the regional group One Caribbean Media. Use its Nation News site for local politics, hurricane and climate resilience coverage, court reporting and community news from the island.
what_makes_it_distinct: The main daily newspaper of Barbados, giving island level reporting that no regional or international outlet provides.

name: War on the Rocks
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Owned by founder Ryan Evans through Metamorphic Media and financed by memberships and sponsorship; authors are mostly security insiders writing from a declared realist lens.
description: War on the Rocks is a Washington platform founded in 2013 by Ryan Evans, publishing analysis, commentary and podcasts on strategy, defence and foreign policy by practitioners and scholars. Use it to understand how military and policy professionals argue about conflicts that shape humanitarian operations.
what_makes_it_distinct: Defence and strategy debate written mainly by people with direct military, intelligence or policy experience.

name: Al-Monitor
format: News, analysis, newsletters, podcasts, paid briefings
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security / Energy
integrity_note: Founded and financed by businessman Jamal Daniel, who has commercial interests in the region; finances are not published, though reporting draws on many national viewpoints.
description: Al-Monitor is a news and analysis site founded in Washington in 2012 by the businessman Jamal Daniel, covering the Middle East through correspondents and columnists in the region. Use it for diplomacy, energy, Gulf business and Turkish, Iranian and Israeli politics, with deeper briefings kept behind its paid PRO tier.
what_makes_it_distinct: Policy focused Middle East coverage drawing on writers inside each country, including Iran, Turkey, Israel and the Gulf.

name: The Line

topics: Politics and Policy / Conflict and Security
modifier_reason: Opinion only; overlaps other Canadian commentary on the list

description: The Line is a Canadian commentary publication on Substack, founded in 2020 by journalists Matt Gurney and Jen Gerson. It publishes opinion essays, a weekly dispatch and podcasts on federal and provincial politics, defence, institutions and public affairs.
what_makes_it_distinct: It offers blunt Canadian commentary paid for by readers, outside the legacy opinion pages, though it adds argument rather than reporting.

name: Popula
owner: Popula (owned by its journalists; member of the Brick House Cooperative)
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Literature and Books / Media and Information Integrity / International Affairs
integrity_note: Owned by its journalists and funded by readers without advertising, with a declared left perspective; output has been sparse and current activity is unconfirmed.
description: Popula is a small magazine of news, essays and culture owned by its journalists, founded in 2018 by Maria Bustillos and later joined to the Brick House Cooperative. Read its archive for idiosyncratic international essays and media criticism, but check how recently it has published before relying on it.
what_makes_it_distinct: An experiment in journalist ownership and permanent archiving that began on a blockchain publishing platform.

name: AllAfrica
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
format: Aggregated news, topic and country pages, archive
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Development / Economy and Finance
integrity_note: A commercial aggregator that republishes African newsrooms alongside government and agency releases, so each item is only as reliable as its original publisher.
description: AllAfrica is an aggregator operated by AllAfrica Global Media that republishes several hundred reports a day from African news organizations, governments and agencies in English and French. Use it to scan coverage by country or topic, then judge each item by its original publisher.
what_makes_it_distinct: A single searchable feed of English and French reports from many national African newsrooms.

name: Assemblage
topics: Architecture / Philosophy and Ideas / History
integrity_note: A closed MIT Press journal, published from 1986 to 2000 and now a JSTOR archive; it represents one critical theory school of architectural thought.
description: Assemblage was a journal of architecture and design culture published by MIT Press from 1986 to 2000, edited by K. Michael Hays, and its 41 issues remain available through JSTOR. Use the archive for foundational debates in critical architectural theory, not for current coverage.
what_makes_it_distinct: The complete run of a journal that defined critical architecture theory in North America during the 1990s.

name: Thai PBS World

modifier_reason: Thai public service voice in English, limited by legal and political constraints
integrity_note: Thai public broadcaster funded by an earmarked alcohol and tobacco tax; politicians periodically seek to change that funding, and Thai law limits coverage of the monarchy.
description: Thai PBS World is the English language service of the Thai Public Broadcasting Service, the national public broadcaster created by statute in 2008. It covers Thai politics, society, the economy and regional affairs through news articles, video programmes and visual stories.
what_makes_it_distinct: Gives a Thai public service view of floods, air quality and national politics in English, with less commercial pressure than private Bangkok dailies.

name: American Affairs

topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Philosophy and Ideas / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Heterodox political economy largely absent from the mainstream press

description: American Affairs is a quarterly journal of public policy and political thought founded in 2017 and edited by Julius Krein. It publishes long essays on industrial policy, finance, technology, infrastructure, foreign policy and social criticism by writers from both the right and the left.
what_makes_it_distinct: Detailed essays on industrial policy, infrastructure costs and political economy from a heterodox position rarely found in mainstream outlets.

name: Montreal Gazette
topics: Politics and Policy / Law
modifier_reason: Useful local daily, but chain ownership adds no ownership diversity
integrity_note: Postmedia, whose largest shareholder and creditor is the American hedge fund Chatham Asset Management, owns it; the chain has cut newsrooms deeply and once ordered Conservative endorsements.
description: The Montreal Gazette is the city's English language daily, with roots going back to 1778, and is owned by Postmedia Network. It covers Montreal news, Quebec politics, crime and courts, culture and the Canadiens, with a prominent group of columnists.
what_makes_it_distinct: It is the daily record of anglophone Montreal and an English counterpoint to the French press on Quebec language politics.

name: NHK World-Japan Spanish
format: Short articles, radio bulletins, audio on demand
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Language Learning
modifier_reason: Language edition of a broadcaster already listed
integrity_note: NHK is funded by household receiving fees, but its governors are appointed with government involvement and the state may request topics for international broadcasts.
description: Spanish language service of NHK World-Japan, the international arm of Japan's public broadcaster. Use it for Japanese and Asian news in plain broadcast Spanish, with radio bulletins and short articles that double as language practice; content largely mirrors NHK's other language services.
what_makes_it_distinct: Japan's public broadcaster reporting on Japan in Spanish, joining two of the reader's study languages.

name: Works in Progress
format: Longform essays, newsletter, podcast, print edition
topics: Economy and Finance / Urban Planning / Science / Technology and AI
integrity_note: Wholly owned and funded by the payments company Stripe, and its editors argue a consistent pro growth, market liberal line.
description: Works in Progress is a magazine of ideas about economic growth, science, housing and technology, founded in 2020 and published by the payments company Stripe since 2022. Use it for well illustrated explanatory essays on urban form, construction and infrastructure, keeping in mind its pro growth, market liberal stance.
what_makes_it_distinct: Illustrated essays on how things came to work, from housing rules to vaccines, argued from a pro growth stance.

name: La Scena Musicale
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Visual Arts
modifier_reason: Useful bilingual concert calendar; much content is promotional
integrity_note: Published by a small charity that depends on advertising from the presenters and ensembles it covers, so much of its content is preview and promotion.
description: La Scena Musicale is a bilingual Montreal magazine on classical music, opera, jazz and the wider arts, founded in 1996. It publishes interviews, previews, reviews and an extensive concert calendar in French and English, in print and on its mySCENA website.
what_makes_it_distinct: Its bilingual concert calendar is a practical guide to the Montreal classical season, alongside interviews with performers.

name: e-flux
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas / Architecture
modifier_reason: Artist run publisher; adds curatorial and architecture theory
integrity_note: A privately run platform whose free journal is paid for by announcements bought by museums and galleries, the same art world institutions its writers discuss.
description: e-flux is a New York publishing platform founded by artist Anton Vidokle that combines paid institutional announcements with a free journal of art theory, criticism, architecture and film. Use the journal and its archive for essays on contemporary art and curatorial thinking, and skim the announcements for exhibitions.
what_makes_it_distinct: An artist run platform whose announcement service funds a free journal of theory.

name: The News Lens (關鍵評論網)

integrity_note: Part of TNL Mediagene, a listed digital media group financed by advertising and sponsored content, with much material contributed or syndicated.
description: The News Lens is a Taipei digital outlet founded in 2013 by Joey Chung and Mario Yang, now part of the listed group TNL Mediagene. Read it in Traditional Chinese for explainers, commentary and columns on Taiwan and the region, checking sources because much content is syndicated or contributed.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Taiwanese digital native outlet mixing newsroom explainers with a wide pool of outside columnists in Traditional Chinese.

name: Jeune Afrique
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs

what_makes_it_distinct: The longest running Francophone news magazine on Africa, with unusual access to presidents and business elites.

name: Unseen Japan

topics: Politics and Policy / History / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Useful context but mostly secondary reporting
integrity_note: A small reader funded site run by its founder; articles synthesise Japanese media more than they report first hand, and it also sells memberships and tours.
description: Unseen Japan is an independent English site founded in 2018 that explains Japanese news, history, language and social change, drawing mainly on Japanese language media. It gives regular space to women, LGBT people, Indigenous peoples, Zainichi Koreans and other communities that English coverage tends to overlook.
what_makes_it_distinct: A readable bridge into Japanese domestic debates and minority issues, built on local media that the reader can follow up in the original Japanese.

name: The Drift
owner: Unconfirmed (independent, founded by Kiara Barrow and Rebecca Panovka)
format: Essays, criticism, fiction, poetry, short reviews
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy

what_makes_it_distinct: Shows how a younger generation of American critics on the left argues about culture, media and politics, with careful editing.

name: The Marginalian
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / Science / Visual Arts
integrity_note: Written and owned by one person, Maria Popova, and paid for by reader donations and book affiliate links; it is personal reflection, not reporting.
description: The Marginalian is the solo publication of the writer Maria Popova, begun in 2006 as Brain Pickings and renamed in 2021, funded by reader donations and free of advertising. Use it for reflective essays that draw passages from literature, philosophy, science and art, as slow reading and not as news.
what_makes_it_distinct: One author's two decade archive of annotated reading across literature, science and philosophy, free and without advertising.

name: Jacobin
format: Quarterly print magazine, daily web essays, podcasts, video
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Economy and Finance / Philosophy and Ideas
integrity_note: Published by the nonprofit Jacobin Foundation and funded mainly by subscribers, it argues openly for democratic socialism, so read it as committed advocacy, not neutral reporting.
description: Jacobin is a socialist magazine founded in 2010 by Bhaskar Sunkara and published in New York by the nonprofit Jacobin Foundation, with a quarterly print edition and daily web commentary. Use it for labour movement coverage, union campaigns and left political economy, reading it as argument from a declared position.
what_makes_it_distinct: The most widely read English language socialist magazine, with steady coverage of strikes and union organizing.

name: Bachtrack
format: Concert, opera and dance reviews, event listings, interviews
topics: Music and Performing Arts / Data and Statistics
integrity_note: Privately owned by its founders and financed by paid listings and advertising from the venues and ensembles it reviews, a commercial tie readers should keep in mind.
description: Bachtrack is a classical music site founded in London in 2008 by David and Alison Karlin, combining a worldwide database of concert, opera and dance listings with reviews by a large network of critics. Use it to find performances in Montreal and abroad and to read reviews in English, French, German and Spanish.
what_makes_it_distinct: The largest searchable listing of live classical music, opera and dance worldwide, with reviews in four languages.

name: Montreal Economic Institute (IEDM)
format: Economic notes, research papers, opinion pieces
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Health / Energy
modifier_reason: Right of centre counterweight to IRIS in Quebec policy debate
integrity_note: Funded by donations from foundations, businesses and individuals whose names it does not publish; it says it takes no government money and argues consistently for market solutions.
description: The Montreal Economic Institute, known in French as IEDM, is a think tank based in Montreal that promotes market based public policy. It publishes short economic notes, research papers and opinion pieces on health care, taxation, energy, housing and regulation, in French and English.
what_makes_it_distinct: It makes the market liberal case on Quebec health, energy and housing policy in both languages, a counterweight to IRIS.

name: Esprit critique
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Science
modifier_reason: Probable duplicate of Esprit; current activity unclear
integrity_note: An online sociology journal run by an editorial association of academics with no commercial publisher; its funding and current activity could not be established.
description: Esprit critique is a French language online journal of sociology and social sciences, founded in 1999 by the Quebec sociologist Jean-François Marcotte and published in thematic issues with free access. It is distinct from the Paris review Esprit, and its recent publishing activity could not be confirmed.
what_makes_it_distinct: An early open access Francophone sociology journal, born online in Quebec in 1999.

name: New Scientist
format: Weekly magazine, news, features, podcasts, newsletters
topics: Science / Technology and AI / Health / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Overlaps Science, Nature news and Quanta; commercial owner
integrity_note: Owned since 2021 by Daily Mail and General Trust, the Rothermere family company, with editorial run separately from the group's newspapers.
description: New Scientist is a British weekly science magazine founded in 1956 and owned since 2021 by Daily Mail and General Trust. Use it for quick, readable news on research, technology, health and environment, then follow its references to the journals for anything that matters to your work.
what_makes_it_distinct: A weekly digest of research news across all sciences, written for general readers rather than specialists.

name: Persuasion
owner: Persuasion (founded and led by Yascha Mounk)
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Heterodox liberal essays, but similar ground to other ideas magazines
integrity_note: Founder led Substack publication supported by subscribers; its legal structure and any donor funding are not stated on the page reviewed.
description: Persuasion is an online magazine and Substack community founded in 2020 by the political scientist Yascha Mounk. It publishes essays and podcasts defending liberal democracy and free expression against illiberal currents on both the right and the left.
what_makes_it_distinct: Short, argued essays in political philosophy from a heterodox liberal position, often by writers from outside the United States.

name: Jihadica
regions: Middle East and North Africa / Global
owner: Jihadica (founded by William McCants, edited by Cole Bunzel)
format: Expert blog posts, primary source analysis
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs
modifier_reason: Academic expertise, reduced because posting appears close to dormant
