description: Jihadica is an academic blog founded in 2008 by William McCants and later edited by Cole Bunzel, in which specialists who read Arabic analyse the texts, debates and internal disputes of jihadi movements. Use its archive for primary source context on ideology, since posting has been infrequent in recent years.
what_makes_it_distinct: Scholars reading jihadi ideological texts in the original Arabic and explaining the internal arguments to outsiders.

name: Nautilus
topics: Science / Philosophy and Ideas / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Overlaps other science and ideas magazines already listed
integrity_note: Owned by NautilusNext, a private investor group formed after the magazine fell behind on freelancer payments; it relies on memberships, advertising and sponsored partnerships with institutions.
description: Nautilus is an American science magazine launched in 2013 that publishes long essays and reported features linking physics, biology, neuroscience and philosophy. Read it for carefully written explanatory pieces by scientists and writers, with a metered paywall and a print edition for members.
what_makes_it_distinct: Science writing organized around ideas and narrative, with commissioned illustration for each piece.

name: Sentient Media
topics: Climate and Environment / Health / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: A donor funded nonprofit that grew out of animal protection advocacy; it publishes its funding and corrections policy, but its single subject frames every story.
description: Sentient is a nonprofit news organization, formerly styled Sentient Media, that reports on factory farming, food systems and their links to climate, public health and animal welfare. Treat it as a specialist source on agriculture and climate policy, noting that it grew out of animal protection advocacy.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of very few newsrooms devoted entirely to animal agriculture and its climate footprint.

name: Korea JoongAng Daily
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Technology and AI
integrity_note: The English daily of JoongAng Group, a family controlled media conglomerate with historic ties to Samsung; its editorial line is conservative and friendly to business.
description: Korea JoongAng Daily is the English language newspaper of the JoongAng Group in Seoul, founded in 2000 and distributed in Korea together with the international edition of The New York Times. Use it for South Korean politics, industry, semiconductors and culture, balanced against the centre left Hankyoreh English edition.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Korean media conglomerate's English daily, distributed together with The New York Times international edition.

name: SSRN
topics: Economy and Finance / Law / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Owned by Elsevier, part of the commercial group RELX; papers are screened but not peer reviewed, and the owner has a commercial interest in the research workflow.
description: SSRN is a repository of preprints and working papers owned by Elsevier, strongest in law, economics, finance, political science and management. Use it to find research before journal publication, remembering that papers there have not been peer reviewed.
what_makes_it_distinct: The main preprint repository for law and economics working papers.

name: Artforum
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Prestige title under a corporate owner; heavy advertising
integrity_note: Owned by Penske Media, which dismissed editor David Velasco in 2023 after a Gaza open letter; gallery advertising is the main income and shapes what gets attention.
description: Artforum is a New York contemporary art magazine founded in 1962 and owned since 2022 by Penske Media Corporation, publishing criticism, exhibition reviews, essays and art world news. Use it to follow international exhibitions and critical debates, aware that advertising galleries and a corporate owner shape its field of attention.
what_makes_it_distinct: The reference record of exhibition reviews for the commercial and institutional contemporary art world since 1962.

name: International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS)
regions: Global / Europe / Southeast Asia / Middle East and North Africa
format: Reports, annual data volumes, journal, online analysis, podcasts
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Data and Statistics
integrity_note: Relies on government and defence industry funding, including host states of its security dialogues; undisclosed Bahraini funding reported in 2016 raised questions about its independence.
description: The International Institute for Strategic Studies is a London based research institute founded in 1958 that publishes The Military Balance, the journal Survival and regular strategic assessments. Use it for reference data on armed forces and defence spending, and for analysis around its Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore.
what_makes_it_distinct: The Military Balance, an annual open source inventory of armed forces and defence budgets worldwide.

name: Contretemps
owner: Contretemps editorial collective (print edition with Éditions Syllepse)
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Politics and Policy / Labour and Work
integrity_note: A volunteer collective from the French revolutionary left that states its aim as arming the radical left, so read it as committed argument.
description: Contretemps is a French review of critical theory and politics founded in 2001 around the philosopher Daniel Bensaïd, now run mainly as a free web review by a volunteer editorial collective. Read it for Marxist, feminist, ecological and decolonial essays and translations, knowing its openly partisan line.
what_makes_it_distinct: A free French language review of Marxist theory that translates international left debates into French.

name: Mousse Magazine
format: Print magazine, essays, interviews, exhibition coverage, books
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Curatorial depth from an independent Italian publisher
integrity_note: A privately owned magazine and publishing house whose income comes from galleries and institutions that it also covers.
description: Mousse is a Milan based contemporary art magazine and publishing house founded in 2006, printing its issues in English and posting exhibition documentation online most days. Use it for extended conversations with artists and curators and for a running survey of exhibitions across Europe and beyond.
what_makes_it_distinct: Extended artist and curator conversations alongside a daily visual record of exhibitions worldwide.

name: The Revelator
topics: Climate and Environment / Science / Politics and Policy
integrity_note: Funded entirely by the Center for Biological Diversity, a conservation advocacy group, with a published statement that the Center does not influence its reporting.
description: The Revelator is an environmental news and commentary site published by the Center for Biological Diversity, an American conservation group, and edited by John R. Platt. Read it for reporting and essays on endangered species, biodiversity loss, public lands and climate, keeping its parent organisation's advocacy role in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: An editorially separate news site funded by a conservation advocacy group, centred on wildlife and extinction.

name: The Baffler
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Labour and Work / Literature and Books
modifier_reason: Small nonprofit; labour and technology criticism against prevailing hype
integrity_note: Owned by the nonprofit Baffler Foundation and supported by subscribers and donors; it describes itself as left wing criticism and makes no claim to balance.
description: The Baffler is a magazine of political and cultural criticism founded in 1988 by Thomas Frank and Keith White, now published in New York by the nonprofit Baffler Foundation. Use it for skeptical essays on business culture, technology hype, labour and media, plus fiction and poetry.
what_makes_it_distinct: Satirical, combative criticism of business and technology boosterism from a small nonprofit magazine.

name: Frieze
owner: Company led by Ari Emanuel (bought from Endeavor in 2025)
topics: Visual Arts / Philosophy and Ideas
modifier_reason: Prestige title tied to fair business; overlaps other art outlets
integrity_note: Shares an owner with the Frieze art fairs, whose exhibitors are the galleries the magazine reviews and sells advertising to; this is a structural conflict of interest.
description: Frieze is a London contemporary art magazine founded in 1991, published alongside the Frieze art fairs and sold in 2025 by Endeavor to a company led by Ari Emanuel. Use it for exhibition reviews and essays on artists and curating, bearing in mind its commercial ties to the fair business.
what_makes_it_distinct: A critical magazine that shares a brand and owner with major commercial art fairs.

name: Monthly Review
format: Magazine, essays, book press, companion website
topics: Economy and Finance / Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Independent socialist foundation; a declared tradition absent elsewhere in the list
integrity_note: Owned by the independent Monthly Review Foundation and reader supported; a committed Marxist voice whose anti imperialist framing is often uncritical of states opposed to Washington.
description: Monthly Review is an independent socialist magazine founded in New York in 1949 by Paul Sweezy and Leo Huberman, published by the Monthly Review Foundation and edited by John Bellamy Foster. Use it for Marxist analysis of capitalism, imperialism, labour and ecology, read as a declared position.
what_makes_it_distinct: The longest continuously published socialist magazine in the United States and a home of ecological Marxism.

name: Revue des Deux Mondes
topics: Literature and Books / Philosophy and Ideas / History / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Heritage title adding prestige more than new perspective
integrity_note: Owned by Fimalac, the holding of Marc Ladreit de Lacharrière, who was convicted in 2018 over a fictitious job the review gave Penelope Fillon.
description: Revue des Deux Mondes is a French monthly review of literature, history and politics founded in 1829, now owned by Fimalac, the holding company of Marc Ladreit de Lacharrière. Use it for essays and interviews from the conservative and liberal side of French intellectual debate.
what_makes_it_distinct: One of the oldest reviews still published in Europe, with an archive reaching back to 1829.

name: Barbados Today
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Direct coverage of Barbados, a named priority geography
integrity_note: Privately owned digital daily financed by advertising; ownership and editorial standards are not clearly published, and coverage follows a mainstream line on Barbadian politics.
description: Barbados Today is a digital daily newspaper published in Barbados that covers national politics, courts, business, education and regional Caribbean affairs. Use it for local detail on government policy, climate resilience and the economy that international outlets rarely carry.
what_makes_it_distinct: A digital daily giving continuous local coverage of Barbados.

name: Landezine
topics: Landscape Architecture / Urban Planning / Architecture
modifier_reason: Fills the landscape architecture practice gap
integrity_note: An independent Slovenian platform whose project texts and images are supplied by the design offices shown, and which earns from sponsors and office profiles; a showcase, not criticism.
description: Landezine is an online platform presenting built landscape architecture projects from around the world with drawings, plans and photographs, and runs the Landezine International Landscape Award. Use it as a visual reference library of contemporary landscape design and its site strategies.
what_makes_it_distinct: Shows landscape projects through plans and sections, not only photographs, which makes site strategies legible.

name: TaiwanPlus
owner: Taiwan Public Television Service Foundation (funded by the Ministry of Culture)
format: Video news, streaming channel, documentaries, articles
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs
integrity_note: Funded by Taiwan's Ministry of Culture and run by the Public Television Service; its stated mission is to give Taiwan an international voice.
description: Taiwan's publicly funded English language video news platform, launched in 2021 with Ministry of Culture funding and operated by the Public Television Service. Use it for accessible daily video on Taiwanese politics, society and cross strait affairs, and read it as a view from Taiwan's public sector alongside independent outlets.
what_makes_it_distinct: An English language television news service produced in Taiwan for an international audience with public funding.

name: CNA (Channel NewsAsia)
format: Articles, television, video documentaries, podcasts, newsletters
topics: International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Southeast Asian vantage and bureaus; state linked ownership noted
integrity_note: Owned by Mediacorp, which belongs to Singapore's state investor Temasek, so reporting on Singapore's own politics stays within establishment limits.
description: A Singapore news network owned by Mediacorp, which belongs to the state investment company Temasek, with bureaus across Southeast and East Asia. Use it for regional business, politics and its CNA Insider documentaries, while noting that coverage of Singapore's own politics stays within establishment limits.
what_makes_it_distinct: A broad English language correspondent network based in Southeast Asia, with strong documentary output.

name: Middle East Eye
topics: Conflict and Security / International Affairs / Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
integrity_note: Published by M.E.E. Limited, which does not disclose its funders and denies reported Qatari links; reporting is original but framing is consistently partisan.
description: Middle East Eye is a news site launched in London in 2014 and edited by David Hearst, published by M.E.E. Limited, which does not disclose its funders and denies claims of Qatari backing. Use it for reporting from Palestine, Egypt, Turkey and the Maghreb in English and French, keeping that opacity in mind.
what_makes_it_distinct: Heavy original reporting from Gaza, Egypt and the Maghreb in English and French, paired with undisclosed funding.

name: Le Journal des Alternatives
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice / Development / Migration
modifier_reason: Montreal civil society voice with Global South partners
integrity_note: Published by the Montreal solidarity organisation Alternatives, so it speaks for social movements and should be read as advocacy, not as neutral reporting.
description: Le Journal des Alternatives is a French language platform published by Alternatives, a Montreal international solidarity organization, carrying analysis from social movements in Quebec and the Global South. Use it for activist perspectives on trade, climate justice, migration and international cooperation, read as advocacy.
what_makes_it_distinct: A Montreal altermondialiste platform linking Quebec social movements with partners across the Global South.

name: PanSci (泛科學)
format: Explainers, video, podcasts, partner articles, sponsored features, courses
topics: Science / Health / Technology and AI
modifier_reason: Sponsored and syndicated content dilutes the signal
integrity_note: A commercial outlet whose stated business model includes sponsored projects for companies; promotional pieces are labelled but sit beside editorial science articles.
description: PanSci is a Taiwanese popular science site and community founded in 2011 and run by PanMedia. It mixes its own explainers and videos with pieces from partner publishers, research bodies and contributing authors, and earns income from sponsored projects, video production, events, online courses and commerce.
what_makes_it_distinct: Accessible Traditional Chinese science reading, though a large share of current items are syndicated health pieces or labelled sponsor content.

name: Africanews
regions: Sub-Saharan Africa / Middle East and North Africa
owner: Euronews SA (majority owned by Alpac Capital)
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Economy and Finance
integrity_note: A subsidiary of Euronews, whose majority owner Alpac Capital has faced press reports of Hungarian state linked financing; most copy comes from agencies.
description: Africanews is a pan African news channel and website launched in 2016 as the sister service of Euronews, publishing parallel English and French editions. Use it as a quick continental baseline, noting that much of its report draws on agency copy and that deeper regional outlets should follow.
what_makes_it_distinct: A continent wide news service with matching English and French editions under the Euronews group.

name: Rice Media
topics: Labour and Work / Migration / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Independent Singapore voice outside state linked media
integrity_note: A privately owned commercial publisher that depends on sponsored content from banks and brands, labelled as such, alongside its social reporting.
description: Rice Media is an independent Singapore digital publication founded in 2016 that publishes long features, commentary and short documentaries on social issues, class, migrant workers and culture. Use it for ground level Singaporean voices outside the state linked press, noting its uneven depth and reliance on sponsored content.
what_makes_it_distinct: Young Singaporean writers covering social life and inequality in a voice the mainstream local press seldom uses.

name: Ludwig van Montréal
format: Concert reviews, news, weekly picks, interviews
topics: Music and Performing Arts / History
modifier_reason: Commercial ownership; overlaps with La Scena Musicale
integrity_note: Hosted by The New Classical FM, a ZoomerMedia radio brand, and funded by advertising, so its criticism sits inside the marketing environment of a commercial broadcaster.
description: Ludwig van Montréal is the French language edition of Ludwig Van, a classical music news site now hosted on the website of The New Classical FM. It publishes concert, opera and ballet reviews, news and weekly editors' picks for the Montreal season.
what_makes_it_distinct: It publishes prompt French language reviews of Montreal concerts, opera and ballet, each labelled as critique, news or editor's choice.

name: The Strad
topics: Music and Performing Arts / History
integrity_note: A commercial trade magazine that depends on advertising from instrument dealers, makers and schools, the same market its features and reviews cover.
description: The Strad is a London monthly magazine for string players, teachers and instrument makers, published since 1890 and now part of Newsquest Specialist Media. Use it for interviews, technique articles, concert reviews and detailed studies of violin making, a narrow field it covers in depth.
what_makes_it_distinct: The long standing magazine of bowed string instruments, including technical posters documenting historic violins.

name: Dezeen
format: News, project features, video, newsletters, awards
topics: Architecture / Urban Planning
modifier_reason: High volume commercial feed overlapping other architecture titles
integrity_note: Owned by Denmark's JP/Politiken Media Group; revenue comes from advertising, awards, events and paid brand promotions, so coverage favours showcasing projects over criticism.
description: Dezeen is a London based online magazine of architecture, interiors and design founded in 2006 by Marcus Fairs and owned since 2021 by the Danish group JP/Politiken Media. Skim its daily feed to track new buildings and industry debates, and turn to slower journals for criticism.
what_makes_it_distinct: A very high volume daily feed of new architecture and design projects from around the world.

name: The Straits Times
topics: Politics and Policy / Economy and Finance / International Affairs
integrity_note: Published by SPH Media Trust, which receives large Singapore government grants and operates under press laws that give the state influence over management.
description: The Straits Times is Singapore's main English language daily, founded in 1845 and published by SPH Media Trust, a nonprofit entity that receives government funding. Use it for Singapore policy, business and Southeast Asian news from its regional bureaus, while reading its domestic political coverage with caution.
what_makes_it_distinct: Singapore's paper of record, with correspondents across Southeast and East Asian capitals.

name: IAI News (Institute of Art and Ideas)
owner: The Institute of Art and Ideas
format: Essays, filmed debates, talks, festival recordings
topics: Philosophy and Ideas / Science / Politics and Policy
modifier_reason: Overlaps stronger philosophy essay platforms already listed
integrity_note: Run by the Institute of Art and Ideas, founded by philosopher Hilary Lawson; funding details are not published, and debates are framed to provoke.
description: IAI News is the online magazine of the Institute of Art and Ideas, the British organization founded by philosopher Hilary Lawson that also runs the HowTheLightGetsIn festival. It pairs short essays with filmed debates among philosophers and scientists, useful for sampling disputes but often framed provocatively.
what_makes_it_distinct: Filmed debates that put philosophers and scientists who disagree on the same stage.

name: gal-dem
topics: Politics and Policy / Human Rights and Justice
modifier_reason: Closed in 2023; archive only
integrity_note: A founder led company that relied on brand partnerships and memberships, closed in March 2023, and now stands only as an archive.
description: gal-dem was a London magazine founded in 2015 by Liv Little and written by women and non binary people of colour, which stopped publishing in March 2023. Its website stayed online as an archive of essays on culture, identity and British politics, useful for research but no longer current.
what_makes_it_distinct: Eight years of British culture and politics written entirely by women and non binary people of colour.

name: News in Slow Spanish
regions: Europe / Latin America and Brazil / Global
topics: Language Learning / International Affairs
integrity_note: A private language learning company funded by subscribers; it rewrites the week's news for learners and discloses that some content is generated with artificial intelligence.
description: Weekly subscription programme from Linguistica 360 that discusses the week's news in slowed, clearly spoken Spanish, with transcripts, grammar notes and separate Spain and Latin America editions. Use it for listening practice at intermediate level; it summarizes news and does not report it.
what_makes_it_distinct: Current affairs delivered at learner pace in Spanish, with full transcripts for intermediate listeners.

name: Pambazuka News
topics: Human Rights and Justice / Politics and Policy / Development / International Affairs
integrity_note: Founded by the social justice organisation Fahamu and written by activists and scholars, so it is movement commentary, not neutral reporting.
description: Pambazuka News is a Pan African platform for commentary and analysis on social justice, founded in 2000 by the organization Fahamu. Use its archive for activist and scholarly writing on human rights, land, gender and governance across Africa, and check whether new issues are still appearing.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running archive of African activist and movement writing.

name: ArcGIS StoryMaps (Esri)
topics: Geography and Mapping / Technology and AI / Climate and Environment
modifier_reason: Fills a cartographic practice gap, though it is a vendor platform
integrity_note: A product of the software company Esri; stories are written by its users with no editorial review, so each one is only as reliable as its author.
description: ArcGIS StoryMaps is Esri's web tool and public gallery for narratives built from interactive maps, published by governments, universities, humanitarian agencies and newsrooms. Browse it for working examples of map based storytelling and method, remembering that it is a vendor platform with no editorial review of user stories.
what_makes_it_distinct: A very large public gallery of map led narratives, built on the same ArcGIS stack the reader uses at work.

name: Taipei Times
topics: Politics and Policy / International Affairs / Language Learning
integrity_note: Owned by the Liberty Times Group of the Lin family; editorials consistently back Taiwanese sovereignty and the pan green camp, and much news copy comes from wires.
description: Taipei Times is an English language daily founded in 1999 and owned by the Liberty Times Group, with an editorial line sympathetic to Taiwanese sovereignty. Use it for domestic politics, cross strait news and translated commentary, and its bilingual pages for parallel English and Chinese reading.
what_makes_it_distinct: Carries English translations of Liberty Times editorials and bilingual study pages alongside its own Taiwan reporting.

name: The Scientist
topics: Science / Health
modifier_reason: Off theme; life science news is covered by stronger outlets
integrity_note: A trade magazine owned by LabX Media Group and financed largely by advertising and sponsored content from laboratory suppliers, the same industry its readers buy from.
description: The Scientist is a magazine for life science researchers published by LabX Media Group, covering biology, biomedicine, laboratory methods and research careers. Use it occasionally for readable accounts of new findings in the life sciences, which sit outside the core themes of this directory.
what_makes_it_distinct: Written for working life scientists, with attention to laboratory methods and careers.

name: Energy Monitor
topics: Energy / Climate and Environment / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Overlaps the climate outlets already listed; status unknown
integrity_note: Owned by the data company GlobalData, which sells marketing services across its business sites, so the line between journalism and commercial content needs watching.
description: Energy transition news and analysis site launched in 2020 within New Statesman Media Group and now part of GlobalData. It covers power markets, policy and decarbonization data, and was publishing new articles when checked on 1 October 2026.
what_makes_it_distinct: Energy transition coverage built on a commercial data provider's market figures.

name: Tribune
owner: Owner of Islam Channel (acquired 2025, per Press Gazette)
topics: Politics and Policy / Labour and Work / Economy and Finance
integrity_note: A committed voice of the Labour left, reported by Press Gazette to have been bought in 2025 by the owner of Islam Channel; ownership terms are not public.
description: British socialist magazine founded in 1937, relaunched in 2018 under Jacobin's publisher and acquired in 2025 by the owner of Islam Channel. Read it for arguments from the Labour left on unions, housing, public ownership and political economy, as one committed voice among others.
what_makes_it_distinct: The historic magazine of the British Labour left, once edited by Aneurin Bevan and Michael Foot.

name: Resilience.org
topics: Climate and Environment / Energy / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Largely an aggregator with a single advocacy line
integrity_note: A programme of the Post Carbon Institute, an advocacy nonprofit; it republishes writing selected to support a post growth worldview and does little original reporting.
description: Resilience.org is a website run by the nonprofit Post Carbon Institute that republishes and commissions articles on energy descent, local economies, food systems and community responses to climate change. Skim it occasionally for perspectives on degrowth and adaptation, checking original sources because much of it is aggregated.
what_makes_it_distinct: A long running digest of post growth and community resilience writing from many small publishers.

name: Geopolitical Monitor
topics: International Affairs / Conflict and Security / Economy and Finance
modifier_reason: Overlaps stronger analysis outlets; thin published standards
